text: A focus SHOULD support the conference package RFC 4575 [9], behave as a notifier for that package, and indicate its support in the Allow- Events header fields in requests and responses.
notes: SUBSCRIBE Event: conference to the conference URI gets 200 and a NOTIFY; Allow-Events on focus INVITE/200 lists conference

text: A focus MAY include information about the conference in Session Description Protocol (SDP) bodies sent as part of normal SIP signaling by populating the Session Information, URI, Email Address, and Phone Number SDP fields.
notes: optional: if configured, SDP from the focus carries i=/u=/e=/p= lines describing the conference

text: In order to support advanced features, where a session established between two endpoints can migrate to a centralized conference, a focus SHOULD support the Replaces header field [6].
notes: INVITE with Replaces naming a focus leg is accepted; Supported lists replaces

text: As a result, note that the Conference Factory URI and the newly created focus URI MAY resolve to different physical devices.
notes: INVITE to the factory URI gets 200 with a Contact conference URI distinct from the factory URI; later requests to it reach the focus

text: ...typically a conferencing system needs to allocate a SIP conference URI such that SIP requests to this URI are not forked and are routed to a dedicated conference focus.
notes: network routing duty: the deployment must not fork requests to the conference URI

text: In session establishment, a focus MUST include the 'isfocus' feature parameter in the Contact header field unless the focus wishes to hide the fact that it is a focus.
notes: every INVITE/2xx the focus sends on a conference leg has Contact with ;isfocus unless hiding is configured

text: A focus MUST include the 'isfocus' feature parameter in a 200 OK response to an OPTIONS unless the focus wishes to hide the fact that it is a focus.
notes: OPTIONS to the conference URI (in and out of dialog) returns 200 with Contact ;isfocus

text: The focus MUST include the 'isfocus' feature parameter in the Contact header field of the 200 OK response to the INVITE.
notes: dial-in INVITE to the conference URI gets 200 whose Contact carries ;isfocus

text: To directly add a participant to a conference, a focus SHOULD send an INVITE to the participant containing a Contact header field with the conference URI and the 'isfocus' feature parameter.
notes: dial-out INVITE from the focus has Contact = conference URI with ;isfocus

text: As discussed in the conferencing framework, the conference URI must be unique across all distinct conferences within the same domain.
notes: n/a, application duty: chappe_sip_focus:new/1 takes the conference URI the app allocates; chappe keeps no conference registry

text: The Contact header field MUST contain the 'isfocus' feature parameter to indicate that this URI is for a conference.
notes: 200 to an INVITE sent to the factory URI has Contact = new conference URI with ;isfocus

text: Upon receipt of the REFER containing a Refer-To header with a SIP URI, the focus SHOULD send an INVITE to the new participant identified by the Refer-To SIP URI containing a Contact header field with the conference URI and the 'isfocus' feature parameter.
notes: REFER to the conference URI with Refer-To sip:carol yields an INVITE to carol with Contact conference URI;isfocus

text: A UA wishing to add a new participant SHOULD send a REFER request to the participant with a Refer-To header containing the conference URI.
notes: participant side; the focus only has to accept the resulting dial-in INVITE (see R4579-08)

text: A participant may request that the focus refer a participant into the conference by sending a REFER method. The Refer-To header field will have the method set to REFER and an escaped Refer-To header field containing the conference URI.
notes: REFER with Refer-To <uri;method=REFER?Refer-To=conf URI> makes the focus send a REFER to that participant

text: A UA can request to be added to a conference by sending a request to the focus containing a Join [7] header field containing a dialog ID of one leg of the conference (a dialog between another participant and the focus).
notes: INVITE with Join naming an existing focus leg adds the caller to that conference

text: Alice's user agent #2 is added into the conference by the focus. The focus sends a BYE to user agent #1.
notes: INVITE with Replaces naming a focus leg: new leg joins the same conference, focus sends BYE on the replaced leg

text: Alice then sends a REFER request to the focus to send an INVITE request to the other participant. Alice includes an escaped Replaces header field in the URI included in the Refer-To header field.
notes: REFER with Refer-To bob?Replaces=A-B yields a focus INVITE to bob carrying Replaces: A-B

text: ...a properly authorized SIP UA (typically the conference owner) can send a REFER to the conference URI with a Refer-To containing the URI of the participant and with the method set to BYE.
notes: authorized REFER Refer-To carol;method=BYE makes the focus send BYE on carol's leg; unauthorized one is rejected

text: The default conference policy for conferences created using the Conference Factory URI is that the conference is deleted when the creator departs.
notes: with delete-on-creator-exit policy, creator BYE ends the conference: other legs get BYE, subscriptions get terminated NOTIFY

text: Note that the Allow, Accept, Allow-Events, and Supported header fields should be present in an INVITE from a focus or a 200 OK answer from the focus to an INVITE as a part of a normal dialog establishment process.
notes: focus INVITE and 200 carry Allow, Accept, Allow-Events (conference, refer) and Supported (replaces)

text: A focus SHOULD authenticate participants before joining them to a conference and allowing utilization of conferencing resources.
notes: with authentication configured, dial-in INVITE without credentials is challenged (401/407) before it is joined

text: In addition, a focus SHOULD support Secure SIP connections so that hop-by-hop mutual authentication and confidentiality provided by TLS can be achieved.
notes: focus accepts and originates SIP over TLS (sips:) with certificate verification

text: A participant and focus SHOULD support an end-to-end integrity mechanism such as S/MIME.
notes: S/MIME not implemented; TLS hop-by-hop is the documented substitute

text: A focus MUST support a participant's request for privacy, either through conference policy or as expressed through the signaling.
notes: participant with Privacy: id (or anonymous policy) is not identified to others in conference-info or signaling

text: For example, a participant joining a conference and including a Privacy header field [10] must not have identity information revealed to other participants by the focus.
notes: INVITE with Privacy: id: conference-info entity for that user is anonymous and no From/PAI identity leaks to other legs

text: If other signaling protocols are used, privacy signaled through them also must be respected.
notes: privacy flag set through the API is honoured in conference-info and dial-out identity

text: A focus accepting subscriptions to the conference package must follow the security considerations in RFC 4575 [9].
notes: n/a: umbrella over R4575-52..59, not a testable statement of its own; covered by R4575-53, -54, -56, -57, -58

text: Since notifications can carry sensitive information, the subscriptions should be authenticated and the notifications delivered with confidentiality and integrity protection.
notes: with auth configured, conference SUBSCRIBE without credentials is challenged; NOTIFY goes over TLS when the subscriber used sips

text: This conference URI should be registered by the newly created focus to become routable as a conference URI within the conf.example.com domain.
notes: conference URI allocated by the factory is routable (GRUU or registered) for later dial-in and SUBSCRIBE

text: The name of this event package is "conference". This package name is carried in the Event and Allow-Events header...
notes: SUBSCRIBE Event: conference to the conference URI gets 2xx; Allow-Events on focus requests and responses lists conference

text: Notifications are generated every time there is any change in the state of the conference.
notes: any roster or state change triggers a NOTIFY to each active subscriber (subject to rate limit)

text: The exception is a NOTIFY sent in response to a SUBSCRIBE. These NOTIFYs contain the full state of the information requested by the subscriber.
notes: first NOTIFY after SUBSCRIBE and after each refresh carries conference-info state="full"

text: The default expiration time for a subscription to a conference is one hour.
notes: SUBSCRIBE without Expires gets 2xx with Expires: 3600

text: Once the conference ends, all subscriptions to that particular conference are terminated, with a reason of "noresource"...
notes: on conference end every subscriber gets NOTIFY Subscription-State: terminated;reason=noresource

text: All subscribers and notifiers MUST support the "application/conference-info+xml" data format...
notes: NOTIFY Content-Type is application/conference-info+xml when SUBSCRIBE has no Accept

text: If the Accept header field is present, it MUST include "application/conference-info+xml" and MAY include any other types.
notes: SUBSCRIBE with Accept lacking application/conference-info+xml is rejected 406

text: Therefore, all subscriptions SHOULD be authenticated and then authorized before approval.
notes: unauthenticated conference SUBSCRIBE is challenged 401/407 or rejected 403 when auth is configured

text: However, it is RECOMMENDED that all users in the conference be allowed to subscribe to the conference event package.
notes: SUBSCRIBE from a current participant to the conference URI is accepted

text: Notifications SHOULD be generated for the conference state when a new participant joins ... or a participant leaves ... the conference.
notes: join and leave each produce a partial NOTIFY with endpoint status connected / disconnected

text: Subject to a local focus policy, additional changes in participants' status, changes in their media types, and other optional information MAY be reported by the focus.
notes: hold on a participant leg produces a NOTIFY with endpoint status on-hold if the policy reports it

text: Changes in sidebar rosters SHOULD be reported by the focus to their participants and MAY be reported to others, subject to local policy.
notes: sidebar roster change produces NOTIFY to sidebar participants (only if sidebars supported)

text: Changes in conference identifiers and service URIs SHOULD be reported by the focus to the conference package subscribers.
notes: change of conf-uris or service-uris produces a NOTIFY with conference-description

text: Therefore, SUBSCRIBE requests for a conference should not generally fork.
notes: conference URI resolves to a single focus; one SUBSCRIBE yields exactly one dialog

text: If forking happens in the network, subscribers to this package MUST NOT establish more than a single SIP dialog as a result of a single SUBSCRIBE request.
notes: n/a: chappe plays no conference-package subscriber role; NOTIFYs go to the app's handler

text: ...it is RECOMMENDED that the server does not generate notifications for a single subscriber at a rate faster than once every 5 seconds.
notes: a burst of joins yields at most one NOTIFY per subscriber per 5 s (changes coalesced)

text: Cascaded foci MAY implement state agents (as defined in RFC 3265 [10]) for this package.
notes: cascaded focus state agent, role not played

text: Conference information is an XML document that MUST be well-formed and valid. It MUST be based on ... XML 1.0 and MUST be encoded using UTF-8.
notes: every NOTIFY body parses as UTF-8 XML 1.0 and validates against the RFC 4575 schema

text: The 'version' attribute MUST be included in the root <conference-info> element.
notes: root conference-info element carries version, entity and state attributes

text: A 'state' attribute of a child element in the document MUST be consistent with its parent 'state'.
notes: child state attributes never contradict the parent state in any NOTIFY

text: This means that if the parent's 'state' is "full", the state of its children MUST be "full".
notes: a state="full" document contains no partial or deleted child state

text: A parent element with "deleted" 'state' SHOULD NOT contain child elements.
notes: user or endpoint with state="deleted" is emitted with no child elements

text: The key value MUST be unique for the element among its siblings of the same type.
notes: no two sibling users, endpoints or media share an entity/id key in one document

text: Consequently, using relative URIs and lexical white space in these keys is NOT RECOMMENDED.
notes: entity keys are absolute URIs without whitespace

text: The first time a NOTIFY with a "full" document is received ... the conference package subscriber MUST set the local 'version' number...
notes: n/a: subscriber role not played (see R4575-15); chappe_sip_confinfo renders documents, it does not parse them

text: ...if the 'version' number in the received document is more than one number higher than the previous local version number, the subscriber MUST generate a subscription refresh request...
notes: n/a: subscriber role not played (see R4575-15)

text: A server MUST increment the version number for each notification (full, partial, and deleted) being sent to a subscriber and reporting a change in the conference document state.
notes: version increases on every change-reporting NOTIFY within one subscription

text: For each partial notification, the version number MUST be increased by one.
notes: consecutive partial NOTIFYs on one dialog carry version n, n+1 with no gaps

text: Note that a partial notification and a subsequent full notification over the same dialog MAY contain the same version number if no change in the conference state occurred in between.
notes: full NOTIFY after a refresh with no state change may reuse the previous version

text: Therefore, a conferencing server MUST ensure that all critical changes (stated as "SHOULD") are communicated to these specific subscribers; otherwise, these changes MUST be communicated to all subscribers...
notes: every SHOULD-level change (join/leave, conf-uris) reaches privileged subscribers when views are filtered by role

text: A "full" conference document MUST at least include the <conference-description> and <users> child elements.
notes: full NOTIFY contains conference-description and users

text: The value of the URI MUST be unique in the conference context and is included in the <uri> sub-element.
notes: conf-uris entries have distinct uri values

text: Each <entry> element SHOULD contain a <purpose> sub-element that describes what happens when accessing the URI.
notes: each conf-uris entry has a purpose element (e.g. participation)

text: The value of the URI MUST be unique in the conference context and is included in the <uri> sub-element.
notes: n/a: chappe_sip_confinfo never emits <service-uris>, so uniqueness there is vacuous; if added, reuse unique/3 as conf_uris does

text: The value of this element MUST be one of the values registered for "media" of SDP ... for example, "audio", "video", "text", and "message".
notes: available-media type is an SDP media token (audio) matching the m= line

text: The 'entity' value MUST be unique among all participants in the conference.
notes: user entity attributes are distinct across the roster

text: If, for some participants, the focus decides not to reveal this information ..., the host portion of the user URI MUST use the .invalid top level domain (TLD)...
notes: participant whose identity is hidden appears with an entity host ending in .invalid

text: ...SHOULD be used for a participant requesting privacy in accordance with the guidelines for generating anonymous URIs of RFC 3323 [11].
notes: participant joining with Privacy: id gets an RFC 3323 style anonymous URI in the roster

text: The focus also MUST construct the user portion of the URI so that the URI is unique among all participants of the same domain.
notes: two anonymous participants get distinct .invalid entity URIs

text: To do so, the focus MAY aggregate the multiple signaling sessions' information under a single <endpoint> element.
notes: separate signaling sessions of one device may appear under one endpoint element

text: entity: The server MUST generate the 'entity' key for each <endpoint> element included under the parent <user>, such that its value is unique in the user context.
notes: endpoint entity values are distinct within a user

text: when: This element ... contains the date and time that the endpoint was referred to the conference and SHOULD be expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) format.
notes: endpoint added by REFER carries referred/when as a UTC dateTime (Z suffix)

text: This element contains the status of the endpoint and can assume the following values: connected ... disconnected ... on-hold ... muted-via-focus ... pending ... alerting ... dialing-in ... dialing-out ... disconnecting
notes: endpoint status is one of the enumerated values and tracks the leg state (dialing-out, alerting, connected, on-hold, disconnected)

text: In this case, it is RECOMMENDED that the "aggregated" endpoint connectivity <status> reflects the status of the most active media.
notes: endpoint with muted video but live audio reports status connected

text: Therefore, implementations MAY choose to generate notifications on these statuses to certain participants only or not generate them at all, subject to local policy.
notes: transient statuses (alerting, disconnecting) are either always or never reported, per documented policy

text: This element contains the method by which the endpoint joined the conference and can assume the following values: dialed-in ... dialed-out ... focus-owner
notes: incoming legs report joining-method dialed-in, focus-initiated legs dialed-out

text: This element contains the method by which the endpoint departed the conference and can assume the following values: departed ... booted ... failed ... busy
notes: participant BYE gives disconnection-method departed, focus BYE booted, 486 on outgoing leg busy, other failure failed

text: Privacy policies MUST be consulted before revealing this information to other participants.
notes: call-info (SIP dialog ids) is omitted from views sent to other participants unless policy allows

text: The value of this element MUST be one of the values registered for "media" of SDP [3] and its later revision(s).
notes: endpoint media type is an SDP media token matching the negotiated m= line

text: If the <available-media> information ... is included in the conference document, the value of this element MUST be equal to the 'label' value of the corresponding media stream <entry>...
notes: endpoint media label equals an available-media entry label when available-media is present

text: For example, for Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) / RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) [13] media streams, the value MUST contain the synchronization source (SSRC) identifier value generated by the endpoint...
notes: endpoint media src-id, when present, equals the SSRC the endpoint sends

text: ...it is RECOMMENDED that a focus use a strong means for authentication and conference information protection and that it apply ... authorization rules when using the conference notification mechanism...
notes: conference subscriptions require authentication and pass an authorization check when configured

text: The mechanism used for conveying the conference information MUST ensure integrity and SHOULD ensure confidentially of the information.
notes: NOTIFYs are sent over TLS (sips) when the subscription arrived over TLS

text: It is RECOMMENDED that a focus authenticate a conference package subscriber using the normal SIP authentication mechanisms, such as Digest...
notes: SUBSCRIBE without credentials gets a 401/407 digest challenge; valid credentials accepted

text: ...an end-to-end means..., such as S/MIME described in Section 26.2.4 of RFC 3261 [8], SHOULD be used.
notes: S/MIME not implemented; mutual TLS hop-by-hop (R4575-56) is the substitute

text: If a strong end-to-end security means (such as above) is not available, it is RECOMMENDED that a focus use mutual hop-by-hop Transport Layer Security (TLS)...
notes: focus accepts SUBSCRIBE and sends NOTIFY over mutual TLS

text: As a result, a notification server MUST be capable of generating distinct conference information views to different subscribers, subject to a subscriber's role in a conference...
notes: two subscribers with different roles receive different documents (e.g. call-info only to a moderator)

text: For a participant requesting privacy, no identity information SHOULD be revealed by the focus in any included URI (e.g., the Address of Record, Contact, or GRUU).
notes: roster for a privacy-requesting participant shows no AoR, Contact or GRUU in any uri or entity element

text: A focus MUST support requests by participants for privacy.
notes: Privacy: id on the join INVITE changes the participant's roster rendering to anonymous

text: For these cases, the anonymous URI generation method outlined in Section 5.6 of this document MUST be followed.
notes: anonymous entity uses a .invalid host and a unique user part (see R4575-37, R4575-39)

text: reason: This element contains the reason the endpoint was referred to the conference. Including the information in the format defined by RFC 3326 [12] is RECOMMENDED.
notes: referred/reason, when present, is formatted as a Reason header value

text: by: This element contains the URI of the entity that caused the endpoint to be referred to the conference. In the case of SIP, it will be populated from the Referred-By header...
notes: referred/by equals the Referred-By URI of the REFER that added the endpoint

text: when: This element ... contains the date and time that the endpoint joined the conference and SHOULD be expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
notes: joining-info/when is a UTC dateTime (Z suffix)

text: reason: This element contains the reason the endpoint joined the conference. Including the information in the format defined by RFC 3326 [12] is RECOMMENDED.
notes: joining-info/reason, when present, is a Reason header value

text: when: This element ... contains the date and time that the endpoint departed the conference and SHOULD be expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
notes: disconnection-info/when is a UTC dateTime (Z suffix)

text: When known and meaningful, including the information as conveyed/reported by the call signaling in the format defined by RFC 3326 [12] is RECOMMENDED.
notes: disconnection-info/reason carries the Reason or cause from the BYE or failure response

text: Each <entry> element SHOULD contain a <purpose> sub-element.
notes: each service-uris entry, when emitted, has a purpose element

text: ...if the parent's 'state' is "partial", the state of its children MAY be either "partial", "full", or "deleted".
notes: participant removal is sent as a partial document with user state="deleted"

text: entity: This attribute contains the conference URI that identifies the conference being described in the document.
notes: conference-info entity equals the conference URI

text: REFER creates a dialog, and MAY be Record-Routed, hence MUST contain a single Contact header field value.
notes: REFER sent by chappe carries exactly one Contact; 2xx to a received REFER carries one Contact

text: REFERs occurring inside an existing dialog MUST follow the Route/Record-Route logic of that dialog.
notes: in-dialog REFER and its NOTIFYs carry the dialog route set (Route from Record-Route)

text: A REFER request MUST contain exactly one Refer-To header field value.
notes: REFER emitted by chappe has exactly one Refer-To

text: A UA accepting a well-formed REFER request SHOULD request approval from the user to proceed (this request could be satisfied with an interactive query or through accessing configured policy).
notes: received REFER is passed to the application policy before acceptance; a refused REFER gets 403 and no INVITE

text: If approval is granted, the UA MUST contact the resource identified by the URI in the Refer-To header field value as discussed in Section 2.4.3.
notes: accepted REFER triggers an INVITE (or BYE for method=BYE) to the Refer-To URI

text: An agent responding to a REFER method MUST return a 400 (Bad Request) if the request contained zero or more than one Refer-To header field values.
notes: REFER with no Refer-To and with two Refer-To each get 400; no INVITE is sent

text: An agent (including proxies generating local responses) MAY return a 100 (Trying) or any appropriate 4xx-6xx class response as prescribed by [1].
notes: rejected REFER gets a 4xx-6xx final response and no subscription is created

text: A UA not capable of accessing non-SIP URIs SHOULD NOT accept REFER requests to them.
notes: REFER with Refer-To tel:/http: (unsupported scheme) is rejected (416/488/403), not 2xx

text: If no final response has been generated according to the rules above, the UA MUST return a 202 Accepted response before the REFER transaction expires.
notes: superseded by RFC 7647 (R7647-04): accepted REFER gets 200, never 202, before Timer F

text: If a REFER request is accepted (that is, a 2xx class response is returned), the recipient MUST create a subscription and send notifications of the status of the refer as described in Section 2.4.4.
notes: after 2xx to REFER (without Refer-Sub: false) an initial NOTIFY Event: refer is sent

text: The NOTIFY mechanism defined in [2] MUST be used to inform the agent sending the REFER of the status of the reference.
notes: referrer receives RFC 6665 NOTIFYs reporting the referenced INVITE outcome

text: The dialog identifiers (To, From, and Call-ID) of each NOTIFY must match those of the REFER as they would if the REFER had been a SUBSCRIBE request.
notes: NOTIFY Call-ID equals REFER Call-ID, NOTIFY From tag = REFER To tag, To tag = REFER From tag

text: Each NOTIFY MUST contain an Event header field with a value of refer and possibly an id parameter (see Section 2.4.6).
notes: every refer NOTIFY has Event: refer (optionally ;id=)

text: Each NOTIFY MUST contain a body of type "message/sipfrag" [3].
notes: every refer NOTIFY has Content-Type: message/sipfrag

text: Terminating a subscription, either by explicitly unsubscribing or rejecting NOTIFY, is not an indication that the referenced request should be withdrawn or abandoned.
notes: referrer unsubscribing (Expires: 0) or rejecting a NOTIFY does not stop the triggered INVITE

text: In particular, an agent acting on a REFER request SHOULD NOT issue a CANCEL to any referenced SIP requests because the agent sending the REFER terminated its subscription to the refer event before the referenced request completes.
notes: after the referrer unsubscribes while the target rings, no CANCEL is sent on the triggered INVITE

text: If a SUBSCRIBE request for event refer is received for a subscription that does not already exist, it MUST be rejected with a 403.
notes: unsolicited SUBSCRIBE Event: refer with no matching subscription gets 403

text: The body of a NOTIFY MUST begin with a SIP Response Status-Line as defined in [1].
notes: sipfrag body first line matches "SIP/2.0 NNN reason"

text: The body MAY contain other SIP header fields to provide information about the outcome of the referenced action.
notes: sipfrag with extra headers is accepted when received; emitted body may carry only the status line

text: If a NOTIFY is generated when the subscription state is pending, its body should consist only of a status line containing a response code of 100.
notes: initial NOTIFY (pending) body is "SIP/2.0 100 Trying" while the triggered INVITE is in progress

text: Note that if the reference was to a non-SIP URI, status in any NOTIFYs to the referrer must still be in the form of SIP Response Status-Lines.
notes: sipfrag stays a SIP status line whatever the Refer-To scheme

text: Thus, for the second and subsequent REFER requests a UA receives in a given dialog, it MUST include an id parameter[2] in the Event header field of each NOTIFY containing the sequence number (the number from the CSeq header field value) of the REFER...
notes: second in-dialog REFER: its NOTIFYs carry Event: refer;id=<REFER CSeq number>

text: The final NOTIFY sent in response to a REFER MUST indicate the subscription has been "terminated" with a reason of "noresource".
notes: NOTIFY carrying the final status has Subscription-State: terminated;reason=noresource

text: The duration of an implicit subscription created by a REFER request is initially determined by the agent accepting the REFER and communicated to the subscribing agent in the Subscription-State header field's expire parameter in the first NOTIFY...
notes: first refer NOTIFY carries Subscription-State: active or pending with expires=N

text: The duration SHOULD be chosen to be longer than the time the referenced request will be given to complete.
notes: initial expires exceeds the triggered INVITE timeout

text: NOTIFYs to event refer SHOULD NOT be sent more frequently than once per second.
notes: with rapid 180/183/200 on the triggered INVITE, refer NOTIFYs are spaced >= 1 s or coalesced

text: A REFER must always receive an immediate (within the lifetime of a non-INVITE transaction) final response.
notes: final response to REFER is sent without waiting for the triggered INVITE to complete

text: An implementation MAY include more of a SIP message in that body to convey more information. ... Implementers must carefully consider what they choose to include.
notes: sipfrag does not carry the target's full response headers (identity) to the referrer

text: Each NOTIFY must contain a Subscription-State header field as defined in [2].
notes: every refer NOTIFY carries Subscription-State

text: This id parameter MAY be included in NOTIFYs to the first REFER a UA receives in a given dialog.
notes: NOTIFYs for the first REFER in a dialog may omit id; use is consistent within a subscription

text: A SUBSCRIBE sent to refresh or terminate this subscription MUST contain this id parameter.
notes: refresh/unsubscribe with Event: refer;id=<cseq> matches the right refer subscription; wrong id gets 481

text: Analogous to the case for SUBSCRIBE described in that document, the agent that issued the REFER MUST be prepared to receive a NOTIFY before the REFER transaction completes.
notes: when chappe sends a REFER, a NOTIFY arriving before the 2xx is accepted (200) and matched

text: A registrar aware of the definition of REFER SHOULD return a 405 response.
notes: registrar role

text: A user agent (UA) accepting a REFER that creates a subscription MUST populate its Contact header field with a GRUU.
notes: GRUU (RFC 5627) not implemented: the REFER 2xx carries the stack Contact; for a focus the conference URI already routes to it

text: A user agent constructing a REFER request that could result in an implicit subscription in a dialog MUST build it as an out-of-dialog message as defined in [RFC3261], unless the remote endpoint is an older implementation of RFC 3515...
notes: REFER that may create a subscription is sent out of dialog (with Target-Dialog) unless the peer lacks GRUU/6665 support

text: A user agent wishing to identify an existing dialog (such as for call transfer as defined in [RFC5589]) MUST use the "Target-Dialog" extension defined in [RFC4538] to do so, and user agents accepting REFER MUST be able to process that extension...
notes: out-of-dialog REFER with Target-Dialog naming an existing dialog is associated with that dialog

text: Specifically, an element accepting a REFER request MUST NOT reply with a 202 response code and MUST treat any 202 responses received as identical to a 200 response.
notes: accepted REFER gets 200 not 202; a received 202 to our REFER is handled like 200; dup: R7647-05

text: If a user agent can be certain that no implicit subscription will be created as a result of sending a REFER request (such as by requiring an extension that disallows any such subscription [RFC7614]), the REFER request MAY be sent within an existing dialog...
notes: in-dialog REFER from chappe only with Refer-Sub: false plus Require: norefersub or explicitsub

text: If the REFER-Recipient supports the extension and is willing to process the REFER transaction without establishing an implicit subscription, it MUST insert the "Refer-Sub" header field set to "false" in the 2xx response to the REFER-Issuer.
notes: REFER with Refer-Sub: false gets 2xx with Refer-Sub: false and no NOTIFY follows

text: If the REFER-Issuer inserts the "Refer-Sub" header field set to "false", but the REFER-Recipient doesn't grant the suggestion (i.e., either does not include the "Refer-Sub" header field or includes ... "true" in the 2xx response), an implicit subscription is created...
notes: if the 2xx omits Refer-Sub or says true, refer NOTIFYs are sent as usual

text: This document also defines a new option tag, "norefersub". This tag, when included in the Supported header field, specifies that a User Agent (UA) is capable of accepting a REFER request without creating an implicit subscription...
notes: Supported: norefersub is advertised only when Refer-Sub: false is honoured

text: As described in Section 8.2.2.3 in [2], a REFER-Recipient will reject a REFER request containing a Require: norefersub header field with a 420 (Bad Extension) response unless it supports this extension.
notes: Require: norefersub is accepted if supported, else 420 with Unsupported: norefersub

text: If more than one Replaces header field is present in an INVITE, or if a Replaces header field is present in a request other than INVITE, the UAS MUST reject the request with a 400 Bad Request response.
notes: INVITE with two Replaces, and OPTIONS/REFER with Replaces, get 400

text: If both a Replaces header field and another header field with contradictory semantics are present in a request, the request MUST be rejected with a 400 "Bad Request" response.
notes: INVITE carrying both Replaces and Join gets 400

text: If the Replaces header field matches more than one dialog, the UA MUST act as if no match is found.
notes: n/a, holds by construction: the dialog index is one ETS set keyed by the full dialog id (chappe_sip_dialog_index), so a Replaces header matches at most one dialog

text: If no match is found, the UAS rejects the INVITE and returns a 481 Call/Transaction Does Not Exist response.
notes: Replaces naming an unknown Call-ID/tags gets 481

text: Likewise, if the Replaces header field matches a dialog which was not created with an INVITE, the UAS MUST reject the request with a 481 response.
notes: Replaces naming a SUBSCRIBE/REFER dialog gets 481

text: If the Replaces header field matches a dialog which has already terminated, the UA SHOULD decline the request with a 603 Declined response.
notes: Replaces naming a dialog already terminated by BYE gets 603

text: If the Replaces header field matches an active dialog, the UA MUST verify that the initiator of the new INVITE is authorized to replace the matched dialog.
notes: INVITE with valid Replaces refused by the authorization policy gets 401/403 and the matched dialog is unchanged

text: If the replacement request contains a Referred-By header that corresponds to the user being replaced, the UA SHOULD treat the replacement as if the replacement was authorized by the replaced party.
notes: Replaces with Referred-By equal to the replaced party identity is authorized

text: The UA MAY apply other local policy to authorize the remainder of the request.
notes: application policy hook can refuse the replacement INVITE

text: If the UA cannot accept the new INVITE (for example: it cannot establish required QoS or keying, or it has incompatible media), the UA MUST return an appropriate error response and MUST leave the matched dialog unchanged.
notes: Replaces INVITE with no common codec gets 488 and the old dialog keeps its media

text: If the Replaces header field matches a confirmed dialog, it checks for the presence of the "early-only" flag ... If the flag is present, the UA rejects the request with a 486 Busy response. Otherwise, it accepts the new INVITE ... and shuts down the replaced dialog by sending a BYE.
notes: confirmed dialog: early-only gives 486; otherwise 200 to new INVITE and BYE on the replaced dialog

text: If the Replaces header field matches an early dialog that was not initiated by this UA, it returns a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) response to the new INVITE, and leaves the matched dialog unchanged.
notes: Replaces naming an early dialog not initiated by chappe gets 481; own early dialog is CANCELled after 200

text: A UAC MUST NOT send an INVITE with a Replaces header field that attempts to replace an early dialog which was not originated by the target of the INVITE with a Replaces header field.
notes: application duty: chappe never builds an INVITE with Replaces; the value comes from the app headers or verbatim from a Refer-To

text: Although this specification takes reasonable precautions to prevent unexpected behavior in the face of forking, implementations SHOULD only address replacement requests (i.e., set the Request-URI of the replacement request) to the SIP Contact URI of the target.
notes: INVITE with Replaces from chappe has Request-URI = remote target (Contact) of the named dialog

text: A Replaces header field MUST contain exactly one to-tag and exactly one from-tag, as they are required for unique dialog matching.
notes: generated Replaces has one to-tag and one from-tag; received Replaces missing a tag gets 400

text: UAs which support the Replaces header MUST include the "replaces" option tag in a Supported header field.
notes: INVITEs, 200s and OPTIONS responses from chappe carry Supported: replaces

text: As such, invitations with the Replaces header MUST only be accepted if the peer requesting replacement has been properly authenticated using a standard SIP mechanism (Digest or S/MIME), and authorized to request a replacement of the target dialog.
notes: Replaces INVITE accepted only from a peer authenticated by Digest (or TLS identity)

text: In addition, implementations which support the Replaces header SHOULD also implement the Referred-By mechanism.
notes: Referred-By from REFER is copied into the triggered INVITE and parsed on received INVITE with Replaces

text: Implementations SHOULD NOT rely on this method as an authorization mechanism.
notes: prior participation alone does not authorize a Replaces

text: Since manipulating this dialog information could cause User Agents to replace the wrong dialog, use of message integrity protection for this information is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED.
notes: no end-to-end integrity (S/MIME) by design; TLS hop-by-hop only

text: Use of end-to-end security mechanisms to encrypt this information is also RECOMMENDED.
notes: no end-to-end encryption (S/MIME) by design; TLS hop-by-hop only

text: The Referred-By header SHOULD reference a corresponding, valid Refererred-By Authenticated Identity Body [5].
notes: S/MIME Authenticated Identity Body not verified by design; Referred-By trusted only from authenticated peers

text: A User Agent that wishes to replace a single existing early or confirmed dialog with a new dialog of its own, MAY send the target User Agent an INVITE request containing a Replaces header field.
notes: attended transfer: chappe sends INVITE with Replaces carrying Call-ID/to-tag/from-tag of the target dialog

text: UAs that want explicit failure notification if Replaces is not supported MAY include the "replaces" option in a Require header field.
notes: INVITE with Replaces may carry Require: replaces so a non-supporting target answers 420

text: 200-class responses to SUBSCRIBE requests also MUST contain an "Expires" header field.
notes: 200 to SUBSCRIBE carries Expires

text: The period of time in the response MAY be shorter but MUST NOT be longer than specified in the request.
notes: SUBSCRIBE Expires: 60 gets 200 Expires <= 60

text: The package name in the "Event" header field MUST match the "Event" header field in the corresponding SUBSCRIBE request.
notes: NOTIFY Event equals the SUBSCRIBE Event

text: When present, the body of the NOTIFY request MUST be formatted into one of the body formats specified in the "Accept" header field of the corresponding SUBSCRIBE request (or the default type according to the event package description...)
notes: NOTIFY Content-Type is in the SUBSCRIBE Accept list or the package default

text: Notifiers MUST NOT create subscriptions except upon receipt of a SUBSCRIBE request.
notes: no NOTIFY (other than implicit refer) is sent to a peer that did not SUBSCRIBE

text: In particular, notifiers MUST NOT wait for a user response before returning a final response to a SUBSCRIBE request.
notes: SUBSCRIBE gets a final response without waiting on user input, within the non-INVITE transaction lifetime

text: If not, the notifier SHOULD return a 489 (Bad Event) response to indicate that the specified event/event class is not understood.
notes: SUBSCRIBE with an unsupported Event (e.g. presence) to the conference URI gets 489 with Allow-Events

text: The notifier SHOULD also perform any necessary authentication and authorization per its local policy.
notes: with auth configured, SUBSCRIBE without credentials is challenged (401/407) or rejected

text: Upon successfully accepting or refreshing a subscription, notifiers MUST send a NOTIFY request immediately to communicate the current resource state to the subscriber.
notes: a NOTIFY follows each 200 to SUBSCRIBE and each refresh

text: If authorization fails based on an access list or some other automated mechanism (i.e., it can be automatically authoritatively determined that the subscriber is not authorized to subscribe), the notifier SHOULD reply to the request with a 403...
notes: SUBSCRIBE from an identity denied by policy gets 403

text: If the duration specified in a SUBSCRIBE request is unacceptably short, the notifier SHOULD respond with a 423 (Interval Too Brief) response.
notes: SUBSCRIBE Expires below the configured minimum (and > 0) gets 423 with Min-Expires

text: When removing a subscription, the notifier SHOULD send a NOTIFY request with a "Subscription-State" value of "terminated" to inform it that the subscription is being removed. If such a request is sent, the "Subscription-State" header field SHOULD contain a "reason=timeout"...
notes: subscription not refreshed gets NOTIFY Subscription-State: terminated;reason=timeout at expiry

text: When a change in the subscribed state occurs, the notifier SHOULD immediately construct and send a NOTIFY request, unless the state transition is caused by a NOTIFY transaction failure.
notes: roster change produces a NOTIFY without waiting for a refresh (subject to rate limit)

text: If the NOTIFY transaction fails due to the receipt of a 404, 405, 410, 416, 480-485, 489, 501, or 604 response to the NOTIFY request, the notifier MUST remove the corresponding subscription.
notes: subscriber answers NOTIFY with 481; no further NOTIFY is sent on that subscription

text: If the value of the "Subscription-State" header field is "active" or "pending", the notifier MUST also include in the "Subscription-State" header field an "expires" parameter that indicates the time remaining on the subscription.
notes: active/pending NOTIFYs carry ;expires= with the remaining time

text: Any user agent that can act as a notifier for one or more event packages SHOULD include an appropriate "Allow-Events" header field indicating all supported events in all methods which initiate dialogs and their responses (such as INVITE and 200-class...)
notes: focus INVITE and 200 carry Allow-Events listing conference and refer

text: Notifiers MUST implement the Globally Routable User Agent URI (GRUU) extension defined in [RFC5627], and MUST use a GRUU as their local target.
notes: GRUU (RFC 5627) not implemented, as R7647-01: the NOTIFY and 200 Contact is the stack Contact; for a focus the conference URI already routes back to the notifier

text: If an "id" parameter is present in the SUBSCRIBE request used to establish a subscription, that "id" parameter MUST also be present in all corresponding NOTIFY requests.
notes: SUBSCRIBE Event: conference;id=7 gets NOTIFYs with Event: conference;id=7

text: If a User Agent Server (UAS) receives a CANCEL request that matches a known SUBSCRIBE or NOTIFY transaction, it MUST respond to the CANCEL request, but otherwise ignore it.
notes: CANCEL of a pending SUBSCRIBE gets 200 and the SUBSCRIBE still completes normally

text: To reduce the chances of such an attack, implementations of notifiers SHOULD require authentication.
notes: with auth configured, SUBSCRIBE without credentials is challenged

text: Implementations conformant with the current specification MUST treat an incoming 202 response as identical to a 200 response and MUST NOT generate 202 response codes to SUBSCRIBE or NOTIFY requests.
notes: SUBSCRIBE is answered 200, never 202; a 202 received to our SUBSCRIBE is treated as 200

text: If the value of the "Subscription-State" header field is "terminated", the notifier SHOULD also include a "reason" parameter.
notes: terminated NOTIFYs carry reason= (noresource, timeout, deactivated, rejected)

text: NOTIFY requests MUST contain a "Subscription-State" header field with a value of "active", "pending", or "terminated".
notes: every NOTIFY has Subscription-State with active, pending or terminated

text: The notifier MAY use this mechanism to shorten a subscription; however, this mechanism MUST NOT be used to lengthen a subscription.
notes: NOTIFY ;expires never exceeds the Expires granted in the 200

text: If the NOTIFY request fails due to expiration of SIP Timer F (transaction timeout), the notifier SHOULD remove the subscription.
notes: NOTIFY left unanswered until Timer F removes the subscription; no further NOTIFYs

text: As with the initial subscription, the server MAY shorten the amount of time until expiration but MUST NOT increase it.
notes: refresh SUBSCRIBE Expires: 30 gets 200 Expires <= 30

text: The "Allow-Events" header field, if present, MUST include a comprehensive and inclusive list of tokens that indicates the event packages for which the user agent can act as a notifier.
notes: Allow-Events lists every package the focus serves (conference, refer) and no unsupported token

text: If a notifier receives a SUBSCRIBE request for a new subscription on an existing dialog, it MAY choose to implement dialog sharing behavior. ... The error text of such 403 responses SHOULD indicate that dialog sharing is not supported.
notes: SUBSCRIBE inside an INVITE dialog either works or gets 403 with reason text about dialog sharing

text: If a notifier does not support PINT, it SHOULD return 489 (Bad Event) to any SUBSCRIBE requests without an "Event" header field.
notes: SUBSCRIBE without Event gets 489

text: In these cases, the notifier SHOULD always return a 200 (OK) response. While the subsequent NOTIFY request may not convey true state, it MUST appear to contain a potentially correct piece of data from the point of view of the subscriber...
notes: subscriber denied by privacy policy gets 200 and a plausible (e.g. empty-roster) NOTIFY

text: To prevent such attacks, implementations SHOULD provide integrity protection across the "Call-ID", "CSeq", and "Subscription-State" header fields and the bodies of NOTIFY requests.
notes: NOTIFYs sent over TLS when the subscription arrived over TLS (hop-by-hop integrity)

text: Upon receiving a NOTIFY request, the subscriber should check that it matches at least one of its outstanding subscriptions; if not, it MUST return a 481 (Subscription does not exist) response...
notes: NOTIFY matching no outstanding subscription (e.g. stale refer) gets 481

text: In particular, subscribers MUST NOT wait for a user response before returning a final response to a NOTIFY request.
notes: refer NOTIFYs received after chappe sends REFER are answered immediately with 200

text: It MUST NOT appear in any other SIP requests and MUST NOT appear in responses.
notes: Event header appears only in SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY; never in INVITE or responses sent by chappe

text: Subscribers MUST include exactly one "Event" header field in SUBSCRIBE requests, indicating to which event or class of events they are subscribing.
notes: chappe_sip:subscribe_to/3: the initial SUBSCRIBE, its refresh and the unsubscribe each carry one Event, the package asked for

text: SUBSCRIBE requests SHOULD contain an "Expires" header field (defined in [RFC3261]).
notes: every SUBSCRIBE the subscriber sends carries Expires: the duration asked for, 0 to unsubscribe

text: If a SUBSCRIBE request to refresh a subscription receives a 404, 405, 410, 416, 480-485, 489, 501, or 604 response, the subscriber MUST consider the subscription terminated.
notes: a refresh answered 481 ends the subscription: the owner gets {terminated, {refresh_failed, 481}} and no SUBSCRIBE follows

text: After the expiration of Timer N, the subscriber SHOULD reject any such NOTIFY requests that would otherwise establish a new dialog usage with a 481 (Subscription does not exist) response code.
notes: the SUBSCRIBE is answered 200 but no NOTIFY comes before Timer N: the owner gets {failed, timer_n} and a NOTIFY sent after it gets 481

text: Due to the potential for out-of-order messages, packet loss, and forking, the subscriber MUST be prepared to receive NOTIFY requests before the SUBSCRIBE transaction has completed.
notes: a NOTIFY sent before the 200 to the SUBSCRIBE gets 200 and reaches the owner; the dialog is formed from it

text: To prevent spoofing of events, NOTIFY requests SHOULD be authenticated using any defined SIP authentication mechanism, such as those described in Sections 22.2 and 23 of [RFC3261].
notes: chappe does not challenge NOTIFYs itself: a NOTIFY matches a subscription only by Call-ID, tags and Event, and a chappe_sip:use(<<"NOTIFY">>, Mw) middleware can challenge them

text: If the header field also contains an "expires" parameter, the subscriber SHOULD take it as the authoritative subscription duration and adjust accordingly.
notes: a NOTIFY active;expires=N shorter than the granted Expires brings the refresh SUBSCRIBE before N seconds

text: If the header field also contains an "expires" parameter, the subscriber SHOULD take it as the authoritative subscription duration and adjust accordingly.
notes: the same for pending;expires=N: the refresh comes before N seconds

text: If the "Subscription-State" value is "terminated", the subscriber MUST consider the subscription terminated.
notes: a NOTIFY terminated;reason=noresource gets 200, the owner gets {terminated, noresource} and no SUBSCRIBE follows

text: The "expires" parameter has no semantics for "terminated" -- notifiers SHOULD NOT include an "expires" parameter on a "Subscription-State" header field with a value of "terminated", and subscribers MUST ignore any such parameter, if present.
notes: a terminated NOTIFY with expires=600 still ends the subscription

text: If no reason code or an unknown reason code is present, the client MAY attempt to re-subscribe at any time (unless a "retry-after" parameter is present, in which case the client SHOULD NOT attempt re-subscription until after the number of seconds specified by the "retry-after" parameter).
notes: terminated with an unknown reason and retry-after=1: the new SUBSCRIBE comes no sooner than 1 s

text: deactivated:  The subscription has been terminated, but the subscriber SHOULD retry immediately with a new subscription.
notes: terminated;reason=deactivated: a new SUBSCRIBE at once, with a new Call-ID and From tag

text: probation:  The subscription has been terminated, but the client SHOULD retry at some later time (as long as the resource's state is still relevant to the client at that time).
notes: terminated;reason=probation: a new SUBSCRIBE later (after retry-after, else probation_retry seconds)

text: If a "retry-after" parameter is also present, the client SHOULD wait at least the number of seconds specified by that parameter before attempting to re-subscribe.
notes: probation;retry-after=1: the new SUBSCRIBE comes no sooner than 1 s

text: rejected:  The subscription has been terminated due to change in authorization policy.  Clients SHOULD NOT attempt to re-subscribe.
notes: terminated;reason=rejected: no new SUBSCRIBE, the owner gets {terminated, rejected}

text: giveup:  The subscription has been terminated because the notifier could not obtain authorization in a timely fashion.  If a "retry-after" parameter is also present, the client SHOULD wait at least the number of seconds specified by that parameter before attempting to re-subscribe; otherwise, the client MAY retry immediately, but will likely get put back into pending state.
notes: giveup;retry-after=1: the new SUBSCRIBE comes no sooner than 1 s

text: noresource:  The subscription has been terminated because the resource state that was being monitored no longer exists.  Clients SHOULD NOT attempt to re-subscribe.
notes: terminated;reason=noresource: no new SUBSCRIBE

text: Clients SHOULD NOT attempt to re-subscribe after receiving a reason code of "invariant", regardless of the presence of or value of a "retry-after" parameter.
notes: terminated;reason=invariant;retry-after=1: no new SUBSCRIBE

text: Once the notification is deemed acceptable to the subscriber, the subscriber SHOULD return a 200 response.
notes: every NOTIFY matching a subscription of ours gets 200 before it reaches the owner

text: The subscriber MUST therefore be prepared to receive NOTIFY requests with "From:" tags that differ from the "To:" tag received in the SUBSCRIBE 200-class response.
notes: a NOTIFY from a tag other than the 200's gets 200 and is a subscription of its own: the owner gets {forked, Sub2}, then its NOTIFYs

text: If the subscriber receives a success response to the SUBSCRIBE request that indicates that no NOTIFY request will be generated -- such as the 204 response defined for use with the optional extension described in [RFC5839] -- then it MUST cancel Timer N.
notes: n/a: chappe does not do RFC 5839 conditional subscriptions, so it never asks for a 204

text: However, 1800 seconds (30 minutes) is RECOMMENDED as the value for the Session-Expires header field.
notes: Session-Expires chappe inserts (INVITE or 2xx) defaults to 1800 s

text: In other words, SIP entities MUST be prepared to handle Session-Expires header field values of any duration greater than 90 seconds, but entities that insert the Session-Expires header field SHOULD NOT choose values of less tha...
notes: peer Session-Expires of 91 s accepted; chappe's own inserted value is not below 1800 s unless configured

text: When present in a request or response, its value MUST NOT be less than 90 seconds.
notes: chappe never emits Min-SE or Session-Expires below 90 s; Session-Expires below 90 from the peer gets 422

text: The Min-SE header field MUST NOT be used in responses except for those with a 422 response code.
notes: Min-SE appears only in chappe's 422 responses, never in 2xx or other responses

text: The 422 response MUST contain a Min-SE header field with the minimum timer for that server.
notes: every 422 chappe sends carries Min-SE

text: A UAC that supports the session timer extension defined here MUST include a Supported header field in each request (except ACK), listing the option tag 'timer' [2].
notes: outgoing INVITE, re-INVITE, UPDATE, BYE, REFER, SUBSCRIBE all carry Supported: timer

text: It MUST do so even if the UAC is not requesting usage of the session timer for this session.
notes: Supported: timer present even with session timers disabled for the call

text: However, usage of either Require or Proxy-Require by the UAC is NOT RECOMMENDED.
notes: outgoing INVITE has no Require: timer and no Proxy-Require: timer

text: If a Min-SE header is included in the initial session refresh request, the value of the Session-Expires MUST be greater than or equal to the value in Min-SE.
notes: when chappe sends Min-SE, Session-Expires is >= Min-SE

text: However, it is RECOMMENDED that the parameter be omitted so that it can be selected by the negotiation mechanisms described below.
notes: initial outgoing INVITE omits the refresher parameter

text: If it does, the UAC MUST look for the Session-Expires header field to process the response.
notes: 2xx with Require: timer is processed for Session-Expires and refresher

text: UACs MUST be prepared to receive a Session-Expires header field in a response, even if none were present in the request.
notes: 2xx with Session-Expires to an INVITE without one arms the timer per the response

text: The UAC MUST set the identity of the refresher to the value of this parameter.
notes: refresher=uac in 2xx: chappe refreshes; refresher=uas: chappe expects the peer to refresh

text: If the UA seeks to continue with the session beyond the session expiration, it MUST generate a refresh before the session expiration.
notes: as UAC refresher, chappe sends re-INVITE or UPDATE before session expiration

text: RECOMMENDED that this refresh be sent once half the session interval has elapsed.
notes: as UAC refresher, the refresh is sent at about half the session interval

text: If the response to a session refresh request is a 422 (Session Interval Too Small) response message, then the UAC MAY retry the request.
notes: 422 to an outgoing INVITE triggers one retry with Min-SE and a raised Session-Expires

text: This new request constitutes a new transaction and SHOULD have the same value as the Call-ID, To, and From of the previous request, but the CSeq should contain a new sequence number that is one higher than the previous.
notes: retry after 422 keeps Call-ID, To, From and increments CSeq by one

text: The values of Supported, Require, and Proxy-Require used in the initial Session refresh request MUST be used.
notes: refreshes repeat the Supported/Require values of the initial request

text: The UAC MUST insert the Min-SE header field into a session refresh request for a particular dialog if it has ever received a 422 response to a previous session refresh request on the same dialog, or if it has received a session...
notes: after a 422 or a received Min-SE on the dialog, all chappe refreshes carry Min-SE

text: The value of the Min-SE header field present in a session refresh request MUST be the largest value among all Min-SE header field values returned in all 422 responses or received in session refresh requests, on the same dialog,...
notes: Min-SE chappe sends equals the largest value seen in 422s or requests on the dialog

text: In a session refresh request sent within a dialog with an active session timer, the Session-Expires header field SHOULD be present.
notes: mid-dialog refresh carries Session-Expires = max(Min-SE, current interval)

text: If the session refresh request is not the initial one, it is RECOMMENDED that the refresher parameter be set to 'uac' if the element sending the request is currently performing refreshes, and to 'uas' if its peer is performing...
notes: non-initial refresh from the refresher side sets refresher=uac; from the other side refresher=uas

text: If a UAC knows that its peer supports the UPDATE method, it is RECOMMENDED that UPDATE be used instead of a re-INVITE.
notes: refresh uses UPDATE when the peer Allow lists UPDATE, else re-INVITE

text: It is RECOMMENDED that the UPDATE request not contain an offer [4], but a re-INVITE SHOULD contain one, even if the details of the session have not changed.
notes: UPDATE refresh has no SDP; re-INVITE refresh carries an offer

text: In that case, the offer MUST indicate that it has not changed.
notes: refresh re-INVITE offer keeps the SDP o= version unchanged when media is unchanged

text: The same is true for an answer exchanged as a result of a session refresh request; if it has not changed, that MUST be indicated.
notes: answer to a peer refresh keeps the SDP o= version unchanged when media is unchanged

text: Unlike the UA, it MUST NOT send a BYE.
notes: proxy role; chappe as UA or B2BUA does send BYE (see R4028-39, R4028-41)

text: If an incoming request contains a Supported header field with a value 'timer' and a Session Expires header field, the UAS MAY reject the INVITE request with a 422 (Session Interval Too Small) response if the session interval in...
notes: incoming INVITE with Supported: timer and Session-Expires below the local minimum gets 422

text: When sending the 422 response, the UAS MUST include a Min-SE header field with the value of its minimum interval.
notes: 422 to an incoming INVITE includes Min-SE with chappe's minimum

text: This minimum interval MUST NOT be lower than 90 seconds.
notes: configured minimum below 90 s is refused or clamped to 90

text: If the UAS wishes to accept the request, it copies the value of the Session-Expires header field from the request into the 2xx response.
notes: accepted INVITE with Session-Expires gets a 200 OK echoing Session-Expires (same or reduced value)

text: The UAS response MAY reduce its value but MUST NOT set it to a duration lower than the value in the Min-SE header field in the request, if it is present; otherwise the UAS MAY reduce its value but MUST NOT set it to a duration...
notes: 2xx Session-Expires is never below the request Min-SE (or 90 s)

text: The UAS MUST NOT increase the value of the Session-Expires header field.
notes: 2xx Session-Expires is never above the request value

text: The UAS MUST set the value of the refresher parameter in the Session-Expires header field in the 2xx response.
notes: 2xx Session-Expires always has refresher; UAC choice honoured, uas when the UAC lacks timer support

text: If the refresher parameter in the Session-Expires header field in the 2xx response has a value of 'uac', the UAS MUST place a Require header field into the response with the value 'timer'.
notes: 2xx with refresher=uac carries Require: timer

text: If the refresher parameter in the 2xx response has a value of 'uas' and the Supported header field in the request contained the value 'timer', the UAS SHOULD place a Require header field into the response with the value 'timer'.
notes: 2xx with refresher=uas to a request with Supported: timer carries Require: timer

text: If UA wishes to continue with the session beyond the session expiration, it MUST generate a refresh before the session expiration.
notes: as UAS refresher, chappe sends re-INVITE or UPDATE before expiration

text: It is RECOMMENDED that this refresh be sent once half the session interval has elapsed.
notes: as UAS refresher, the refresh is sent at about half the interval

text: If the session refresh request transaction times out or generates a 408 or 481 response, then the UAC sends a BYE request as per Section 12.2.1.2 of RFC 3261 [2].
notes: refresh that times out or gets 408/481 causes chappe to send BYE on that leg

text: However, the UAC SHOULD NOT continuously retry the request if the server indicates the same error response.
notes: repeated identical error to a refresh does not loop; at most one retry per error

text: Similarly, if the side not performing refreshes does not receive a session refresh request before the session expiration, it SHOULD send a BYE to terminate the session, slightly before the session expiration.
notes: no refresh received from the peer refresher: chappe sends BYE before expiry

text: The minimum of 32 seconds and one third of the session interval is RECOMMENDED.
notes: BYE sent min(32 s, interval/3) before session expiration

text: As a result, it is RECOMMENDED that an element send a request with a Session-Expires header field or a Supported header field with the value 'timer' by using TLS.
notes: session timer requests go over TLS when the peer supports it

text: A UA that inserts a Session-Expires header into a request or response SHOULD include a Contact URI that is a SIPS URI.
notes: on a sips/TLS dialog the Contact sent with Session-Expires is a sips URI

text: The Reason header field MAY appear in any request within a dialog, in any CANCEL request and in any response whose status code explicitly allows the presence of this header field.
notes: BYE and CANCEL sent by chappe may carry Reason; Reason is not added to other requests outside a dialog

text: Proxies generating a CANCEL request upon reception of a CANCEL from the previous hop that contains a Reason header field SHOULD copy it into the new CANCEL request.
notes: addressed to proxies; B2BUA equivalent: CANCEL relayed to the other leg copies the inbound Reason

text: Any SIP status code MAY appear in the Reason header field of a request.
notes: received request with Reason: SIP;cause=<any code> is accepted

text: A SIP message MAY contain more than one Reason value (i.e., multiple Reason lines), but all of them MUST have different protocol values (e.g., one SIP and another Q.850).
notes: multiple Reason values emitted have distinct protocols (e.g. one SIP, one Q.850)

text: Reason protocols MUST refer to either an ITU-T Recommendation number, an IETF protocol name or the recognized protocol identifier from another standardization organization.
notes: protocol token in emitted Reason is SIP, Q.850 or another registered identifier

text: Thus, it is RECOMMENDED that this header field is protected by a suitable integrity mechanism.
notes: Reason carried over TLS when the transport is available

text: A REFER request MUST NOT contain more than one Referred-By header field value.
notes: REFER with two Referred-By values is rejected with 400

text: A UA accepting a REFER request (a referee) to a SIP URI (using either the sip: or sips: scheme) MUST copy any Referred-By header field value and token into the referenced request without modification.
notes: INVITE triggered by REFER carries the Referred-By value (and token body if any) unchanged

text: A referee MAY reject a REFER request that does not contain a Referred-By token with a 429 "Provide Referrer Identity" response.
notes: REFER without Referred-By token is accepted (no 429) unless policy requires it

text: A referee SHOULD NOT reject a request that contains a Referred-By token encrypted to a key it does not possess simply because it cannot decrypt the token.
notes: REFER with an undecryptable Referred-By token is not rejected for that reason

text: A referee SHOULD present the same identity to the referrer and the refer target.
notes: From identity of the triggered INVITE matches the identity presented to the referrer

text: If a Referred-By header field value is present, the receiving UA can consider itself a refer target and MAY apply additional admission policies based on the contents of the Referred-By header field and token.
notes: INVITE carrying Referred-By may be subject to admission policy on that value

text: If such behavior could affect admission policy (including influencing the agent's user by rendering misleading content), the refer target SHOULD require that a valid Referred-By token be present.
notes: if admission uses Referred-By, an unsigned value is not trusted alone

text: If the agent provides any information from the Referred-By header to its user as part of processing the request, it MUST notify the user that the information is suspect.
notes: n/a: chappe has no user or UI; Referred-By tokens are never verified (R3892-09/12 deviations), so every value is unverified by definition

text: The refer target MUST reject an otherwise well-formed request with an invalid Referred-By token (see Section 4) with a 429 error response.
notes: S/MIME token validation not implemented by design, so an invalid token cannot be detected for 429

text: If the referrer-uri contains a comma, question mark, or semicolon, (for example, if it contains URI parameters) the URI MUST be enclosed in angle brackets (< and >).
notes: Referred-By URI with parameters is emitted within angle brackets

text: Proxies do not need to be able to read Referred-By header field values and MUST NOT remove or modify them.
notes: proxy role

text: A refer target MUST treat a Referred-By token with an invalid signature as an invalid token.
notes: S/MIME token signature validation not implemented by design; tokens treated as absent

text: It is RECOMMENDED that user agents seeking anonymity use a display- name of "Anonymous".
notes: anonymised identity chappe presents (From, roster display) uses display-name "Anonymous"

text: For these reasons, the hostname value 'anonymous.invalid' SHOULD be used for anonymous URIs (see [3] for more information about the reserved 'invalid' DNS TLD).
notes: anonymised URIs use host anonymous.invalid

text: The full recommended form of the From header for anonymity is (note that this From header, like all others, MUST contain a valid and unique 'tag=' parameter):
notes: anonymous From on an outgoing INVITE still has a unique tag

text: This document thus recommends that the host portion of URIs that are used in the routing of subsequent requests, such as URIs appearing in the Contact header, SHOULD NOT be altered by the user agent due to privacy considerations.
notes: Contact host of anonymised dialogs stays routable

text: An intermediary MUST NOT modify the Privacy header in any way if the 'none' priv-value is already specified.
notes: Privacy: none is relayed untouched to the other leg

text: When session privacy is requested, user agents MUST NOT encrypt SDP bodies in messages.
notes: SDP stays unencrypted when session privacy is requested

text: User agents MUST NOT populate any other priv-values (including 'critical') in a Privacy header that contains a value of 'none'.
notes: application duty: chappe never builds a Privacy header, it only relays one (R3323-05)

text: When a Privacy header is constructed, it MUST consist of either the value 'none', or one or more of the values 'user', 'header' and 'session' (each of which MUST appear at most once) which MAY in turn be followed by the 'critic...
notes: application duty: chappe never builds a Privacy header, it only relays one (R3323-05)

text: When a message arrives at a server that can act as a privacy service, the service SHOULD evaluate the level of privacy requested in a Privacy header.
notes: Privacy on an ingress INVITE is evaluated and drives identity anonymisation on the other leg

text: However, if the Privacy header value of 'none' is specified in a message, privacy services MUST NOT perform any privacy function and MUST NOT remove or modify the Privacy header.
notes: Privacy: none: identity relayed as is and header left intact

text: Privacy services MUST implement support for the 'none' and 'critical' privacy tokens, and MAY implement any of other privacy levels described in Section 4.2 as well as any extensions that are not detailed in this document.
notes: none and critical tokens supported by the privacy function

text: If the 'critical' privacy level is present in the Privacy header of a request, then if the privacy service is incapable of performing all of the levels of privacy specified in the Privacy header then it MUST fail the request wi...
notes: Privacy with critical and a level chappe cannot apply gets 500

text: The reason phrase of the status line of the response SHOULD contain appropriate text indicating that there has been a privacy failure as well as an enumeration of the priv-value(s) which were not supported by the privacy servic...
notes: reason phrase of that 500 names the unsupported priv-values

text: Firstly, a request for header privacy entails that the server SHOULD NOT add any headers to the message that reveal any identity or personal information, including the following: Call-Info, Server, and Organization.
notes: header privacy: no Call-Info/Server/Organization revealing the originator on the other leg

text: A privacy service SHOULD replace the value of the Contact header in a message with a URI that does not dereference to the originator of the message (such as the anonymous URI described in Section 4.1.1.3).
notes: header privacy: originator Contact replaced by an anonymous URI on the other leg

text: Note that the privacy service MUST remove any non-essential informational headers that have been added by the user agent, including the Subject, Call-Info, Organization, User-Agent, Reply-To and In-Reply-To.
notes: user privacy: Subject, Call-Info, Organization, User-Agent, Reply-To, In-Reply-To of the originator not relayed

text: Therefore, any time that a privacy service needs to modify any dialog-matching headers for privacy reasons, it SHOULD act as a transparent back-to-back user agent, and it MUST persist the former values of the dialog-matching he...
notes: identity changes are done as B2BUA; original dialog identifiers restored toward the originator

text: A valid SIP request formulated by a UAC MUST, at a minimum, contain the following header fields:
notes: outbound INVITE/OPTIONS/BYE carry To, From, CSeq, Call-ID, Max-Forwards, Via

text: The initial Request-URI of the message SHOULD be set to the value of the URI in the To field.
notes: out-of-dialog INVITE Request-URI equals the To URI

text: When a provider wishes to configure a UA with an outbound proxy, it is RECOMMENDED that this be done by providing it with a pre-existing route set with a single URI, that of the outbound proxy.
notes: the outbound_route start option preloads the proxy as a single loose Route on requests with no route of their own

text: When a pre-existing route set is present, the procedures for populating the Request-URI and Route header field detailed in Section 12.2.1.1 MUST be followed (even though there is no dialog), using the desired Request-URI as the remote target URI.
notes: with a preloaded route set, Request-URI and Route follow 12.2.1.1 (lr vs strict)

text: The To header field MAY contain a SIP or SIPS URI, but it may also make use of other URI schemes (the tel URL (RFC 2806 [9]), for example) when appropriate.
notes: UAC can send a request with a tel: URI in To

text: All SIP implementations MUST support the SIP URI scheme.
notes: sip: URIs in Request-URI/To/From/Contact parse and are routed

text: Any implementation that supports TLS MUST support the SIPS URI scheme.
notes: with TLS enabled, sips: URIs are accepted and generated

text: A request outside of a dialog MUST NOT contain a To tag; the tag in the To field of a request identifies the peer of the dialog.
notes: out-of-dialog INVITE/OPTIONS/REFER has no To tag

text: A UAC SHOULD use the display name "Anonymous", along with a syntactically correct, but otherwise meaningless URI (like sip:thisis@anonymous.invalid), if the identity of the client is to remain hidden.
notes: anonymous call has From "Anonymous" <sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid>

text: The From field MUST contain a new "tag" parameter, chosen by the UAC.
notes: every new outbound request has a fresh From tag

text: It MUST be the same for all requests and responses sent by either UA in a dialog.
notes: all requests and responses in a dialog carry the same Call-ID

text: It SHOULD be the same in each registration from a UA.
notes: repeated REGISTERs from chappe reuse one Call-ID

text: In a new request created by a UAC outside of any dialog, the Call-ID header field MUST be selected by the UAC as a globally unique identifier over space and time unless overridden by method-specific behavior.
notes: each out-of-dialog request gets a new globally unique Call-ID

text: Use of cryptographically random identifiers (RFC 1750 [12]) in the generation of Call-IDs is RECOMMENDED.
notes: Call-IDs are random and not guessable across calls

text: Implementations MAY use the form "localid@host".
notes: informative format choice for Call-ID

text: The method MUST match that of the request.
notes: CSeq method equals the request method on every request; dup: R3261-159

text: The sequence number value MUST be expressible as a 32-bit unsigned integer and MUST be less than 2**31.
notes: initial CSeq number is below 2**31

text: A UAC MUST insert a Max-Forwards header field into each request it originates with a value that SHOULD be 70.
notes: every originated request carries Max-Forwards: 70

text: When the UAC creates a request, it MUST insert a Via into that request.
notes: every outbound request has a top Via added by chappe

text: The protocol name and protocol version in the header field MUST be SIP and 2.0, respectively.
notes: Via protocol is SIP/2.0/<transport>

text: The Via header field value MUST contain a branch parameter.
notes: top Via of each request carries a branch parameter

text: The branch parameter value MUST be unique across space and time for all requests sent by the UA.
notes: branch differs across all requests sent (except CANCEL/ACK-non-2xx reuse)

text: The branch ID inserted by an element compliant with this specification MUST always begin with the characters "z9hG4bK".
notes: branch starts with z9hG4bK

text: The Contact header field MUST be present and contain exactly one SIP or SIPS URI in any request that can result in the establishment of a dialog.
notes: INVITE/SUBSCRIBE/REFER carry exactly one SIP Contact URI

text: That is, the Contact header field value contains the URI at which the UA would like to receive requests, and this URI MUST be valid even if used in subsequent requests outside of any dialogs.
notes: Contact URI in INVITE reaches chappe when used out of dialog (e.g. OPTIONS to it gets a response)

text: If the Request-URI or top Route header field value contains a SIPS URI, the Contact header field MUST contain a SIPS URI as well.
notes: INVITE to a sips: Request-URI carries a sips: Contact

text: If the UAC supports extensions to SIP that can be applied by the server to the response, the UAC SHOULD include a Supported header field in the request listing the option tags (Section 19.2) for those extensions.
notes: outbound INVITE has Supported listing 100rel, timer, replaces as enabled

text: The option tags listed MUST only refer to extensions defined in standards-track RFCs.
notes: Supported lists only standards-track option tags

text: If the UAC wishes to insist that a UAS understand an extension that the UAC will apply to the request in order to process the request, it MUST insert a Require header field into the request listing the option tag for that extension.
notes: INVITE that needs 100rel/timer carries Require with that tag

text: traversed understand that extension, it MUST insert a Proxy-Require header field into the request listing the option tag for that extension.
notes: n/a: chappe needs no proxy extension, so it never inserts Proxy-Require; an app that needs one adds it through `headers`

text: As with the Supported header field, the option tags in the Require and Proxy-Require header fields MUST only refer to extensions defined in standards-track RFCs.
notes: Require/Proxy-Require contain only standards-track option tags

text: SIP requests MAY contain a MIME-encoded message-body.
notes: requests with SDP/sipfrag/xml bodies are sent and accepted

text: Unless there is local policy specifying otherwise, the destination MUST be determined by applying the DNS procedures described in [4] as follows.
notes: request to a domain name is resolved per RFC 3263 (NAPTR/SRV/A)
