text: If the first element in the route set indicated a strict router (resulting in forming the request as described in Section 12.2.1.1), the procedures MUST be applied to the Request-URI of the request.
notes: with a strict-router first hop, RFC 3263 applies to the Request-URI

text: Independent of which URI is used as input to the procedures of [4], if the Request-URI specifies a SIPS resource, the UAC MUST follow the procedures of [4] as if the input URI were a SIPS URI.
notes: sips: Request-URI resolves as SIPS (TLS only)

text: Local policy MAY specify an alternate set of destinations to attempt.
notes: configured alternate destinations are tried

text: If the Request-URI contains a SIPS URI, any alternate destinations MUST be contacted with TLS.
notes: alternate destinations for a sips: Request-URI use TLS

text: However, that approach for configuring an outbound proxy is NOT RECOMMENDED; a pre-existing route set with a single URI SHOULD be used instead.
notes: outbound proxy configured as route set, not as forced destination

text: If the request contains a Route header field, the request SHOULD be sent to the locations derived from its topmost value, but MAY be sent to any server that the UA is certain will honor the Route and Request-URI policies specified in this document (as opposed to those in RFC 2543).
notes: request with Route is sent to the address of the top Route URI

text: In particular, a UAC configured with an outbound proxy SHOULD
notes: with outbound proxy configured, requests go to that proxy

text: The UAC SHOULD follow the procedures defined in [4] for stateful elements, trying each address until a server is contacted.
notes: on failure, next SRV/A address is tried

text: When a timeout error is received from the transaction layer, it MUST be treated as if a 408 (Request Timeout) status code has been received.
notes: INVITE to a silent peer surfaces as 408 to the application after Timer B

text: If a fatal transport error is reported by the transport layer (generally, due to fatal ICMP errors in UDP or connection failures in TCP), the condition MUST be treated as a 503 (Service Unavailable) status code.
notes: ICMP unreachable / connect failure surfaces as 503 to the application

text: A UAC MUST treat any final response it does not recognize as being equivalent to the x00 response code of that class, and MUST be able to process the x00 response code for all classes.
notes: unknown final code e.g. 499 is handled as 400 (and 299 as 200)

text: A UAC MUST treat any provisional response different than 100 that it does not recognize as 183 (Session Progress).
notes: unknown 1xx e.g. 199 is handled as 183

text: A UAC MUST be able to process 100 and 183 responses.
notes: 100 and 183 received on INVITE are processed without error

text: If more than one Via header field value is present in a response, the UAC SHOULD discard the message.
notes: nta (sofia-sip, vendored, patched at build time from c_src/sofia-patches) accepts a response carrying two Via values

text: Upon receipt of a redirection response (for example, a 301 response status code), clients SHOULD use the URI(s) in the Contact header field to formulate one or more new requests based on the redirected request.
notes: 3xx with Contact leads to a new INVITE to the Contact URI

text: As with proxy recursion, a client processing 3xx class responses MUST NOT add any given URI to the target set more than once.
notes: 3xx recursion never INVITEs the same URI twice

text: If the original request had a SIPS URI in the Request- URI, the client MAY choose to recurse to a non-SIPS URI, but SHOULD inform the user of the redirection to an insecure URI.
notes: redirect from sips: to sip: is reported to the application

text: As the target set grows, the client MAY generate new requests to the URIs in any order.
notes: 3xx targets tried in any order

text: Requests to the URIs MAY be generated serially or in parallel.
notes: 3xx targets tried serially or in parallel

text: Failures SHOULD be detected through failure response codes (codes greater than 399); for network errors the client transaction will report any transport layer failures to the transaction user.
notes: >399 on a redirected target counts as failure for that target

text: When a failure for a particular contact address is received, the client SHOULD try the next contact address.
notes: after a failed 3xx target, next Contact is tried

text: In order to create a request based on a contact address in a 3xx response, a UAC MUST copy the entire URI from the target set into the Request-URI, except for the "method-param" and "header" URI parameters (see Section 19.1.1 for a definition of these parameters).
notes: new request Request-URI is the full 3xx Contact URI minus method-param and headers

text: As a general rule, if the header field can accept a comma-separated list of values, then the new header field value MAY be appended to any existing values in the original redirected request.
notes: URI header params from 3xx Contact appended to list headers

text: If the header field does not accept multiple values, the value in the original redirected request MAY be overwritten by the header field value communicated in the contact address.
notes: URI header params from 3xx Contact overwrite single-value headers

text: It is RECOMMENDED that the UAC reuse the same To, From, and Call-ID used in the original redirected request, but the UAC MAY also choose to update the Call-ID header field value for new requests, for example.
notes: redirected request reuses To, From, Call-ID

text: Finally, once the new request has been constructed, it is sent using a new client transaction, and therefore MUST have a new branch ID in the top Via field as discussed in Section 8.1.1.7.
notes: redirected request has a new branch

text: In all other respects, requests sent upon receipt of a redirect response SHOULD re-use the header fields and bodies of the original request.
notes: redirected request reuses headers and body of the original

text: If a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response is received, the UAC SHOULD follow the authorization procedures of Section 22.2 and Section 22.3 to retry the request with credentials.
notes: 401/407 leads to retried request with Authorization/Proxy-Authorization

text: If possible, the UAC SHOULD retry the request, either omitting the body or using one of a smaller length.
notes: 413 leads to retry without body or with a smaller one

text: The UAC SHOULD retry sending the request, this time only using content with types listed in the Accept header field in the response, with encodings listed in the Accept-Encoding header field in the response, and with languages listed in the Accept-Language in the response.
notes: 415 leads to retry using Accept/Accept-Encoding/Accept-Language from the response

text: The client SHOULD retry the request, this time, using a SIP URI.
notes: 416 on a non-SIP URI leads to retry with a SIP URI

text: The UAC SHOULD retry the request, this time omitting any extensions listed in the Unsupported header field in the response.
notes: 420 leads to retry without the Unsupported option tags

text: This new request constitutes a new transaction and SHOULD have the same value of the Call-ID, To, and From of the previous request, but the CSeq should contain a new sequence number that is one higher than the previous.
notes: retry after 4xx keeps Call-ID/To/From and CSeq +1

text: If a request is accepted, all state changes associated with it MUST be performed.
notes: accepted re-INVITE/UPDATE applies the new session state

text: If it is rejected, all state changes MUST NOT be performed.
notes: rejected re-INVITE (e.g. 488) leaves the previous session unchanged

text: UASs SHOULD process the requests in the order of the steps that follow in this section (that is, starting with authentication, then inspecting the method, the header fields, and so on throughout the remainder of this section).
notes: auth checked before method and header inspection (401 precedes 405/420)

text: Once a request is authenticated (or authentication is skipped), the UAS MUST inspect the method of the request.
notes: UAS inspects method after auth (unknown method gets 501/405)

text: If the UAS recognizes but does not support the method of a request, it MUST generate a 405 (Method Not Allowed) response.
notes: known but unsupported method (e.g. PUBLISH) gets 405

text: The UAS MUST also add an Allow header field to the 405 (Method Not Allowed) response.
notes: 405 carries an Allow header

text: The Allow header field MUST list the set of methods supported by the UAS generating the message.
notes: Allow lists exactly the methods chappe supports

text: If a UAS does not understand a header field in a request (that is, the header field is not defined in this specification or in any supported extension), the server MUST ignore that header field and continue processing the message.
notes: request with an unknown header X-Foo is processed normally

text: A UAS SHOULD ignore any malformed header fields that are not necessary for processing requests.
notes: request with a malformed non-essential header still gets processed

text: A UAS MAY apply any policy it wishes to determine whether to accept requests when the To
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (To and Request-URI policy, 403/404)

text: However, it is RECOMMENDED that a UAS accept requests even if they do not recognize the URI scheme (for example, a tel:
notes: INVITE with To tel: URI is accepted

text: If, on the other hand, the UAS decides to reject the request, it SHOULD generate a response with a 403 (Forbidden) status code and pass it to the server transaction for transmission.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (To and Request-URI policy, 403/404)

text: If the Request-URI uses a scheme not supported by the UAS, it SHOULD reject the request with a 416 (Unsupported URI Scheme) response.
notes: Request-URI with unsupported scheme gets 416

text: If the Request-URI does not identify an address that the UAS is willing to accept requests for, it SHOULD reject the request with a 404 (Not Found) response.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (To and Request-URI policy, 403/404)

text: If the request has no tag in the To header field, the UAS core MUST check the request against ongoing transactions.
notes: tagless-To request is matched against pending transactions (merge detection)

text: If the From tag, Call-ID, and CSeq exactly match those associated with an ongoing transaction, but the request does not match that transaction (based on the matching rules in Section 17.2.3), the UAS core SHOULD generate a 482 (Loop Detected) response and pass it to the server transaction.
notes: forked INVITE copy with same From tag/Call-ID/CSeq, other branch gets 482

text: If a UAS does not understand an option-tag listed in a Require header field, it MUST respond by generating a response with status code 420 (Bad Extension).
notes: Require: foo gets 420

text: The UAS MUST add an Unsupported header field, and list in it those options it does not understand amongst those in the Require header field of the request.
notes: 420 carries Unsupported: foo

text: Note that Require and Proxy-Require MUST NOT be used in a SIP CANCEL request, or in an ACK request sent for a non-2xx response.
notes: CANCEL and non-2xx ACK sent by chappe carry no Require/Proxy-Require

text: These header fields MUST be ignored if they are present in these requests.
notes: CANCEL with Require: foo is not rejected with 420

text: An ACK request for a 2xx response MUST contain only those Require and Proxy-Require values that were present in the initial request.
notes: ACK for 2xx has only the Require values of the INVITE

text: If there are any bodies whose type (indicated by the Content-Type), language (indicated by the Content-Language) or encoding (indicated by the Content-Encoding) are not understood, and that body part is not optional (as indicated by the Content- Disposition header field), the UAS MUST reject the request with a 415 (Unsupported Media Type) response.
notes: INVITE with a mandatory body of unknown type gets 415

text: The response MUST contain an Accept header field listing the types of all bodies it understands, in the event the request contained bodies of types not supported by the UAS.
notes: 415 carries Accept listing supported body types

text: If the request contained content encodings not understood by the UAS, the response MUST contain an Accept-Encoding header field listing the encodings understood by the UAS.
notes: unknown Content-Encoding gives 415 with Accept-Encoding

text: If the request contained content with languages not understood by the UAS, the response MUST contain an Accept-Language header field indicating the languages understood by the UAS.
notes: n/a: chappe never rejects a request for its Content-Language (SDP has none), so it never sends this 415; an app that rejects on language adds Accept-Language itself

text: A UAS that wishes to apply some extension when generating the response MUST NOT do so unless support for that extension is indicated in the Supported header field in the request.
notes: no 100rel/timer in response unless in request Supported/Require; dup: R3261-098

text: If the desired extension is not supported, the server SHOULD rely only on baseline SIP and any other extensions supported by the client.
notes: without 100rel in Supported, UAS sends unreliable 18x

text: In rare circumstances, where the server cannot process the request without the extension, the server MAY send a 421 (Extension Required) response.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (sending 421)

text: The needed extension(s) MUST be included in a Require header field in the response.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (sending 421)

text: This behavior is NOT RECOMMENDED, as it will generally break interoperability.
notes: 421 is not sent by default configuration

text: Any extensions applied to a non-421 response MUST be listed in a Require header field included in the response.
notes: response applying 100rel/timer lists it in Require

text: One largely non-method-specific guideline for the generation of responses is that UASs SHOULD NOT issue a provisional response for a non-INVITE request.
notes: no 1xx sent for OPTIONS/BYE/REFER

text: Rather, UASs SHOULD generate a final response to a non-INVITE request as soon as possible.
notes: non-INVITE final response sent without delay

text: When a 100 (Trying) response is generated, any Timestamp header field present in the request MUST be copied into this 100 (Trying) response.
notes: 100 Trying copies Timestamp from the request

text: If there is a delay in generating the response, the UAS SHOULD add a delay value into the Timestamp value in the response.
notes: delayed response adds delay value to Timestamp

text: This value MUST contain the difference between the time of sending of the response and receipt of the request, measured in seconds.
notes: Timestamp delay is response time minus receive time in seconds

text: The From field of the response MUST equal the From header field of the request.
notes: response From equals request From

text: The Call-ID header field of the response MUST equal the Call-ID header field of the request.
notes: response Call-ID equals request Call-ID

text: The CSeq header field of the response MUST equal the CSeq field of the request.
notes: response CSeq equals request CSeq

text: The Via header field values in the response MUST equal the Via header field values in the request and MUST maintain the same ordering.
notes: response Via values equal request Via values in order

text: If a request contained a To tag in the request, the To header field in the response MUST equal that of the request.
notes: in-dialog request with To tag gets response with identical To

text: However, if the To header field in the request did not contain a tag, the URI in the To header field in the response MUST equal the URI in the To header field; additionally, the UAS MUST add a tag to the To header field in the response (with the exception of the 100 (Trying) response, in which a tag MAY be present).
notes: response to tagless request adds a To tag, same To URI

text: The same tag MUST be used for all responses to that request, both final and provisional (again excepting the 100 (Trying)).
notes: 180 and 200 to one INVITE carry the same To tag

text: o A stateless UAS MUST NOT send provisional (1xx) responses.
notes: stateless UAS role not used by chappe

text: o A stateless UAS MUST NOT retransmit responses.
notes: stateless UAS role not used by chappe

text: o A stateless UAS MUST ignore ACK requests.
notes: stateless UAS role not used by chappe

text: o A stateless UAS MUST ignore CANCEL requests.
notes: stateless UAS role not used by chappe

text: o To header tags MUST be generated for responses in a stateless manner - in a manner that will generate the same tag for the same request consistently.
notes: stateless UAS role not used by chappe

text: For well-formed CANCEL requests, it SHOULD return a 2xx response.
notes: redirect server role

text: However, redirect servers MUST NOT redirect a request to a URI equal to the one in the Request-URI; instead, provided that the URI does not point to itself, the server MAY proxy the request to the destination URI, or MAY reject it with a 404.
notes: redirect server role

text: Note that a Contact header field value MAY also refer to a different resource than the one originally called.
notes: redirect server role

text: Malformed values SHOULD be treated as equivalent to 3600.
notes: redirect server role

text: Redirect servers MUST ignore features that are not understood (including unrecognized header fields, any unknown option tags in Require, or even method names) and proceed with the redirection of the request in question.
notes: redirect server role

text: Extensions MAY define other means for creating dialogs.
notes: informative, extensions only

text: UAs MUST assign values to the dialog ID components as described below.
notes: dialog ID is Call-ID plus local and remote tags as in 12.1.1/12.1.2

text: When a UAS responds to a request with a response that establishes a dialog (such as a 2xx to INVITE), the UAS MUST copy all Record-Route header field values from the request into the response (including the URIs, URI parameters, and any Record-Route header field parameters, whether they are known or unknown to the UAS) and MUST maintain the order of those values.
notes: 200 to INVITE copies all Record-Route values in order

text: The UAS MUST add a Contact header field to the response.
notes: 200 to INVITE carries Contact

text: The URI provided in the Contact header field MUST be a SIP or SIPS URI.
notes: Contact in 200 is a sip: URI

text: SIPS URI in the Request-URI or in the top Record-Route header field value, if there was any, or the Contact header field if there was no Record-Route header field, the Contact header field in the response MUST be a SIPS URI.
notes: sips: Request-URI or top Record-Route gives a sips: Contact in 200

text: The URI SHOULD have global scope (that is, the same URI can be used in messages outside this dialog).
notes: Contact in 200 is reachable out of dialog

text: This state MUST be maintained for the duration of the dialog.
notes: dialog state is kept until BYE completes

text: The route set MUST be set to the list of URIs in the Record-Route header field from the request, taken in order and preserving all URI parameters.
notes: UAS route set is request Record-Route in order, seen as Route on its in-dialog BYE

text: If no Record-Route header field is present in the request, the route set MUST be set to the empty set.
notes: no Record-Route in INVITE gives no Route on UAS in-dialog requests

text: The remote target MUST be set to the URI from the Contact header field of the request.
notes: UAS in-dialog requests go to the INVITE Contact URI

text: The remote sequence number MUST be set to the value of the sequence number in the CSeq header field of the request.
notes: remote CSeq initialised from INVITE; lower CSeq later gets 500

text: The local sequence number MUST be empty.
notes: UAS first in-dialog request picks a fresh local CSeq

text: The call identifier component of the dialog ID MUST be set to the value of the Call-ID in the request.
notes: UAS in-dialog requests use the INVITE Call-ID

text: The local tag component of the dialog ID MUST be set to the tag in the To field in the response to the request (which always includes a tag), and the remote tag component of the dialog ID MUST be set to the tag from the From field in the request.
notes: UAS in-dialog requests have From tag = its To tag and To tag = caller From tag

text: A UAS MUST be prepared to receive a request without a tag in the From field, in which case the tag is considered to have a value of null.
notes: INVITE without From tag (RFC 2543) is accepted

text: The remote URI MUST be set to the URI in the From field, and the local URI MUST be set to the URI in the To field.
notes: UAS in-dialog requests have From URI = INVITE To URI and To URI = INVITE From URI

text: When a UAC sends a request that can establish a dialog (such as an INVITE) it MUST provide a SIP or SIPS URI with global scope (i.e., the same SIP URI can be used in messages outside this dialog) in the Contact header field of the request.
notes: INVITE Contact is a globally reachable sip: URI

text: The route set MUST be set to the list of URIs in the Record-Route header field from the response, taken in reverse order and preserving all URI parameters.
notes: UAC route set is 2xx Record-Route reversed, seen as Route on ACK/BYE

text: If no Record-Route header field is present in the response, the route set MUST be set to the empty set.
notes: no Record-Route in 2xx gives no Route on ACK/BYE

text: The remote target MUST be set to the URI from the Contact header field of the response.
notes: ACK/BYE Request-URI is the 2xx Contact URI

text: The local sequence number MUST be set to the value of the sequence number in the CSeq header field of the request.
notes: next in-dialog request CSeq is INVITE CSeq + 1

text: The remote sequence number MUST be empty (it is established when the remote UA sends a request within the dialog).
notes: UAC accepts any CSeq on the first request from the peer

text: The local tag component of the dialog ID MUST be set to the tag in the From field in the request, and the remote tag component of the dialog ID MUST be set to the tag in the To field of the response.
notes: UAC in-dialog requests have From tag = its tag and To tag = 2xx To tag

text: A UAC MUST be prepared to receive a response without a tag in the To field, in which case the tag is considered to have a value of null.
notes: 2xx without To tag is accepted and dialog formed with null remote tag

text: The remote URI MUST be set to the URI in the To field, and the local URI MUST be set to the URI in the From field.
notes: UAC in-dialog requests use the original To/From URIs

text: Once a dialog has been established between two UAs, either of them MAY initiate new transactions as needed within the dialog.
notes: either side can send re-INVITE/BYE/REFER in the dialog

text: Requests within a dialog MAY contain Record-Route and Contact header fields.
notes: in-dialog requests with Contact/Record-Route are accepted

text: The URI in the To field of the request MUST be set to the remote URI from the dialog state.
notes: in-dialog request To URI is the dialog remote URI

text: The tag in the To header field of the request MUST be set to the remote tag of the dialog ID.
notes: in-dialog request To tag is the dialog remote tag

text: The From URI of the request MUST be set to the local URI from the dialog state.
notes: in-dialog request From URI is the dialog local URI

text: The tag in the From header field of the request MUST be set to the local tag of the dialog ID.
notes: in-dialog request From tag is the dialog local tag

text: If the value of the remote or local tags is null, the tag parameter MUST be omitted from the To or From header fields, respectively.
notes: null tag in dialog state gives no tag parameter

text: The Call-ID of the request MUST be set to the Call-ID of the dialog.
notes: in-dialog request Call-ID equals the dialog Call-ID

text: Requests within a dialog MUST contain strictly monotonically increasing and contiguous CSeq sequence numbers (increasing-by-one) in each direction (excepting ACK and CANCEL of course, whose numbers equal the requests being acknowledged or cancelled).
notes: in-dialog CSeq increases by one per request in each direction; dup: R3261-157

text: If the local sequence number is empty, an initial value MUST be chosen using the guidelines of Section 8.1.1.5.
notes: UAS-side first in-dialog request picks a CSeq below 2**31

text: If the route set is empty, the UAC MUST place the remote target URI into the Request-URI.
notes: empty route set gives Request-URI = remote target

text: The UAC MUST NOT add a Route header field to the request.
notes: empty route set gives no Route header

text: If the route set is not empty, and the first URI in the route set contains the lr parameter (see Section 19.1.1), the UAC MUST place the remote target URI into the Request-URI and MUST include a Route header field containing the route set values in order, including all parameters.
notes: loose-routing first hop gives Request-URI = remote target and Route = route set

text: If the route set is not empty, and its first URI does not contain the lr parameter, the UAC MUST place the first URI from the route set into the Request-URI, stripping any parameters that are not allowed in a Request-URI.
notes: strict-router first hop becomes the Request-URI minus disallowed params

text: The UAC MUST add a Route header field containing the remainder of the route set values in order, including all parameters.
notes: strict routing: Route holds remaining route set in order

text: The UAC MUST then place the remote target URI into the Route header field as the last value.
notes: strict routing: remote target is the last Route value

text: A UAC SHOULD include a Contact header field in any target refresh requests within a dialog, and unless there is a need to change it, the URI SHOULD be the same as used in previous requests within the dialog.
notes: re-INVITE/UPDATE carry the same Contact as earlier

text: If the "secure" flag is true, that URI MUST be a SIPS URI.
notes: secure dialog gives sips: Contact on target refresh

text: When a UAC receives a 2xx response to a target refresh request, it MUST replace the dialog's remote target URI with the URI from the Contact header field in that response, if present.
notes: 2xx to re-INVITE with new Contact changes the Request-URI of later BYE

text: If the response for a request within a dialog is a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) or a 408 (Request Timeout), the UAC SHOULD terminate the dialog.
notes: 481 or 408 to in-dialog request ends the dialog

text: A UAC SHOULD also terminate a dialog if no response at all is received for the request (the client transaction would inform the TU about the timeout.)
notes: in-dialog request timing out ends the dialog

text: Based on the To tag, the UAS MAY either accept or reject the request.
notes: request with unknown To tag after UAS restart is accepted or rejected (481); no crash

text: If the UAS wishes to reject the request because it does not wish to recreate the dialog, it MUST respond to the request with a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) status code and pass that to the server transaction.
notes: in-dialog request with unknown To tag rejected with 481

text: If the remote sequence number is empty, it MUST be set to the value of the sequence number in the CSeq header field value in the request.
notes: first in-dialog request from peer sets remote CSeq; later request with that CSeq+1 accepted

text: If the remote sequence number was not empty, but the sequence number of the request is lower than the remote sequence number, the request is out of order and MUST be rejected with a 500 (Server Internal Error) response.
notes: in-dialog request with CSeq lower than last seen gets 500

text: This is not an error condition, and a UAS SHOULD be prepared to receive and process requests with CSeq values more than one higher than the previous received request.
notes: in-dialog request with CSeq jumping by more than one gets 2xx, not an error

text: The UAS MUST then set the remote sequence number to the value of the sequence number in the CSeq header field value in the request.
notes: after in-dialog request, a request with a lower CSeq than it gets 500

text: When a UAS receives a target refresh request, it MUST replace the dialog's remote target URI with the URI from the Contact header field in that request, if present.
notes: re-INVITE with new Contact; next in-dialog request from chappe uses new Contact as Request-URI

text: A UA that supports INVITE MUST also support ACK, CANCEL and BYE.
notes: UA handling INVITE also answers ACK, CANCEL and BYE (no 405/501)

text: An Allow header field (Section 20.5) SHOULD be present in the INVITE.
notes: INVITE sent by chappe carries Allow header

text: For example, a UA capable of receiving INFO requests within a dialog [34] SHOULD include an Allow header field listing the INFO method.
notes: Allow on INVITE lists every in-dialog method chappe accepts (e.g. INFO, REFER, UPDATE)

text: A Supported header field (Section 20.37) SHOULD be present in the INVITE.
notes: INVITE sent by chappe carries Supported header

text: An Accept (Section 20.1) header field MAY be present in the INVITE.
notes: optional: INVITE may carry Accept listing application/sdp

text: The UAC MAY add an Expires header field (Section 20.19) to limit the validity of the invitation.
notes: optional: outgoing INVITE may carry Expires when configured

text: If the time indicated in the Expires header field is reached and no final answer for the INVITE has been received, the UAC core SHOULD generate a CANCEL request for the INVITE, as per Section 9.
notes: INVITE with Expires and no final answer by expiry is followed by CANCEL

text: A UAC MAY also find it useful to add, among others, Subject (Section 20.36), Organization (Section 20.25) and User-Agent (Section 20.41) header fields.
notes: optional: INVITE may carry Subject/Organization/User-Agent when configured

text: The UAC MAY choose to add a message body to the INVITE.
notes: INVITE with or without SDP body both supported (offerless INVITE)

text: o The initial offer MUST be in either an INVITE or, if not there, in the first reliable non-failure message from the UAS back to the UAC.
notes: initial offer appears in INVITE or in the first reliable non-failure response (200 or reliable 18x)

text: o If the initial offer is in an INVITE, the answer MUST be in a reliable non-failure message from UAS back to UAC which is correlated to that INVITE.
notes: INVITE with SDP offer gets answer in 200 (or reliable 18x)

text: That same exact answer MAY also be placed in any provisional responses sent prior to the answer.
notes: 183 before 200 may carry the same SDP answer as the 200

text: The UAC MUST treat the first session description it receives as the answer, and MUST ignore any session descriptions in subsequent responses to the initial INVITE.
notes: UAC uses first SDP received (e.g. 183) as answer; different SDP in later 200 ignored

text: o If the initial offer is in the first reliable non-failure message from the UAS back to UAC, the answer MUST be in the acknowledgement for that message (in this specification, ACK for a 2xx response).
notes: offerless INVITE: 200 carries offer and chappe ACK carries the answer

text: o After having sent or received an answer to the first offer, the UAC MAY generate subsequent offers in requests based on rules specified for that method, but only if it has received answers to any previous offers, and has not sent any offers to which it hasn't gotten an answer.
notes: chappe sends no new offer (re-INVITE/UPDATE) while a previous offer is unanswered

text: o Once the UAS has sent or received an answer to the initial offer, it MUST NOT generate subsequent offers in any responses to the initial INVITE.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (SDP bodies the app puts on 18x)

text: All user agents that support INVITE MUST support these two exchanges.
notes: both offer-in-INVITE and offer-in-200/answer-in-ACK exchanges succeed

text: The Session Description Protocol (SDP) (RFC 2327 [1]) MUST be supported by all user agents as a means to describe sessions, and its usage for constructing offers and answers MUST follow the procedures defined in [13].
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (SDP validity of app-built bodies)

text: Depending on the status code of the 3xx response (see Section 21.3), the UAC MAY choose to try those new addresses.
notes: 3xx with Contact may be retried to new targets when enabled

text: Subsequent final responses (which would only arrive under error conditions) MUST be ignored.
notes: second final response to an INVITE (after first final) is ignored, no state change

text: If the dialog identifier in the 2xx response matches the dialog identifier of an existing dialog, the dialog MUST be transitioned to the "confirmed" state, and the route set for the dialog MUST be recomputed based on the 2xx response using the procedures of Section 12.2.1.2.
notes: 200 matching an early dialog confirms it; route set taken from the 200 Record-Route

text: Otherwise, a new dialog in the "confirmed" state MUST be constructed using the procedures of Section 12.1.2.
notes: 200 with a new To tag (forked) creates a new confirmed dialog

text: The UAC core MUST generate an ACK request for each 2xx received from the transaction layer.
notes: each 2xx to INVITE (incl. per forked To tag) gets an ACK

text: The sequence number of the CSeq header field MUST be the same as the INVITE being acknowledged, but the CSeq method MUST be ACK.
notes: ACK for 2xx has INVITE CSeq number and method ACK

text: The ACK MUST contain the same credentials as the INVITE.
notes: ACK after authenticated INVITE carries the same Authorization credentials

text: If the 2xx contains an offer (based on the rules above), the ACK MUST carry an answer in its body.
notes: offerless INVITE: ACK to 200 with offer carries SDP answer

text: If the offer in the 2xx response is not acceptable, the UAC core MUST generate a valid answer in the ACK and then send a BYE immediately.
notes: unacceptable offer in 200: ACK with valid answer then BYE sent

text: The ACK MUST be passed to the client transport every time a retransmission of the 2xx final response that triggered the ACK arrives.
notes: retransmitted 200 to INVITE triggers retransmitted ACK

text: If, after acknowledging any 2xx response to an INVITE, the UAC does not want to continue with that dialog, then the UAC MUST terminate the dialog by sending a BYE request as described in Section 15.
notes: unwanted 2xx dialog (e.g. extra fork) is ACKed then BYEd

text: If the invitation expires before the UAS has generated a final response, a 487 (Request Terminated) response SHOULD be generated.
notes: INVITE with Expires unanswered by expiry gets 487

text: If desired, the UAS MAY use identifiers within the session description to detect this duplication.
notes: optional detection of duplicate invitations; no observable duty

text: If the user is already a member of the session, and the session parameters contained in the session description have not changed, the UAS MAY silently accept the INVITE (that is, send a 2xx response without prompting the user).
notes: optional silent accept; application policy

text: It MUST provide the offer in its first non-failure reliable message back to the UAC.
notes: offerless INVITE: offer appears in first reliable non-failure response (200 or reliable 18x)

text: A UAS MAY send as many provisional responses as it likes.
notes: UAS can send several provisionals (180, 183) before final

text: Each of these MUST indicate the same dialog ID.
notes: all provisionals and final for one INVITE carry the same To tag

text: To prevent cancellation, the UAS MUST send a non-100 provisional response at every minute, to handle the possibility of lost provisional responses.
notes: INVITE left ringing over a minute gets a repeated non-100 provisional each minute

text: A 300 (Multiple Choices), 301 (Moved Permanently) or 302 (Moved Temporarily) response SHOULD contain a Contact header field
notes: redirect server role

text: A 486 (Busy Here) SHOULD be returned in such a scenario.
notes: busy application reject yields 486

text: If the UAS knows that no other end system will be able to accept this call, a 600 (Busy Everywhere) response SHOULD be sent instead.
notes: application can reject with 600 Busy Everywhere

text: A UAS rejecting an offer contained in an INVITE SHOULD return a 488 (Not Acceptable Here) response.
notes: application duty: chappe_sip passes it to the app, which decides (codec matching, 488)

text: Such a response SHOULD include a Warning header field value explaining why the offer was rejected.
notes: 488 carries a Warning header explaining the rejection

text: A 2xx response to an INVITE SHOULD contain the Allow header field and the Supported header field, and MAY contain the Accept header field.
notes: 200 to INVITE carries Allow and Supported

text: If the INVITE request contained an offer, and the UAS had not yet sent an answer, the 2xx MUST contain an answer.
notes: INVITE with offer and no prior answer: 200 carries SDP answer

text: If the INVITE did not contain an offer, the 2xx MUST contain an offer if the UAS had not yet sent an offer.
notes: offerless INVITE with no prior offer: 200 carries SDP offer

text: If the server retransmits the 2xx response for 64*T1 seconds without receiving an ACK, the dialog is confirmed, but the session SHOULD be terminated.
notes: 200 retransmitted 64*T1 with no ACK: chappe sends BYE

text: However, automated generation of re-INVITE or BYE is NOT RECOMMENDED to avoid flooding the network with traffic when there is congestion.
notes: no automatic re-INVITE/BYE storm on error without randomization

text: In any case, if these messages are sent automatically, they SHOULD be sent after some randomized interval.
notes: automatic re-INVITE/BYE are sent after a randomized delay

text: Of course, a UAC MAY
notes: re-INVITE without SDP gets offer in 200, answered in ACK

text: If the session description format has the capability for version numbers, the offerer SHOULD indicate that the version of the session description has changed.
notes: re-offer increments SDP o= version

text: A UAC MAY choose not to add an Alert-Info header field or a body with Content-Disposition "alert" to re-INVITEs because UASs do not typically alert the user upon reception of a re-INVITE.
notes: optional omission of Alert-Info; no duty

text: Note that a UAC MUST NOT initiate a new INVITE transaction within a dialog while another INVITE transaction is in progress in either direction.
notes: no second re-INVITE sent while an INVITE transaction is pending in either direction

text: If there is an ongoing INVITE client transaction, the TU MUST wait until the transaction reaches the completed or terminated state before initiating the new INVITE.
notes: re-INVITE held until prior INVITE client transaction completes

text: If there is an ongoing INVITE server transaction, the TU MUST wait until the transaction reaches the confirmed or terminated state before initiating the new INVITE.
notes: re-INVITE held until received INVITE server transaction gets its ACK

text: However, a UA MAY initiate a regular transaction while an INVITE transaction is in progress.
notes: BYE/OPTIONS/INFO can be sent while an INVITE is pending on the dialog

text: A UA MAY also initiate an INVITE transaction while a regular transaction is in progress.
notes: re-INVITE can be sent while a non-INVITE transaction is pending

text: If a UA receives a non-2xx final response to a re-INVITE, the session parameters MUST remain unchanged, as if no re-INVITE had been issued.
notes: re-INVITE rejected (e.g. 488) leaves prior SDP/media unchanged

text: If a UAC receives a 491 response to a re-INVITE, it SHOULD start a timer with a value T chosen as follows:
notes: 491 to re-INVITE starts randomized retry timer per role (2.1-4 s or 0-2 s)

text: When the timer fires, the UAC SHOULD attempt the re-INVITE once more, if it still desires for that session modification to take place.
notes: after 491 and timer, re-INVITE is retried once

text: A UAS that receives a second INVITE before it sends the final response to a first INVITE with a lower CSeq sequence number on the same dialog MUST return a 500 (Server Internal Error) response to the second INVITE and MUST include a Retry-After header field with a randomly chosen value of between 0 and 10 seconds.
notes: second INVITE before final to first gets 500 with Retry-After 0-10

text: A UAS that receives an INVITE on a dialog while an INVITE it had sent on that dialog is in progress MUST return a 491 (Request Pending) response to the received INVITE.
notes: re-INVITE glare: incoming INVITE while own INVITE pending gets 491

text: If a UA receives a re-INVITE for an existing dialog, it MUST check any version identifiers in the session description or, if there are no version identifiers, the content of the session description to see if it has changed.
notes: re-INVITE with unchanged SDP (same o= version) causes no media change

text: If the session description has changed, the UAS MUST adjust the session parameters accordingly, possibly after asking the user for confirmation.
notes: re-INVITE with changed SDP (e.g. sendonly hold) updates media and answer

text: This response SHOULD include a Warning header field.
notes: 488 to unacceptable re-INVITE carries a Warning header

text: If a UAS generates a 2xx response and never receives an ACK, it SHOULD generate a BYE to terminate the dialog.
notes: 200 never ACKed: chappe sends BYE on the dialog

text: A UAS MAY choose not to generate 180 (Ringing) responses for a re- INVITE because UACs do not typically render this information to the user.
notes: re-INVITE answered directly with 200 without 180

text: For the same reason, UASs MAY choose not to use an Alert-Info header field or a body with Content-Disposition "alert" in responses to a re-INVITE.
notes: optional omission of Alert-Info; no duty

text: A UAS providing an offer in a 2xx (because the INVITE did not contain an offer) SHOULD construct the offer as if the UAS were making a brand new call, subject to the constraints of sending an offer that updates an existing session, as described in [13] in the case of SDP.
notes: offerless re-INVITE: 200 carries full offer like a new call

text: Specifically, this means that it SHOULD include as many media formats and media types that the UA is willing to support.
notes: offer in 200 to offerless re-INVITE lists all supported codecs

text: The UAS MUST ensure that the session description overlaps with its previous session description in media formats, transports, or other parameters that require support from the peer.
notes: offer in 200 to offerless re-INVITE overlaps previous SDP (same m-lines/codecs subset)

text: If, however, it is unacceptable to the UAC, the UAC SHOULD generate an answer with a valid session description, and then send a BYE to terminate the session.
notes: unacceptable offer in re-INVITE 200: ACK with valid answer then BYE

text: When a BYE is received on a dialog, any session associated with that dialog SHOULD terminate.
notes: incoming BYE stops media on the session

text: A UA MUST NOT send a BYE outside of a dialog.
notes: chappe never sends BYE outside a dialog

text: The caller's UA MAY send a BYE for either confirmed or early dialogs, and the callee's UA MAY send a BYE on confirmed dialogs, but MUST NOT send a BYE on early dialogs.
notes: callee side sends no BYE on an early dialog (uses final error instead)

text: However, the callee's UA MUST NOT send a BYE on a confirmed dialog until it has received an ACK for its 2xx response or until the server transaction times out.
notes: callee BYE deferred until ACK received or 200 retransmission times out

text: The UAC MAY continue with the sessions established by any 2xx responses, or MAY terminate them with BYE.
notes: extra forked 2xx dialogs kept or BYEd per application

text: The UAC MUST consider the session terminated (and therefore stop sending or listening for media) as soon as the BYE request is passed to the client transaction.
notes: after sending BYE, media stops immediately

text: response at all is received for the BYE (that is, a timeout is returned by the client transaction), the UAC MUST consider the session and the dialog terminated.
notes: BYE timing out (no response) still ends the dialog

text: If the BYE does not match an existing dialog, the UAS core SHOULD generate a 481 (Call/Transaction Does Not Exist) response and pass that to the server transaction.
notes: BYE with no matching dialog gets 481

text: A UAS core receiving a BYE request for an existing dialog MUST follow the procedures of Section 12.2.2 to process the request.
notes: in-dialog BYE checks CSeq/dialog rules (lower CSeq gets 500)

text: Once done, the UAS SHOULD terminate the session (and therefore stop sending and listening for media).
notes: after BYE 200, media stops

text: Whether or not it ends its participation on the session, the UAS core MUST generate a 2xx response to the BYE, and MUST pass that to the server transaction for transmission.
notes: BYE on an existing dialog gets 200

text: The UAS MUST still respond to any pending requests received for that dialog.
notes: pending in-dialog requests get a final response when BYE arrives

text: It is RECOMMENDED that a 487 (Request Terminated) response be generated to those pending requests.
notes: pending INVITE/re-INVITE gets 487 when BYE arrives

text: Because of the non-INVITE transaction's reliance on a two-way handshake, TUs SHOULD respond immediately to non-INVITE requests.
notes: non-INVITE requests (BYE, OPTIONS, NOTIFY) answered promptly, before Timer E retransmits

text: The initial state, "calling", MUST be entered when the TU initiates a new client transaction with an INVITE request.
notes: INVITE client transaction starts in calling state

text: The client transaction MUST pass the request to the transport layer for transmission (see Section 18).
notes: INVITE is sent on the wire by the client transaction

text: If an unreliable transport is being used, the client transaction MUST start timer A with a value of T1.
notes: an INVITE over UDP with T1 = 100 ms is first sent again after about T1; nta floored Timer A at 1000 ms until sofia patch 0005 (c_src/sofia-patches)

text: If a reliable transport is being used, the client transaction SHOULD NOT start timer A (Timer A controls request retransmissions).
notes: TCP INVITE is not retransmitted

text: For any transport, the client transaction MUST start timer B with a value of 64*T1 seconds (Timer B controls transaction timeouts).
notes: INVITE unanswered for 64*T1 times out (408 to TU)

text: When timer A fires, the client transaction MUST retransmit the request by passing it to the transport layer, and MUST reset the timer with a value of 2*T1.
notes: UDP INVITE retransmits at doubling intervals 0.5,1,2,4 s; dup: R3261-268

text: This process MUST continue so that the request is retransmitted with intervals that double after each transmission.
notes: INVITE retransmission intervals keep doubling until Timer B

text: These retransmissions SHOULD only be done while the client transaction is in the "calling" state.
notes: INVITE retransmissions stop after a provisional arrives

text: Elements MAY (though it is NOT RECOMMENDED) use smaller values of T1 within closed, private networks that do not permit general Internet connection.
notes: T1 default stays 500 ms unless configured

text: T1 MAY be chosen larger, and this is RECOMMENDED if it is known in advance (such as on high latency access links) that the RTT is larger.
notes: T1 configurable larger for high latency links

text: Whatever the value of T1, the exponential backoffs on retransmissions described in this section MUST be used.
notes: with any configured T1, retransmission intervals double

text: If the client transaction is still in the "Calling" state when timer B fires, the client transaction SHOULD inform the TU that a timeout has occurred.
notes: Timer B expiry reports timeout to application (408)

text: The client transaction MUST NOT generate an ACK.
notes: client transaction sends no ACK for 2xx (UAC core does)

text: In the "Proceeding" state, the client transaction SHOULD NOT retransmit the request any longer.
notes: no INVITE retransmission after 1xx received

text: Furthermore, the provisional response MUST be passed to the TU.
notes: provisional response reaches the application

text: Any further provisional responses MUST be passed up to the TU while in the "Proceeding" state.
notes: each further provisional (180 then 183) reaches the application

text: When in either the "Calling" or "Proceeding" states, reception of a response with status code from 300-699 MUST cause the client transaction to transition to "Completed".
notes: 3xx-6xx to INVITE moves client transaction to completed

text: The client transaction MUST pass the received response up to the TU, and the client transaction MUST generate an ACK request, even if the transport is reliable (guidelines for constructing the ACK from the response are given in Section 17.1.1.3) and then pass the ACK to the transport layer for transmission.
notes: 3xx-6xx to INVITE is ACKed by the transaction, over UDP and TCP

text: The ACK MUST be sent to the same address, port, and transport to which the original request was sent.
notes: ACK for non-2xx goes to the same address, port and transport as the INVITE

text: The client transaction SHOULD start timer D when it enters the "Completed" state, with a value of at least 32 seconds for unreliable transports, and a value of zero seconds for reliable transports.
notes: Timer D at least 32 s over UDP absorbs final response retransmissions

text: Any retransmissions of the final response that are received while in the "Completed" state MUST cause the ACK to be re-passed to the transport layer for retransmission, but the newly received response MUST NOT be passed up to the TU.
notes: retransmitted 4xx gets ACK resent; application not notified twice

text: If timer D fires while the client transaction is in the "Completed" state, the client transaction MUST move to the terminated state.
notes: client transaction terminates when Timer D fires

text: When in either the "Calling" or "Proceeding" states, reception of a 2xx response MUST cause the client transaction to enter the "Terminated" state, and the response MUST be passed up to the TU.
notes: 2xx to INVITE terminates client transaction and reaches the application

text: The client transaction MUST be destroyed the instant it enters the "Terminated" state.
