text: Clients MAY apply content encodings to the body in requests.
notes: optional: request bodies may be content-encoded

text: A server MAY apply content encodings to the bodies in responses.
notes: optional: response bodies may be content-encoded

text: The server MUST only use encodings listed in the Accept-Encoding header field in the request.
notes: response body encoding is always one listed in the request Accept-Encoding

text: Applications SHOULD use this field to indicate the size of the message-body to be transferred, regardless of the media type of the entity.
notes: every sent UDP message carries Content-Length equal to the body size

text: If a stream-based protocol (such as TCP) is used as transport, the header field MUST be used.
notes: every message sent over TCP/TLS carries Content-Length (WS frames delimit messages; Content-Length optional there, see ws_transport)

text: If no body is present in a message, then the Content-Length header field value MUST be set to zero.
notes: body-less messages are sent with Content-Length: 0

text: The Content-Type header field MUST be present if the body is not empty.
notes: every message with a body carries Content-Type

text: The sequence number MUST be expressible as a 32-bit unsigned integer.
notes: CSeq up to 2^32-1 is accepted; larger is rejected with 400

text: A UAC MAY treat a SIP or SIPS URI in an Error-Info header field as if it were a Contact in a redirect and generate a new INVITE, resulting in a recorded announcement session being established.
notes: optional announcement behaviour, product policy

text: A non-SIP URI MAY be rendered to the user.
notes: rendering to a user

text: A system SHOULD use the display name "Anonymous" if the identity of the client is to remain hidden.
notes: anonymous outbound call has From display name Anonymous

text: The field MAY be used by client software to filter calls.
notes: client filtering policy

text: For these decisions, a message containing no Priority header field SHOULD be treated as if it specified a Priority of "normal".
notes: request without Priority is handled as normal

text: It is RECOMMENDED that the value of "emergency" only be used when life, limb, or property are in imminent danger.
notes: usage guidance for the calling user

text: For example, the URI MAY be used to return missed calls or unestablished sessions.
notes: descriptive use of Reply-To

text: If the user wished to remain anonymous, the header field SHOULD either be omitted from the request or populated in such a way that does not reveal any private information.
notes: anonymous outbound request carries no Reply-To revealing identity

text: Although an optional header field, the Require MUST NOT be ignored if it is present.
notes: INVITE with Require: foo (unknown) gets 420 with Unsupported: foo; dup: R3261-456, R3261-492

text: A UAC compliant to this specification MUST only include option tags corresponding to standards-track RFCs.
notes: Require/Supported sent carry only standards-track tags (100rel, timer, replaces, norefersub, tdialog); dup: R3261-459

text: Implementers SHOULD make the Server header field a configurable option.
notes: Server header value is configurable or omitted

text: Implementers SHOULD make the User-Agent header field a configurable option.
notes: User-Agent header value is configurable or omitted

text: For implementations compliant to this specification, the value of the branch parameter MUST start with the magic cookie "z9hG4bK", as discussed in Section 8.1.1.7.
notes: every Via branch generated starts with z9hG4bK

text: A system receiving this warning MUST NOT take any automated action.
notes: response with a Warning header gets no automated action beyond normal status handling

text: Other HTTP/1.1 response codes SHOULD NOT be used.
notes: chappe only sends status codes defined for SIP

text: Provisional (1xx) responses MAY contain message bodies, including session descriptions.
notes: 183 with SDP is sent as early media and the UAC plays it

text: This response MAY be used to initiate local ringback.
notes: 180 without SDP triggers local ringback on the UAC side

text: A server MAY use this status code to indicate that the call is being forwarded to a different set of destinations.
notes: optional: 181 sent when the call is forwarded

text: The reason phrase MAY give further details about the status of the call, for example, "5 calls queued; expected waiting time is 15 minutes".
notes: optional: 182 reason phrase carries queue detail

text: The server MAY issue several 182 (Queued) responses to update the caller about the status of the queued call.
notes: optional: repeated 182 responses while queued

text: The Reason-Phrase, header fields, or message body MAY be used to convey more details about the call progress.
notes: 183 reason phrase or body conveys progress, UAC accepts it

text: The response MAY include a message body containing a list of resource characteristics and location(s) from which the user or UA can choose the one most appropriate, if allowed by the Accept request header field.
notes: redirect server role

text: The choices SHOULD also be listed as Contact fields (Section 20.10).
notes: redirect server role

text: Unlike HTTP, the SIP response MAY contain several Contact fields or a list of addresses in a Contact field.
notes: 3xx with several Contacts is parsed without error

text: UAs MAY use the Contact header field value for automatic redirection or MAY ask the user to confirm a choice.
notes: 3xx Contact may be followed automatically by the UAC

text: The user can no longer be found at the address in the Request-URI, and the requesting client SHOULD retry at the new address given by the Contact header field (Section 20.10).
notes: 301 makes the UAC retry the INVITE at the Contact

text: The requestor SHOULD update any local directories, address books, and user location caches with this new value and redirect future requests to the address(es) listed.
notes: address-book caching is user-agent product policy

text: The requesting client SHOULD retry the request at the new address(es) given by the Contact header field (Section 20.10).
notes: 302 makes the UAC retry the INVITE at the Contact

text: Both proxies and UAs MAY cache this URI for the duration of the expiration time.
notes: optional cache, product policy

text: If there is no explicit expiration time, the address is only valid once for recursing, and MUST NOT be cached for future transactions.
notes: 302 Contact without expires is not reused for a later call

text: If the URI cached from the Contact header field fails, the Request- URI from the redirected request MAY be tried again a single time.
notes: optional retry of cached target, product policy

text: The requested resource MUST be accessed through the proxy given by the Contact field.
notes: 305 makes the UAC resend the request via the Contact proxy

text: The recipient is expected to repeat this single request via the proxy. 305 (Use Proxy) responses MUST only be generated by UASs.
notes: n/a, holds by construction: chappe never generates 305 (the proxy only relays a downstream 3xx); a UAS handler sending one is the app's choice

text: The client SHOULD NOT retry the same request without modification (for example, adding appropriate authorization).
notes: 4xx final response is not retried unchanged (only 401/407 with credentials)

text: The Reason-Phrase SHOULD identify the syntax problem in more detail, for example, "Missing Call-ID header field".
notes: 400 reason phrase names the syntax problem

text: Authorization will not help, and the request SHOULD NOT be repeated.
notes: 403 is not retried

text: The response MUST include an Allow header field containing a list of valid methods for the indicated address.
notes: 405 response carries Allow listing supported methods

text: This code is similar to 401 (Unauthorized), but indicates that the client MUST first authenticate itself with the proxy.
notes: 407 makes the UAC resend with Proxy-Authorization

text: The client MAY repeat the request without modifications at any later time.
notes: request that got 408 may be resent later unchanged

text: If the server does not know, or has no facility to determine, whether or not the condition is permanent, the status code 404 (Not Found) SHOULD be used instead.
notes: 410 only used when permanence is known, else 404

text: The server MAY close the connection to prevent the client from continuing the request.
notes: oversized request over TCP gets 413 and the connection may close

text: If the condition is temporary, the server SHOULD include a Retry- After header field to indicate that it is temporary and after what time the client MAY try again.
notes: 413/other temporary refusal carries Retry-After

text: The server MUST return a list of acceptable formats using the Accept, Accept-Encoding, or Accept-Language header field, depending on the specific problem with the content.
notes: 415 carries Accept (or Accept-Encoding/Language) listing supported formats

text: Responses with this status code MUST contain a Require header field listing the required extensions.
notes: n/a: duplicate of R3261-095; application duty: chappe_sip never sends 421 itself, an app that does adds Require

text: A UAS SHOULD NOT use this response unless it truly cannot provide any useful service to the client.
notes: 421 is not sent when baseline service is possible

text: Instead, if a desirable extension is not listed in the Supported header field, servers SHOULD process the request using baseline SIP capabilities and any extensions supported by the client.
notes: INVITE without Supported: 100rel/timer is still answered using baseline SIP

text: The response MAY indicate a better time to call in the Retry-After header field.
notes: 480/486 may carry Retry-After

text: The reason phrase SHOULD indicate a more precise cause as to why the callee is unavailable.
notes: 480 reason phrase gives a more precise cause

text: This value SHOULD be settable by the UA.
notes: 480 reason phrase is settable through the API

text: Status 486 (Busy Here) MAY be used to more precisely indicate a particular reason for the call failure.
notes: busy callee rejects with 486

text: Additional information SHOULD be provided in the reason phrase.
notes: 482/483 reason phrase carries extra detail

text: The response MAY contain a listing of possible unambiguous addresses in Contact header fields.
notes: 485 lists choices, proxy or registrar role

text: It MUST be possible to configure a server to respond with status 404 (Not Found) or to suppress the listing of possible choices for ambiguous Request-URIs.
notes: 485 listing policy of a location server

text: Status 600 (Busy Everywhere) SHOULD be used if the client knows that no other end system will be able to accept this call.
notes: 600 used only when no other endpoint can accept

text: A message body containing a description of media capabilities MAY be present in the response, which is formatted according to the Accept header field in the INVITE (or application/sdp if not present), the same as a message body in a 200 (OK) response to an OPTIONS request.
notes: 488/606 may carry an SDP capability body

text: This response MAY have a single body containing an appropriate public key that should be used to encrypt MIME bodies sent to this UA.
notes: 493 may carry a public key body (S/MIME)

text: The client MAY display the specific error condition and MAY retry the request after several seconds.
notes: user display and retry policy

text: If the condition is temporary, the server MAY indicate when the client may retry the request using the Retry-After header field.
notes: 500 may carry Retry-After

text: The server MAY indicate when the client should retry the request in a Retry-After header field.
notes: 503 may carry Retry-After

text: If no Retry-After is given, the client MUST act as if it had received a 500 (Server Internal Error) response.
notes: 503 without Retry-After is handled like 500

text: A client (proxy or UAC) receiving a 503 (Service Unavailable) SHOULD attempt to forward the request to an alternate server.
notes: UAC with RFC 3263 alternates retries the request on another server after 503

text: It SHOULD NOT forward any other requests to that server for the duration specified in the Retry-After header field, if present.
notes: server that sent 503 with Retry-After is avoided for that duration

text: Servers MAY refuse the connection or drop the request instead of responding with 503 (Service Unavailable).
notes: overloaded server may drop requests instead of 503

text: The 606 (Not Acceptable) response MAY contain a list of reasons in a Warning header field describing why the session described cannot be supported.
notes: 606 may carry Warning with reasons

text: The offer (and answer) MUST be a valid SDP message, as defined by RFC 2327 [1], with one exception.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: This specification relaxes that constraint; an SDP formulated for an offer/answer application MAY omit both the e and p lines.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The numeric value of the session id and version in the o line MUST be representable with a 64 bit signed integer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The initial value of the version MUST be less than (2**62)-1, to avoid rollovers.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Although the SDP specification allows for multiple session descriptions to be concatenated together into a large SDP message, an SDP message used in the offer/answer model MUST contain exactly one session description.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For unicast sessions, it is RECOMMENDED that it consist of a single space character (0x20) or a dash (-).
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In that case, the "t=" line SHOULD have a value of "0 0".
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The streams MAY be for a mix of unicast and multicast; the latter obviously implies a multicast address in the relevant "c=" line(s).
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the offerer wishes to only send media on a stream to its peer, it MUST mark the stream as sendonly with the "a=sendonly" attribute.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the offerer wishes to only receive media from its peer, it MUST mark the stream as recvonly.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the offerer wishes to communicate, but wishes to neither send nor receive media at this time, it MUST mark the stream with an "a=inactive" attribute.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the offerer wishes to both send and receive media with its peer, it MAY include an "a=sendrecv" attribute, or it MAY omit it, since sendrecv is the default.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: A port number of zero in the offer indicates that the stream is offered but MUST NOT be used.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In other words, the answerer MAY change formats in the middle of the session, making use of any of the formats listed, without sending a new offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For a sendonly stream, the offer SHOULD indicate those formats the offerer is willing to send for this stream.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For a recvonly stream, the offer SHOULD indicate those formats the offerer is willing to receive for this stream.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For a sendrecv stream, the offer SHOULD indicate those codecs that the offerer is willing to send and receive with.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: However, for sendonly and sendrecv streams, the answer might indicate different payload type numbers for the same codecs, in which case, the offerer MUST send with the payload type numbers from the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: As per RFC 2327, fmtp parameters MAY be present to provide additional parameters of the media format.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In the case of RTP streams, all media descriptions SHOULD contain "a=rtpmap" mappings from RTP payload types to encodings.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In all cases, the formats in the "m=" line MUST be listed in order of preference, with the first format listed being preferred.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In this case, preferred means that the recipient of the offer SHOULD use the format with the highest preference that is acceptable to it.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The ptime attribute MUST be greater than zero.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Each stream MAY use different encodings.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: First, when receiving multiple streams of the same type, each stream MUST be mapped to at least one sink for the purpose of presentation to the user.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Another constraint is that when multiple streams are received and sent to the same sink, they MUST be combined in some media specific way.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The third constraint is that if multiple sources are mapped to the same stream, those sources MUST be combined in some media specific way before they are sent on the stream.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Once the offerer has sent the offer, it MUST be prepared to receive media for any recvonly streams described by that offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: It MUST be prepared to send and receive media for any sendrecv streams in the offer, and send media for any sendonly streams in the offer (of course, it cannot actually send until the peer provides an answer with the needed address and port information).
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the answer is different from the offer in any way (different IP addresses, ports, etc.), the origin line MUST be different in the answer, since the answer is generated by a different entity.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For each "m=" line in the offer, there MUST be a corresponding "m=" line in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The answer MUST contain exactly the same number of "m=" lines as the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: This implies that if the offer contained zero "m=" lines, the answer MUST contain zero "m=" lines.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The "t=" line in the answer MUST equal that of the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: An offered stream MAY be rejected in the answer, for any reason.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If a stream is rejected, the offerer and answerer MUST NOT generate media (or RTCP packets) for that stream.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: To reject an offered stream, the port number in the corresponding stream in the answer MUST be set to zero.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: At least one MUST be present, as specified by SDP.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If a stream is offered with a unicast address, the answer for that stream MUST contain a unicast address.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The media type of the stream in the answer MUST match that of the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If a stream is offered as sendonly, the corresponding stream MUST be marked as recvonly or inactive in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If a media stream is listed as recvonly in the offer, the answer MUST be marked as sendonly or inactive in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If an offered media stream is listed as sendrecv (or if there is no direction attribute at the media or session level, in which case the stream is sendrecv by default), the corresponding stream in the answer MAY be marked as sendonly, recvonly, sendrecv, or inactive.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If an offered media stream is listed as inactive, it MUST be marked as inactive in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For streams marked as recvonly in the answer, the "m=" line MUST contain at least one media format the answerer is willing to receive with from amongst those listed in the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The stream MAY indicate additional media formats, not listed in the corresponding stream in the offer, that the answerer is willing to receive.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For streams marked as sendonly in the answer, the "m=" line MUST contain at least one media format the answerer is willing to send from amongst those listed in the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: For streams marked as sendrecv in the answer, the "m=" line MUST contain at least one codec the answerer is willing to both send and receive, from amongst those listed in the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The stream MAY indicate additional media formats, not listed in the corresponding stream in the offer, that the answerer is willing to send or receive (of course, it will not be able to send them at this time, since it was not listed in the offer).
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: This address and port MUST be present even for sendonly streams; in the case of RTP, the port one higher is still used to receive RTCP.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In the case of RTP, if a particular codec was referenced with a specific payload type number in the offer, that same payload type number SHOULD be used for that codec in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Even if the same payload type number is used, the answer MUST contain rtpmap attributes to define the payload type mappings for dynamic payload types, and SHOULD contain mappings for static payload types.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The media formats in the "m=" line MUST be listed in order of preference, with the first format listed being preferred.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In this case, preferred means that the offerer SHOULD use the format with the highest preference from the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Although the answerer MAY list the formats in their desired order of preference, it is RECOMMENDED that unless there is a specific reason, the answerer list formats in the same relative order they were present in the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In other words, if a stream in the offer lists audio codecs 8, 22 and 48, in that order, and the answerer only supports codecs 8 and 48, it is RECOMMENDED that, if the answerer has
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: This means that the same fmtp parameters with the same values MUST be present in the answer if the media format they describe is present in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In that case, the answer MAY contain fmtp parameters, and those MAY have the same values as those in the offer, or they MAY be different.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: SDP extensions that define new parameters SHOULD specify the proper interpretation in offer/answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The answerer MAY include a non-zero ptime attribute for any media stream; this indicates the packetization interval that the answerer would like to receive.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The answerer MAY include a bandwidth attribute for any media stream; this indicates the bandwidth that the answerer would like the offerer to use when sending media.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If the answerer has no media formats in common for a particular offered stream, the answerer MUST reject that media stream by setting the port to zero.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Once the answerer has sent the answer, it MUST be prepared to receive media for any recvonly streams described by that answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: It MUST be prepared to send and receive media for any sendrecv streams in the answer, and it MAY send media immediately.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The answerer MUST be prepared to receive media for recvonly or sendrecv streams using any media formats listed for those streams in the answer, and it MAY send media immediately.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: When sending media, it SHOULD use a packetization interval equal to the value of the ptime attribute in the offer, if any was present.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: It SHOULD send media using a bandwidth no higher than the value of the bandwidth attribute in the offer, if any was present.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The answerer MUST send using a media format in the offer that is also listed in the answer, and SHOULD send using the most preferred media format in the offer that is also listed in the
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: In the case of RTP, it MUST use the payload type numbers from the offer, even if they differ from those in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If a multicast stream is accepted, the address and port information in the answer MUST match that of the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: Similarly, the directionality information in the answer (sendonly, recvonly, or sendrecv) MUST equal that of the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The set of media formats in the answer MUST be equal to or be a subset of those in the offer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The ptime and bandwidth attributes in the answer MUST equal the ones in the offer, if present.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: If not present, a non-zero ptime MAY be added to the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: When the offerer receives the answer, it MAY send media on the accepted stream(s) (assuming it is listed as sendrecv or recvonly in the answer).
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: It MUST send using a media format listed in the answer, and it SHOULD use the first media format listed in the answer when it does send.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The reason this is a SHOULD, and not a MUST (its also a SHOULD, and not a MUST, for the answerer), is because there will oftentimes be a need to change codecs on the fly.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: The offerer SHOULD send media according to the value of any ptime and bandwidth attribute in the answer.
notes: SDP content is built by the application; chappe_sip carries it opaquely (the product catalogue owns this row)

text: A UAS MAY send any non-100 provisional response to INVITE reliably, so long as the initial INVITE request (the request whose provisional response is being sent reliably) contained a Supported header field with the option tag 100rel.
notes: INVITE with Supported: 100rel may get 18x carrying Require: 100rel and RSeq

text: The UAS MUST send any non-100 provisional response reliably if the initial request contained a Require header field with the option tag 100rel.
notes: INVITE with Require: 100rel gets every non-100 1xx with Require: 100rel and RSeq

text: If the UAS is unwilling to do so, it MUST reject the initial request with a 420 (Bad Extension) and include an Unsupported header field containing the option tag 100rel.
notes: chappe always supports 100rel and has no switch to refuse it, so the unwilling-UAS case never arises; the generic 420 with Unsupported is covered by R3261 8.2.2 tests

text: A UAS MUST NOT attempt to send a 100 (Trying) response reliably.
notes: 100 Trying never carries RSeq or Require: 100rel

text: If the request did not include either a Supported or Require header field indicating this feature, the UAS MUST NOT send the provisional response reliably.
notes: INVITE without 100rel in Supported/Require gets 18x with no RSeq

text: However, it MUST NOT attempt to do so for any request that contains a tag in the To field.
notes: proxy role

text: Of course, unlike a UAS, when the proxy element receives a PRACK that does not match any outstanding reliable provisional response, the PRACK MUST be proxied.
notes: proxy role

text: As a more efficient alternative, the UAS can send the response reliably, in which case the UAS SHOULD send provisional responses once every two and a half minutes.
notes: long-pending INVITE answered with reliable 18x repeated at most every 150 s

text: Use of reliable provisional responses for extending transactions is RECOMMENDED.
notes: transaction extension uses reliable 18x when peer supports 100rel

text: In addition, it MUST contain a Require header field containing the option tag 100rel, and MUST include an RSeq header field.
notes: reliable 18x carries Require: 100rel and an RSeq header

text: The value of the header field for the first reliable provisional response in a transaction MUST be between 1 and 2**31 - 1.
notes: first reliable 18x RSeq is in 1..2^31-1

text: It is RECOMMENDED that it be chosen uniformly in this range.
notes: initial RSeq differs across calls (random start)

text: This means that provisional responses for different requests MAY use the same values for the RSeq number.
notes: UAC accepts equal RSeq values on reliable 18x of different INVITEs

text: The reliable provisional response MAY contain a body.
notes: reliable 183 may carry an SDP body

text: If a PRACK request is received by the UA core that does not match any unacknowledged reliable provisional response, the UAS MUST respond to the PRACK with a 481 response.
notes: PRACK with unknown RAck gets 481

text: If the PRACK does match an unacknowledged reliable provisional response, it MUST be responded to with a 2xx response.
notes: PRACK matching RAck gets 200

text: It SHOULD cease retransmissions of the reliable provisional response, and MUST remove it from the list of unacknowledged provisional responses.
notes: after matching PRACK, the reliable 18x is no longer retransmitted

text: If a reliable provisional response is retransmitted for 64*T1 seconds without reception of a corresponding PRACK, the UAS SHOULD reject the original request with a 5xx response.
notes: reliable 18x unPRACKed for 64*T1 leads to 5xx final on the INVITE

text: After the first reliable provisional response for a request has been acknowledged, the UAS MAY send additional reliable provisional responses.
notes: after PRACK of first reliable 18x, further reliable 18x may follow

text: The UAS MUST NOT send a second reliable provisional response until the first is acknowledged.
notes: second reliable 18x not sent before PRACK of the first

text: After the first, it is RECOMMENDED that the UAS not send an additional reliable provisional response until the previous is acknowledged.
notes: each further reliable 18x waits for PRACK of the previous

text: The value of the RSeq in each subsequent reliable provisional response for the same request MUST be greater by exactly one.
notes: successive reliable 18x RSeq increments by exactly 1

text: RSeq numbers MUST NOT wrap around.
notes: n/a, holds by construction: nta starts RSeq at most 2^31-1 and refuses to send at 0xffffffff, so it never wraps past 2^32-1 within one INVITE; unreachable on the wire (2^31 reliable 1xx)

text: The UAS MAY send a final response to the initial request before having received PRACKs for all unacknowledged reliable provisional responses, unless the final response is 2xx and any of the unacknowledged reliable provisional responses contained a session description.
notes: non-2xx final may be sent while reliable 18x without SDP is unacknowledged

text: In that case, it MUST NOT send a final response until those provisional responses are acknowledged.
notes: 200 OK held until PRACK of an unacknowledged reliable 18x carrying SDP

text: If the UAS does send a final response when reliable responses are still unacknowledged, it SHOULD NOT continue to retransmit the unacknowledged reliable provisional responses, but it MUST be prepared to process PRACK requests for those outstanding responses.
notes: PRACK arriving after the final response still gets 200

text: A UAS MUST NOT send new reliable provisional responses (as opposed to retransmissions of unacknowledged ones) after sending a final response to a request.
notes: no new reliable 18x after the final response

text: A Require header with the value 100rel MUST NOT be present in any requests excepting INVITE, although extensions to SIP may allow its usage with other request methods.
notes: non-INVITE requests from chappe never carry Require: 100rel

text: If the UAC does not wish to insist on usage of reliable provisional responses, but merely indicate that it supports them if the UAS needs to send one, a Supported header MUST be included in the request with the option tag 100rel.
notes: INVITE advertising 100rel carries Supported: 100rel

text: The UAC SHOULD include this in all INVITE requests.
notes: every INVITE sent by chappe has Supported: 100rel

text: If the response is a 100 (Trying) (as opposed to 101 to 199), this option tag MUST be ignored, and the procedures below MUST NOT be used.
notes: 100 Trying with Require: 100rel is not PRACKed

text: The provisional response MUST establish a dialog if one is not yet created.
notes: reliable 18x with To tag creates an early dialog used by the PRACK

text: Assuming the response is to be transmitted reliably, the UAC MUST create a new request with method PRACK.
notes: reliable 18x triggers PRACK with RAck matching RSeq and CSeq

text: PRACK requests MAY contain bodies, which are interpreted according to their type and disposition.
notes: PRACK may carry SDP body

text: In particular, a UAC SHOULD NOT retransmit the PRACK request when it receives a retransmission of the provisional response being acknowledged, although doing so does not create a protocol error.
notes: retransmitted reliable 18x does not trigger a new PRACK

text: Once a reliable provisional response is received, retransmissions of that response MUST be discarded.
notes: retransmitted reliable 18x is dropped, not re-delivered to the app

text: The UAC MUST maintain a sequence number that indicates the most recently received in-order reliable provisional response for the initial request.
notes: UAC tracks last in-order RSeq; out-of-order 18x not PRACKed

text: This sequence number MUST be maintained until a final response is received for the initial request.
notes: RSeq tracking kept until the INVITE final response

text: Its value MUST be initialized to the RSeq header field in the first reliable provisional response received for the initial request.
notes: first reliable 18x RSeq sets the expected sequence

text: As a result, if the UAC receives another reliable provisional response to the same request, and its RSeq value is not one higher than the value of the sequence number, that response MUST NOT be acknowledged with a PRACK, and MUST NOT be processed further by the UAC.
notes: reliable 18x with RSeq gap gets no PRACK and is not delivered

text: An implementation MAY discard the response, or MAY cache the response in the hopes of receiving the missing responses.
notes: out-of-order reliable 18x may be dropped or cached

text: The UAC MAY acknowledge reliable provisional responses received after the final response or MAY discard them.
notes: reliable 18x after final response may be PRACKed or dropped

text: If the INVITE contained an offer, the UAS MAY generate an answer in a reliable provisional response (assuming these are supported by the UAC).
notes: INVITE with offer may get reliable 183 with SDP answer

text: Similarly, if a reliable provisional response is the first reliable message sent back to the UAC, and the INVITE did not contain an offer, one MUST appear in that reliable provisional response.
notes: offerless INVITE gets first reliable 18x carrying an SDP offer

text: If the UAC receives a reliable provisional response with an offer (this would occur if the UAC sent an INVITE without an offer, in which case the first reliable provisional response will contain the offer), it MUST generate an answer in the PRACK.
notes: reliable 18x with offer is PRACKed with the SDP answer

text: If the UAC receives a reliable provisional response with an answer, it MAY generate an additional offer in the PRACK.
notes: PRACK may carry a new offer after an answer in the 18x

text: If the UAS receives a PRACK with an offer, it MUST place the answer in the 2xx to the PRACK.
notes: PRACK with offer gets 200 carrying the SDP answer

text: Once an answer has been sent or received, the UA SHOULD establish the session based on the parameters of the offer and answer, even if the original INVITE itself has not been responded to.
notes: media flows once the answer is in a reliable 18x or PRACK, before 200

text: If the UAS had placed a session description in any reliable provisional response that is unacknowledged when the INVITE is accepted, the UAS MUST delay sending the 2xx until the provisional response is acknowledged.
notes: 200 to INVITE held until reliable 18x with SDP is PRACKed

text: All user agents that support this extension MUST support all offer/answer exchanges that are possible based on the rules in Section 13.2 of RFC 3261, based on the existence of INVITE and PRACK as requests, and 2xx and reliable 1xx as non-failure reliable responses.
notes: offer/answer in INVITE, reliable 18x, PRACK and 2xx all accepted

text: It MAY be sent for both early and confirmed dialogs, and MAY be sent by either caller or callee.
notes: UPDATE accepted in early and confirmed dialogs from either side

text: Although UPDATE can be used on confirmed dialogs, it is RECOMMENDED that a re-INVITE be used instead.
notes: chappe uses re-INVITE, not UPDATE, to modify a confirmed dialog by default

text: The UAC MAY add optional headers for the UPDATE request, as defined in Tables 1 and 2.
notes: UPDATE may carry optional headers from RFC 3311 tables

text: If a UA uses an UPDATE request or response to modify the remote target while an INVITE transaction is in progress, and it is a UAS for that INVITE transaction, it MUST place the same value into the Contact header field of the 2xx to the INVITE that it placed into the UPDATE request or response.

text: A UAS that receives an UPDATE before it has generated a final response to a previous UPDATE on the same dialog MUST return a 500 response to the new UPDATE, and MUST include a Retry-After header field with a randomly chosen value between 0 and 10 seconds.

text: If an UPDATE is received that contains an offer, and the UAS has generated an offer (in an UPDATE, PRACK or INVITE) to which it has not yet received an answer, the UAS MUST reject the UPDATE with a 491 response.

text: Similarly, if an UPDATE is received that contains an offer, and the UAS has received an offer (in an UPDATE, PRACK, or INVITE) to which it has not yet generated an answer, the UAS MUST
notes: UPDATE with offer while peer offer unanswered gets 500 (see R3311-008)

text: reject the UPDATE with a 500 response, and MUST include a Retry-After header field with a randomly chosen value between 0 and 10 seconds.
notes: that 500 carries Retry-After with value 0..10

text: If a UA receives an UPDATE for an existing dialog, it MUST check any version identifiers in the session description or, if there are no version identifiers, the content of the session description to see if it has changed.
notes: UPDATE with unchanged SDP version leaves media untouched

text: If the session description has changed, the UAS MUST adjust the session parameters accordingly and generate an answer in the 2xx response.
notes: UPDATE with changed SDP gets 200 carrying an SDP answer

text: However, unlike a re-INVITE, the UPDATE MUST be responded to promptly, and therefore the user cannot generally be prompted to approve the session changes.
notes: UPDATE is answered without waiting for user input

text: If the UAS cannot change the session parameters without prompting the user, it SHOULD reject the request with a 504 response.
notes: UPDATE needing user approval gets 504

text: This response SHOULD include a Warning header field.
notes: that 504 carries a Warning header

text: If a UA receives a non-2xx final response to a UPDATE, the session parameters MUST remain unchanged, as if no UPDATE had been issued.
notes: UPDATE rejected with non-2xx leaves previous SDP in force

text: When the timer fires, the UAC SHOULD attempt the UPDATE once more, if it still desires for that session modification to take place.

text: Instead, if it is currently within a dialog with the User Agent Server (UAS), it SHOULD attempt to send the request within the existing target dialog.
notes: without tdialog support, REFER sent inside the existing dialog

text: Specifications that intend to make use of the Target-Dialog header field SHOULD discuss specific conditions in which it is to be included.
notes: addressed to specification authors

text: Assuming it is to be included, the value of the callid production in the Target-Dialog header field MUST be equal to the Call-ID of the target dialog.
notes: Target-Dialog callid equals the target dialog Call-ID

text: The "remote-tag" header field parameter MUST be present and MUST contain the tag that would be viewed as the remote tag from the perspective of the recipient of the new request.
notes: Target-Dialog remote-tag is the recipient-view remote tag

text: The "local-tag" header field parameter MUST be present and MUST contain the tag that would be viewed as the local tag from the perspective of the recipient of the new request.
notes: Target-Dialog local-tag is the recipient-view local tag

text: The request sent by the UAC SHOULD include a Require header field that includes the tdialog option tag.
notes: request with Target-Dialog carries Require: tdialog

text: If a user agent server receives a dialog-creating request and wishes to authorize the request, and if that authorization depends on whether or not the sender has knowledge of an existing dialog with the UAS, and information outside of the Target-Dialog header field does not provide proof of this knowledge, the UAS SHOULD check the request for the existence of the Target-Dialog header field.
notes: out-of-dialog REFER authorisation checks Target-Dialog

text: If this header field is not present, the UAS MAY still authorize the request by other means.
notes: request without Target-Dialog may be authorised by other policy

text: If the header field is present, and the value of the callid production, the "remote-tag", and "local-tag" values match the Call-ID, remote tag, and local tag of an existing dialog, and the dialog that they match was established using a sips URI, the UAS SHOULD authorize the request if it would authorize any entity on the path of the request that created that dialog, or any entity trusted by an ...
notes: matching Target-Dialog on a sips dialog authorises the request

text: If the dialog identifiers match, but they match a dialog not created with a sips URI, the UAS MAY authorize the request if it would authorize any entity on the path of the request that created that dialog, or any entity trusted by an entity on the path of the request that created that dialog.
notes: matching Target-Dialog on a sip dialog may authorise the request

text: If the dialog identifiers don't match, or if they don't contain both a "remote-tag" and "local-tag" parameter, the header field MUST be ignored, and authorization MAY be determined by other means.
notes: Target-Dialog missing a tag or not matching is ignored

text: Inclusion of the Supported header fields in requests is at SHOULD strength per RFC 3261.
notes: informative restatement

text: As such, the conditions in which the SHOULD would not be followed would be those rare cases in which the UA does not want to enable usage of this extension.
notes: informative

text: A CANCEL request SHOULD NOT be sent to cancel a request other than INVITE.
notes: our CANCEL only ever targets an INVITE

text: The Request-URI, Call-ID, To, the numeric part of CSeq, and From header fields in the CANCEL request MUST be identical to those in the request being cancelled, including tags.
notes: CANCEL copies Request-URI, Call-ID, To, From (tags) and CSeq number of the INVITE

text: A CANCEL constructed by a client MUST have only a single Via header field value matching the top Via value in the request being cancelled.
notes: CANCEL has one Via equal to the INVITE top Via

text: However, the method part of the CSeq header field MUST have a value of CANCEL.
notes: CANCEL CSeq method is CANCEL

text: If the request being cancelled contains a Route header field, the CANCEL request MUST include that Route header field's values.
notes: CANCEL of a routed INVITE carries the same Route

text: The CANCEL request MUST NOT contain any Require or Proxy-Require header fields.
notes: CANCEL has no Require or Proxy-Require

text: Once the CANCEL is constructed, the client SHOULD check whether it has received any response (provisional or final) for the request being cancelled (herein referred to as the "original request").
notes: CANCEL waits for a provisional

text: If no provisional response has been received, the CANCEL request MUST NOT be sent; rather, the client MUST wait for the arrival of a provisional response before sending the request.
notes: cancel before any 1xx: CANCEL goes out only after the first provisional

text: If the original request has generated a final response, the CANCEL SHOULD NOT be sent, as it is an effective no-op, since CANCEL has no effect on requests that have already generated a final response.
notes: no CANCEL after a final response

text: The destination address, port, and transport for the CANCEL MUST be identical to those used to send the original request.
notes: CANCEL sent to the same address, port and transport as the INVITE

text: defined in Section 17.1.1.1), the client SHOULD then consider the original transaction cancelled and SHOULD destroy the client transaction handling the original request.
notes: after the CANCEL 200 the INVITE client transaction is cancelled

text: If the UAS did not find a matching transaction for the CANCEL according to the procedure above, it SHOULD respond to the CANCEL with a 481 (Call Leg/Transaction Does Not Exist).
notes: CANCEL with no matching transaction gets 481

text: If the original request was an INVITE, the UAS SHOULD immediately respond to the INVITE with a 487 (Request Terminated).
notes: CANCEL of a pending INVITE: 200 to the CANCEL and 487 to the INVITE

text: This response is constructed following the procedures described in Section 8.2.6 noting that the To tag of the response to the CANCEL and the To tag in the response to the original request SHOULD be the same.
notes: 487 to the INVITE and 200 to the CANCEL carry the same To tag

text: All UAs MUST support the OPTIONS method.
notes: OPTIONS gets a final response

text: Alternatively, a server receiving an OPTIONS request with a Max- Forwards header field value of 0 MAY respond to the request regardless of the Request-URI.
notes: OPTIONS with Max-Forwards 0 answered

text: An OPTIONS request MAY be sent as part of an established dialog to query the peer on capabilities that may be utilized later in the dialog.
notes: in-dialog OPTIONS answered in the dialog

text: A Contact header field MAY be present in an OPTIONS.
notes: Contact on our OPTIONS allowed

text: An Accept header field SHOULD be included to indicate the type of message body the UAC wishes to receive in the response.
notes: our OPTIONS carries Accept

text: The response code chosen MUST be the same that would have been chosen had the request been an INVITE.
notes: OPTIONS gets the status an INVITE would get (e.g. 200, 486 busy focus)

text: Allow, Accept, Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language, and Supported header fields SHOULD be present in a 200 (OK) response to an OPTIONS request.
notes: OPTIONS 200 carries Allow, Accept and Supported

text: If the response is generated by a proxy, the Allow header field SHOULD be omitted as it is ambiguous since a proxy is method agnostic.
notes: proxy role

text: Contact header fields MAY be present in a 200 (OK) response and have the same semantics as in a 3xx response.
notes: Contact in the OPTIONS 200

text: A Warning header field MAY be present.
notes: Warning in the OPTIONS 200

text: A message body MAY be sent, the type of which is determined by the Accept header field in the OPTIONS request (application/sdp is the default if the Accept header field is not present).
notes: capability SDP body in the OPTIONS 200

text: If the types include one that can describe media capabilities, the UAS SHOULD include a body in the response for that purpose.
notes: capability SDP body in the OPTIONS 200 when Accept allows it

text: The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request. This is the appropriate response when a UAS does not recognize the request method and is not capable of supporting it for any user.
notes: a request with an unknown method gets 501

text: A missing Session-Expires means the session does not expire; no timer is asked for unless configured.
notes: a call with no timer configured and none asked by the peer carries no Session-Expires and never refreshes

text: A UAS may request a session timer in the 2xx when the UAC supports it, never below the Min-SE of the request.
notes: configured UAS inserts Session-Expires >= Min-SE in the 2xx to a UAC with Supported: timer

text: A 2xx without Session-Expires leaves the requesting UAC refreshing at its own interval.
notes: UAC that asked for a timer refreshes on its own when the 2xx has no Session-Expires

text: A B2BUA is a UA on each side and answers session refreshes on each leg.
notes: an offerless or unchanged refresh on one leg is answered by that leg, not relayed

text: Each B2BUA leg negotiates its own session timer; Session-Expires, Min-SE and Require: timer are not copied across.
notes: legs negotiate different intervals; timer headers are not relayed

text: A B2BUA relays a new re-INVITE offer to the other leg and the answer back.
notes: re-INVITE offer on A reaches B; B answer returned in A 200

text: A non-2xx answer to a relayed re-INVITE, 491 included, goes back to the offering leg.
notes: B rejects the relayed re-INVITE 488 or 491; A gets the same status

text: A B2BUA relays a new UPDATE offer to the other leg and the answer back.
notes: UPDATE offer on A reaches B; B answer returned in A 200

text: A B2BUA relays the body of B provisional responses (early media) to A.
notes: 183 with SDP from B reaches A with the same SDP

text: proxy_response_headers copies the named headers of B 2xx onto A 2xx.
notes: named header from B 200 appears on A 200

text: A Reason on a BYE is repeated on the BYE the B2BUA sends on the other leg.
notes: BYE with Reason on one leg; the other leg BYE carries the same Reason

text: A B2BUA relays an offerless re-INVITE to the other leg: that leg's offer goes into the 2xx, and the answer in the ACK goes on in the ACK of the other leg.
notes: A re-INVITE without SDP reaches B without SDP; B's offer comes back in A's 2xx; A's ACK answer reaches B's ACK

text: A B2BUA passes every offer and answer it relays through the application's hook and, for an anchored call, the media relay, keeping each answer paired with its offer.
notes: rewrite_sdp sees leg and offer or answer; anchored re-offers from either leg go through rtpengine, a refused one restores the last answer

text: A B2BUA relays an UPDATE with an offer between the early dialogs of a ringing call and the answer back.
notes: A's early UPDATE reaches B's early dialog and back; B's early UPDATE reaches A's early dialog and back

text: A request to a group of peers that gets a 503, a 408 or a transport failure from one peer is tried on the next one.
notes: {peer_group, G}: fs1's 503 sends the call to fs2

text: An OPTIONS request queries a peer; its final response tells it is reachable.
notes: Peers probed with OPTIONS go up on any final but 408 and 503, down on timeouts; the registrar drops UDP contacts that stop answering

text: A request within a dialog that arrives while the dialog is being confirmed is still processed as part of that dialog.
notes: a BYE or re-INVITE sent right after the ACK is answered

text: When the originating UAC receives the 401 (Unauthorized), it SHOULD, if it is able, re-originate the request with the proper credentials.
notes: 401 with a WWW-Authenticate: the INVITE goes again with an Authorization answering it and the call is set up

text: When a UAC resubmits a request with its credentials after receiving a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response, it MUST increment the CSeq header field value as it would normally when sending an updated request.
notes: the INVITE retried with credentials has the CSeq number one higher

text: When the originating UAC receives the 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) it SHOULD, if it is able, re-originate the request with the proper credentials.
notes: 407 with a Proxy-Authenticate: the INVITE goes again with a Proxy-Authorization answering it

text: When resubmitting its request in response to a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) that contains multiple challenges, a UAC MAY include an Authorization value for each WWW-Authenticate value and a Proxy-Authorization value for each Proxy-Authenticate value for which the UAC wishes to supply a credential.
notes: a 407 then a 401: the third INVITE carries the Proxy-Authorization and the Authorization; a 401 naming two realms gets one Authorization per realm

text: As noted above, multiple credentials in a request SHOULD be differentiated by the "realm" parameter.
notes: each credential carries the realm of the challenge it answers

text: This MUST be specified if a qop directive is sent (see above), and MUST NOT be specified if the server did not send a qop directive in the WWW-Authenticate header field.
notes: nc is sent with qop=auth and left out of the RFC 2069 form; the registrar tracks it per nonce

text: The authenticating server must assure that the resource designated by the "uri" directive is the same as the resource specified in the Request-Line; if they are not, the server SHOULD return a 400 Bad Request error.
notes: registrar: a digest uri other than the Request-URI gets 400

text: If the algorithm is not understood, the challenge SHOULD be ignored (and a different one used, if there is more than one).
notes: a SHA-512-256 challenge is skipped and a SHA-256 one of the same 401 answered

text: If stale is false, or anything other than true, or the stale parameter is not present, the username and/or password are invalid, and new values MUST be obtained.
notes: stale=true: retried with the new nonce, not counted as a failure; a second plain challenge for the realm ends with the 401 to the app (no other credentials to try)

text: This parameter MUST be used by all implementations.  The nc parameter stands for "nonce count".  The nc value is the hexadecimal count of the number of requests (including the current request) that the client has sent with the nonce value in this request.
notes: after a 420 the INVITE reuses the nonce with nc=00000002 and a fresh response

text: The authenticating server MUST assure that the resource designated by the "uri" parameter is the same as the resource specified in the Request-Line; if they are not, the server SHOULD return a 400 Bad Request error.
notes: registrar: a digest uri other than the Request-URI gets 400

text: Then, the server MUST perform the same digest operation (e.g., MD5, SHA-256) performed by the client and compare the result to the given response value.
notes: answers computed with SHA-256 and with MD5 both verify

text: If the server responds with multiple challenges, then each one of these challenges MUST use a different digest algorithm.
notes: challenges/2: one WWW-Authenticate per algorithm, one nonce

text: The server MUST add these challenges to the response in order of preference, starting with the most preferred algorithm, followed by the less preferred algorithm.
notes: SHA-256 first, MD5 second

text: The purpose of this parameter is to allow the server to detect request replays by maintaining its own copy of this count -- if the same nc value is seen twice, then the request is a replay.
notes: a replayed nonce count gets 401 with stale=true; a higher one on the same nonce passes

text: Its value MUST be one of the alternatives the server indicated it supports in the WWW-Authenticate header field.
notes: the registrar refuses an answer without qop or with auth-int to its qop=auth challenge; the client refuses an auth-int only challenge

text: The client MUST ignore any challenge it does not understand.
notes: a challenge with an unknown algorithm is skipped; the others of the 401 are answered

text: If the UAS challenges the originator using multiple WWW-Authenticate/Proxy-Authenticate header fields with the same realm, then each of these header fields MUST use a different digest algorithm.
notes: challenges/2: SHA-256 and MD5 for one realm

text: When the UAC receives a response with multiple WWW-Authenticate/Proxy-Authenticate header fields with the same realm, it SHOULD use the topmost header field that it supports unless a local policy dictates otherwise.
notes: local policy: the strongest algorithm (SHA-256 before MD5), the topmost on a tie; MD5 listed first still gets a SHA-256 answer

text: When the UAC receives a 401 response with multiple WWW-Authenticate header fields with different realms, it SHOULD retry and add an Authorization header field containing credentials that match the topmost header field of any of the realms unless a local policy dictates otherwise.
notes: a 401 naming two realms: retried with an Authorization for each realm we have credentials for

text: Therefore, in SIP, a UAS MUST check if the Request-URI in the Authorization/Proxy-Authorization header field value corresponds to a user for whom the UAS is willing to accept forwarded or direct requests; however, it MAY still accept it if the two fields are not equivalent.
notes: verify/1 with request_uri compares scheme, user, host and port; the registrar answers a mismatch 400

text: A UAS MUST always send a "qop" parameter in WWW-Authenticate and Proxy-Authenticate header field values, and a UAC MUST send the "qop" parameter in any resulting authorization header field.
notes: our challenges carry qop="auth" and an answer without it is refused; the UAC sends qop for any challenge with it and for a SHA-256 one without it. An MD5 challenge without qop still gets the RFC 2069 form, for older servers

text: SIP clients and servers MUST NOT accept or request Basic authentication.
notes: a Basic challenge is not answered (the app gets the 401); verify/1 refuses a Basic Authorization

text: The UAS MUST add these header fields to the response in the order in which it would prefer to see them used, starting with the most preferred algorithm at the top.
notes: challenges/2 lists SHA-256 above MD5

text: If the stream to be placed on hold was previously a sendrecv media stream, it is placed on hold by marking it as sendonly.  If the stream to be placed on hold was previously a recvonly media stream, it is placed on hold by marking it inactive.
notes: modify(D, hold): each sendrecv m= section sendonly, each recvonly one inactive, port 0 left alone, o= version bumped; unhold reverses it

text: The SIP-Version string is case-insensitive, but implementations MUST send upper-case.
notes: a request or status line with sip/2.0 parses; every message sent starts with SIP/2.0

text: A header field name is a token (25.1 header-name = token); a line whose name is not one makes the message malformed.
notes: a header named "Bad Name" or with ( ) < > / " @ , or non-ASCII bytes makes parse/1 return {error, malformed}

text: Implementations MUST accept both the long and short forms of each header name.
notes: every IANA compact form (a b c d e f i j k l m n o r s t u v x y) reads as its long header

text: The method MUST match that of the request.
notes: a request whose CSeq is not 1*DIGIT LWS Method, or names another method, is malformed: 400 before the app (validate/1 on the WS and engine ingress)

text: If the request does not contain a Max-Forwards header field, this check is passed.
notes: Max-Forwards is not required of a received request (RFC 2543 peers, RFC 4475 3.4.1): a UAS serves an OPTIONS without one

text: If the copy does not contain a Max-Forwards header field, the proxy MUST add one with a field value, which SHOULD be 70.
notes: chappe_sip_msg:decr_max_forwards/1 sets Max-Forwards: 70 on a request without one, decrements one that is present

text: If the request contains a Proxy-Require header field (Section 20.29) with one or more option-tags this element does not understand, the element MUST return a 420 (Bad Extension) response.
notes: a route registered with proxy => true answers 420 with Unsupported to Proxy-Require: foo and passes Require: foo to its handler

text: The Proxy-Require header field is used to indicate proxy-sensitive features that must be supported by the proxy.
notes: a UAS ignores Proxy-Require: an INVITE with Proxy-Require: foo is answered 200

text: The user part of a SIP URI may carry ";" (user-unreserved): sip:alice;day=tuesday@example.com has user alice;day=tuesday and host example.com.
notes: chappe_sip_uri:parse/1 splits the userinfo at the @ before the uri-parameters (RFC 4475 3.1.1.10 semiuri)

text: SIP and SIPS URIs are compared for equality according to the following rules:
notes: chappe_sip_uri:equal/2 passes the equivalent and the different sets of 19.1.4

text: The Require header field is used by UACs to tell UASs about options that the UAC expects the UAS to support in order to process the request.
notes: a proxy route, and the in-dialog forwarding through our Record-Route, pass an unknown Require on to the far UAS instead of answering 420

text: A registrar MUST not generate 6xx responses.
notes: the registrar answers 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 420, 423, 439, 500 or 503, never a 6xx; a 6xx from an auth policy is sent as 403

text: Registrars MUST ignore the Record-Route header field if it is included in a REGISTER request.
notes: a REGISTER with Record-Route binds as one without (no route stored)

text: Registrars MUST NOT include a Record-Route header field in any response to a REGISTER request.
notes: the 200 to a REGISTER carrying Record-Route has none

text: A registrar has to know (for example, through configuration) the set of domain(s) for which it maintains bindings.
notes: registrar_domains (or the domains option): any, or a list; a REGISTER for another domain gets 404

text: REGISTER requests MUST be processed by a registrar in the order that they are received.
notes: chappe_sip_registry serializes every REGISTER through one process

text: REGISTER requests MUST also be processed atomically, meaning that a particular REGISTER request is either processed completely or not at all.
notes: a REGISTER with one contact failing the CSeq check writes none of its contacts

text: Each REGISTER message MUST be processed independently of any other registration or binding changes.
notes: each REGISTER is one call to the registry process, applied to the bindings as they stand

text: If not, and if the server also acts as a proxy server, the server SHOULD forward the request to the addressed domain, following the general behavior for proxying messages described in Section 16.
notes: the ready-made registrar does not proxy; an app that wants this checks the domain and calls proxy_request/3 itself

text: To guarantee that the registrar supports any necessary extensions, the registrar MUST process the Require header field values as described for UASs in Section 8.2.2.
notes: Require: path gets 420 Unsupported: path unless the REGISTER route takes path (handle/3 option_tags)

text: A registrar SHOULD authenticate the UAC.
notes: chappe_sip:registrar/1 requires an auth hook, or allow_unauthenticated => true, else it raises

text: If no authentication mechanism is available, the registrar MAY take the From address as the asserted identity of the originator of the request.
notes: an unauthenticated registrar is an explicit opt-out; identity policy is the app's

text: The registrar SHOULD determine if the authenticated user is authorized to modify registrations for this address-of-record.
notes: built-in digest binds the authenticated user to the AOR user part

text: If the authenticated user is not authorized to modify bindings, the registrar MUST return a 403 (Forbidden) and skip the remaining steps.
notes: alice's credentials on bob's AOR get 403 and write nothing

text: If the address-of-record is not valid for the domain in the Request-URI, the registrar MUST send a 404 (Not Found) response and skip the remaining steps.
notes: a To or Request-URI outside registrar_domains, or a To that is not a URI, gets 404

text: The URI MUST then be converted to a canonical form.
notes: chappe_sip_uri:aor/1: scheme and host lowercased, parameters and headers dropped

text: To do that, all URI parameters MUST be removed (including the user-param), and any escaped characters MUST be converted to their unescaped form.
notes: sip:%61lice@EXAMPLE.COM;user=phone and sip:alice@example.com are one AOR

text: If the request has additional Contact fields or an expiration time other than zero, the request is invalid, and the server MUST return a 400 (Invalid Request) and skip the remaining steps.
notes: Contact: * with Expires other than 0, without Expires, or beside another Contact gets 400

text: If not, it MUST remove the binding.
notes: Contact: * with Expires: 0 removes the bindings of other Call-IDs

text: If it does agree, it MUST remove the binding only if the CSeq in the request is higher than the value stored for that binding.
notes: Contact: * removes a binding of its own Call-ID only with a higher CSeq

text: Otherwise, the update MUST be aborted and the request fails.
notes: Contact: * with a CSeq not above a binding of the same Call-ID gets 400 and removes nothing

text: If the field value has an "expires" parameter, that value MUST be taken as the requested expiration.
notes: each Contact, comma-joined or not, takes its own expires parameter

text: If there is no such parameter, but the request has an Expires header field, that value MUST be taken as the requested expiration.
notes: a Contact without expires takes the Expires header

text: If there is neither, a locally-configured default value MUST be taken as the requested expiration.
notes: registrar_default_expires (3600) or the default_expires option

text: The registrar MAY choose an expiration less than the requested expiration interval.
notes: registrar_max_expires caps the expiry

text: If and only if the requested expiration interval is greater than zero AND smaller than one hour AND less than a registrar-configured minimum, the registrar MAY reject the registration with a response of 423 (Interval Too Brief).
notes: registrar_min_expires defaults to 60: 30 s gets 423, 60 s is accepted, an hour or more never gets 423

text: This response MUST contain a Min-Expires header field that states the minimum expiration interval the registrar is willing to honor.
notes: the 423 carries Min-Expires: 60

text: If the Call-ID value in the existing binding differs from the Call-ID value in the request, the binding MUST be removed if the expiration time is zero and updated otherwise.
notes: a binding refreshed from a new Call-ID is updated whatever the CSeq, and expires=0 from one removes it

text: If the value is higher than that of the existing binding, it MUST update or remove the binding as above.
notes: the CSeq is compared per binding: a higher one on the same Call-ID updates it, a new contact on that Call-ID is added whatever the CSeq

text: If not, the update MUST be aborted and the request fails.
notes: a CSeq not above the binding's on the same Call-ID gets 400

text: The binding updates MUST be committed (that is, made visible to the proxy or redirect server) if and only if all binding updates and additions succeed.
notes: a REGISTER refused 400, 403 or 503 leaves the bindings as they were

text: If any one of them fails (for example, because the back-end database commit failed), the request MUST fail with a 500 (Server Error) response and all tentative binding updates MUST be removed.
notes: the store is one ETS insert after every check passed; a REGISTER the store did not apply in time gets the worker's 500 and is refused unapplied when the store gets to it

text: The response MUST contain Contact header field values enumerating all current bindings.
notes: the 200 lists every live binding of the AOR, the highest q first; a query REGISTER lists them unchanged

text: Each Contact value MUST feature an "expires" parameter indicating its expiration interval chosen by the registrar.
notes: every Contact in the 200 ends with ;expires=<seconds left>

text: The response SHOULD include a Date header field.
notes: the 200 carries an RFC 1123 Date in GMT

text: For each address, the registrar then searches the list of current bindings using the URI comparison rules.
notes: a contact equal by 19.1.4 (case, unknown parameters) refreshes its binding; another port makes a new one

text: The "q" parameter indicates a relative preference for the particular Contact header field value compared to other bindings for this address-of-record.
notes: location/1 and bindings/1 list the highest q first (no q counts as 1.0); the 200 echoes each q

text: If a Path header field exists in a successful REGISTER request, the registrar constructs an ordered list of route elements (a path vector) from the nodes listed in the Path header field values, preserving the order as indicated in the Path header field values.
notes: Path values from several headers and comma lists are kept in order

text: The registrar then stores this path vector in association with that contact and the address-of-record indicated in the REGISTER request (the "binding" as defined in [1]).
notes: bindings/1 returns the path of each binding, the route set toward the contact

text: The registrar copies the Path header field values into a Path header field in the successful (200 class) REGISTER response.
notes: the 200 carries the request's Path

text: In the event that the home proxy and registrar are not co-located, the registrar MAY apply a locally-determined transformation to the stored path vector.
notes: the path is stored as received; a transformation is the app's

text: The recommended policy is for the registrar to reject the request with a 420 "Bad Extension" response indicating the Path extension.
notes: a Path without Supported: path gets 420 Unsupported: path and writes nothing

text: Registrars that implement this specification MUST support the Path header mechanism [RFC3327].
notes: Path is stored and echoed (R3327-R-01..03)

text: When receiving a REGISTER request, the registrar MUST check from its Via header field if the registrar is the first hop or not.
notes: one Via value is the first hop

text: If the registrar is not the first hop, it MUST examine the Path header of the request.
notes: past the first hop the first Path URI decides

text: If the Path header field is missing or it exists but the first URI does not have an "ob" URI parameter, then outbound processing MUST NOT be applied to the registration.
notes: two Vias and no "ob" Path: the reg-id is not used, the contact binds by URI

text: In this case, the following processing applies: if the REGISTER request contains the reg-id and the outbound option tag in a Supported header field, then the registrar MUST respond to the REGISTER request with a 439 (First Hop Lacks Outbound Support) response; otherwise, the registrar MUST ignore the "reg-id" parameter of the Contact header.
notes: with Supported: outbound the same REGISTER gets 439, without it the reg-id is ignored

text: If the registrar processes a Contact header field value with a reg-id but no instance-id, it simply ignores the reg-id parameter.
notes: a reg-id without +sip.instance binds by URI

text: Therefore, if the Contact header field contains more than one header field value with a non-zero expiration and any of these header field values contain a "reg-id" Contact header field parameter, the entire registration SHOULD be rejected with a 400 (Bad Request) response.
notes: two non-zero contacts, one with a reg-id, get 400

text: If the Contact header did not contain a "reg-id" Contact header field parameter or if that parameter was ignored (as described above), the registrar MUST NOT include the outbound option-tag in the Require header field of its response.
notes: no Require: outbound when the reg-id was absent or ignored, or the UA did not list outbound

text: The registrar MUST be prepared to receive, simultaneously for the same AOR, some registrations that use instance-id and reg-id and some registrations that do not.
notes: an AOR holds flow bindings and a plain binding of the same URI side by side
