text: When a "+sip.instance" Contact header field parameter and a "reg-id" Contact header field parameter are present in a Contact header field of a REGISTER request (after the Contact header validation as described above), the corresponding binding is between an AOR and the combination of the instance-id (from the "+sip.instance" Contact header parameter) and the value of "reg-id" Contact header field parameter parameter.
notes: one binding per (instance, reg-id): reg-id 1 and 2 of one instance are two bindings

text: The registrar MUST store in the binding the Contact URI, all the Contact header field parameters, and any Path header field values.
notes: bindings/1 returns contact, params (every Contact parameter), path, instance and reg_id

text: Provided that the UAC had included an outbound option-tag (defined in Section 11.4) in a Supported header field value in the REGISTER request, the registrar MUST include the outbound option-tag in a Require header field value in its response to that REGISTER request.
notes: a flow registration with Supported: outbound gets Require: outbound in its 200

text: If the UAC has a direct flow with the registrar, the registrar MUST store enough information to uniquely identify the network flow over which the request arrived.
notes: an outbound REGISTER sent straight to us binds to its flow: the TCP/TLS connection, or the UDP source address and port; a request for the AOR goes back over it

text: If the registrar receives a re-registration for a specific combination of AOR, and instance-id and reg-id values, the registrar MUST update any information that uniquely identifies the network flow over which the request arrived if that information has changed, and SHOULD update the time the binding was last updated.
notes: a re-registration of a flow over another WS connection moves the binding to it

text: To be compliant with this specification, registrars that can receive SIP requests directly from a UAC without intervening edge proxies MUST implement the same keep-alive mechanisms as edge proxies (Section 5.4).
notes: sofia-sip answers a STUN Binding request on the UDP port and a CRLFCRLF ping on TCP and TLS with a CRLF pong; the WS listener answers the CRLF ping too

text: Registrars with a direct flow with a UA MAY include a Flow-Timer header in a 2xx class registration response that includes the outbound option-tag in the Require header.
notes: a first-hop flow registration gets Flow-Timer: registrar_flow_timer (120); through an edge it gets none

text: If a proxy or registrar receives information from the network that indicates that no future messages will be delivered on a specific flow, then the proxy MUST invalidate all the bindings in the target set that use that flow (regardless of AOR).
notes: remove_flow/1 drops the bindings of that flow only, in every AOR: on a WS disconnect, and when the TCP/TLS connection of an outbound binding closes

text: An SRC MUST include the "siprec" option tag in the Require header when initiating an RS so that UAs that do not support the Session Recording Protocol extensions will simply reject the INVITE request with a 420 (Bad Extension) response.
notes: an INVITE with Require: siprec gets 420 Unsupported: siprec from a route that does not take it

text: As per [RFC3261], only an SRC or an SRS can accept this option tag in an RS.
notes: a route registered with option_tags => [<<"siprec">>] (or siprec in supported_option_tags) takes the INVITE and its in-dialog requests

text: If the first value in the Route header field indicates this proxy, the proxy MUST remove that value from the request.
notes: our top Route (HMAC-checked, unexpired) is popped and the next value, even on the same comma-joined line, is the next hop; a forged or expired marker is not ours

text: If the request contains a Max-Forwards header field with a field value of zero (0), the element MUST NOT forward the request. If the request was for OPTIONS, the element MAY act as the final recipient and respond per Section 11. Otherwise, the element MUST return a 483 (Too many hops) response.
notes: INVITE with Max-Forwards 0 to proxy_request gets 483 and is not forwarded

text: Notice that a proxy is not required to detect merged requests and MUST NOT treat merged requests as an error condition.
notes: a request spiralling back through the proxy (same From tag, Call-ID, CSeq, new branch) is forwarded, not answered 482; merge detection runs only for a non-proxied transaction

text: If the parameters match, the request has looped. If they differ, the request is spiraling, and processing continues. If a loop is detected, the element MAY return a 482 (Loop Detected) response.
notes: our Via branch carries a hash of the received request; back with one of our Vias and the same hash: 482 Loop Detected

text: If they differ, the request is spiraling, and processing continues.
notes: back with one of our Vias and a different hash (new Request-URI): forwarded again

text: If the Request-URI of the request contains a value this proxy previously placed into a Record-Route header field (see Section 16.6 item 4), the proxy MUST replace the Request-URI in the request with the last value from the Route header field, and remove that value from the Route header field. The proxy MUST then proceed as if it received this modified request.
notes: BYE whose Request-URI is our Record-Route URI and whose last Route is the target reaches the target with that URI and the Route value removed

text: The Request-URI in the copy's start line MUST be replaced with the URI for this target.
notes: callee sees the target URI as Request-URI; a host:port target keeps the user of the received Request-URI

text: If the Request-URI contains a SIPS URI, or the topmost Route header field value (after the post processing of bullet 6) contains a SIPS URI, the URI placed into the Record-Route header field MUST be a SIPS URI.
notes: a SIPS request to a SIPS target gets a sips: Record-Route (our TLS address); a request over TLS to a sip: target gets a sip: one

text: If the copy contains a Route header field, the proxy MUST inspect the URI in its first value.
notes: the top Route of a preloaded route set decides the next hop; a strict (no lr) one is swapped with the Request-URI

text: Otherwise, the proxy MUST apply the procedures to the first value in the Route header field, if present, else the Request-URI.
notes: INVITE with a preloaded Route reaches the Route URI with the target as Request-URI and the Route kept

text: Timer C MUST be set for each client transaction when an INVITE request is proxied. The timer MUST be larger than 3 minutes.
notes: each proxied INVITE branch runs Timer C (timer_c_ms, 185 s by default, or the timer_c option); tests use a short one

text: For an INVITE transaction, if the response is a provisional response with status codes 101 to 199 inclusive (i.e., anything but 100), the proxy MUST reset timer C for that client transaction.
notes: a callee sending 180 every 300 ms rings for three times a 600 ms Timer C and still connects (proxy and b2bua)

text: If the client transaction has received a provisional response, the proxy MUST generate a CANCEL request matching that transaction.
notes: Timer C fires on a ringing branch: the callee gets a CANCEL and the caller a 408 (proxy and b2bua)

text: If the client transaction has not received a provisional response, the proxy MUST behave as if the transaction received a 408 (Request Timeout)
notes: a branch that never answered is dropped when Timer C fires and the caller gets 408

text: It MUST choose from the 6xx class responses if any exist in the context. If no 6xx class responses are present, the proxy SHOULD choose from the lowest response class stored in the response context.
notes: best final: a 6xx (relayed once the CANCELled branches answered), else the lowest class

text: If the only response that was received is a 503, the proxy SHOULD generate a 500 response and forward that upstream.
notes: a branch answering 503 makes the caller get 500

text: The proxy SHOULD give preference to responses that provide information affecting resubmission of this request, such as 401, 407, 415, 420, and 484 if the 4xx class is chosen.
notes: 404 from one branch and 484 from another: the caller gets 484

text: If the selected response is a 401 (Unauthorized) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required), the proxy MUST collect any WWW- Authenticate and Proxy-Authenticate header field values from all other 401 (Unauthorized) and 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) responses received so far in this response context and add them to this response without modification before forwarding.
notes: 401 and 407 from two branches: the relayed one carries both challenges

text: After a final response has been sent on the server transaction, the following responses MUST be forwarded immediately: - Any 2xx response to an INVITE request
notes: a 2xx is forwarded at once, also one crossing the caller's CANCEL or arriving after the first 2xx

text: If the proxy received the request over TLS, and sent it out over a non-TLS connection, the proxy MUST rewrite the URI in the Record-Route header field to be a SIPS URI.
notes: TLS in, sip out: two Record-Routes (RFC 5658 5), our sips URI for the TLS side and our sip URI on top for the sip side, so the TLS caller routes back to our sips address without the 2xx being rewritten

text: If there are no final responses in the context, the proxy MUST send a 408 (Request Timeout) response to the server transaction.
notes: no branch gave a final: the caller gets 408

text: A proxy MUST cancel any pending client transactions associated with a response context when it receives a matching CANCEL request.
notes: the caller's CANCEL (initial INVITE, or a re-INVITE in transit through our record route) reaches the ringing callee

text: If a matching response context is found, the element MUST immediately return a 200 (OK) response to the CANCEL request.
notes: the caller's CANCEL gets 200 and its INVITE the 487 the callee sent (callee To-tag), not one the proxy made

text: Furthermore, the element MUST generate CANCEL requests for all pending client transactions in the context as described in Section 16.7 step 10.
notes: a CANCELled INVITE whose callee answered 200 as the CANCEL arrived relays that 200 upstream

text: An element sending or receiving a 2xx to an INVITE transaction MUST NOT destroy any matching INVITE transaction state.
notes: the proxy keeps its INVITE client transactions for 64*T1 after the first 2xx; over TCP/TLS, where nta ends them at the first 2xx, a later 2xx of the branch still reaches the proxy (the agent stray-response callback)

text: If a 2xx response is received while the client INVITE state machine is in the "Calling" or "Proceeding" states, it MUST transition to the "Accepted" state, pass the 2xx response to the TU, and set Timer M to 64*T1.
notes: a 2xx from another fork 6 s after the first still reaches the caller (proxy_accepted_ms, 32 s)

text: A 2xx response received while in the "Accepted" state MUST be passed to the TU and the machine remains in the "Accepted" state.
notes: a second 2xx with another To-tag on the same branch is forwarded, over UDP, TCP and TLS; a retransmission of one already forwarded is absorbed

text: The client transaction MUST NOT generate an ACK to any 2xx response on its own.
notes: a proxy INVITE branch is created outside nta UA mode, so a second 2xx is not ACKed and BYEd by the stack but forwarded

text: The proxy MUST NOT forward the response if there is no matching transaction state machine.
notes: a response matching no client transaction, and no proxy branch still in the Accepted state, is dropped

text: The client MUST determine the SIP domain identities in the server certificate using the procedure in Section 7.1.
notes: outbound TLS (verify => peer, the default) takes the subjectAltName URI/DNS identities of a certificate cafile.pem signs

text: If the server is not authenticated, the client MUST close the connection immediately.
notes: a server with a self-signed certificate gets the handshake closed and no request

text: Then, the client MUST compare the original domain portion of the SIP AUS used as input to the RFC 3263 [8] server location procedures to the SIP domain identities obtained from the certificate.
notes: the target host is matched against the certificate identities (sofia subject search); verify => none needs allow_insecure => true

text: If the client does not present a certificate, the client MUST NOT be considered authenticated.
notes: verify_clients => true: a client without a certificate is refused, one the CA signed is served

text: A proxy MUST use the procedures defined for a User Agent Client (UAC) in Section 7.3 when requesting an authenticated connection to a UAS.
notes: a proxy branch to a sips target is sent over a TLS connection checked as in 7.3

text: If a proxy adds a Record-Route when forwarding a request with the expectation that the route is to use secure connections, the proxy MUST insert into the Record-Route header a URI that corresponds to an identity for which the proxy has a certificate;
notes: the sips Record-Route is the TLS listener address, the identity of the agent.pem certificate

text: Specifically, when a proxy receives a request with a SIPS Request-URI, the proxy MUST only forward or retarget the request to a SIPS Request-URI.
notes: a SIPS request goes on to a SIPS target, record-routed with a sips URI

text: If the request that initiated the dialog contained a SIPS URI in the Request-URI or in the top Record-Route header field value, if there was any, or the Contact header field if there was no Record- Route header field, the Contact header field in the response MUST be a SIPS URI.
notes: 2xx to an INVITE over TLS with a sips Contact carries our sips Contact

text: To emphasize what is already defined in [RFC3261], proxies MUST NOT use the "transport=tls" parameter.
notes: our sips Record-Route and Contact carry no transport=tls; the listener refuses TLS 1.0/1.1

text: When a proxy receives a request with a SIP Request-URI, the proxy MUST NOT forward the request to a SIPS Request-URI. If the target UAS had registered previously using a SIPS Contact header field, and the proxy decides to forward the request, the proxy MUST replace that SIPS scheme with a SIP scheme while leaving the rest of the URI as is, and use the resulting URI as the Request-URI of the forwarded request. The proxy MUST use TLS to forward the request to the UAS.
notes: a SIP request for a sips target goes over TLS with a sip Request-URI

text: If the proxy needs to reject the request for that reason, the proxy MUST reject it with a 480 (Temporarily Unavailable) response.
notes: a SIPS request for a sip target is answered 480

text: The Record-Route header field has no meaning in PUBLISH requests or responses, and MUST be ignored if present.
notes: a Record-Route in the 200 to our PUBLISH is ignored: the refresh carries no Route

text: In particular, the UAC MUST NOT create a new route set based on the presence or absence of a Record-Route header field in any response to a PUBLISH request.
notes: the refresh PUBLISH after a 200 with Record-Route goes to the Request-URI with no Route

text: EPAs MUST NOT send a new PUBLISH request (not a re-transmission) for the same Request-URI, until they have received a final response from the ESC for the previous one or the previous PUBLISH request has timed out.
notes: chappe_sip_publisher:update/2 while a PUBLISH is pending: the modify goes out only after its final response

text: For determining the type of the published event state, the EPA MUST include a single Event header field in PUBLISH requests.
notes: every PUBLISH of chappe_sip:publish_state/4 carries one Event

text: When updating previously published event state, PUBLISH requests MUST contain a single SIP-If-Match header field identifying the specific event state that the request is refreshing, modifying or removing.
notes: the refresh, the modify and the remove each carry one SIP-If-Match

text: This header field MUST contain a single entity-tag that was returned by the ESC in the SIP-ETag header field of the response to a previous publication.
notes: SIP-If-Match is the SIP-ETag of the last 2xx

text: An initial PUBLISH request MUST NOT contain a SIP-If-Match header field.
notes: the first PUBLISH, and the one after a 412, carry no SIP-If-Match

text: However, if the EPA expects an appropriate, locally stored entity-tag to still be valid, it SHOULD first try to modify that event state as described in Section 4.4, instead of submitting an initial publication.
notes: update/2 with a stored entity-tag sends a modify (body and SIP-If-Match), not an initial PUBLISH

text: An initial PUBLISH request MUST contain a body that contains the published event state.
notes: the initial PUBLISH carries the body with its Content-Type

text: To refresh a publication, the EPA MUST create a PUBLISH request that includes in a SIP-If-Match header field the entity-tag of the publication to be refreshed.
notes: before the granted Expires runs out a refresh PUBLISH goes out with SIP-If-Match

text: The EPA MUST store this entity-tag, replacing any existing entity-tag for the refreshed event state.
notes: the PUBLISH after a refresh names the entity-tag of the refresh's 2xx

text: Therefore, a PUBLISH request that refreshes event state MUST NOT have a body.
notes: the refresh PUBLISH has Content-Length 0

text: To modify event state, the EPA MUST construct a PUBLISH request that includes in a SIP-If-Match header field the entity-tag of the event state publication to be modified.
notes: update/2 sends SIP-If-Match with the stored entity-tag

text: A PUBLISH request that modifies event state MUST contain a body that includes the modified event state.
notes: the modify carries the new body

text: The EPA MUST store this entity-tag, replacing any existing entity-tag for the modified event state.
notes: the PUBLISH after a modify names the entity-tag of the modify's 2xx

text: To request the immediate removal of event state, an EPA MUST create a PUBLISH request with an Expires value of "0", and set the SIP-If- Match header field to contain the entity-tag of the event state publication to be removed.
notes: unpublish/1 sends Expires: 0 with SIP-If-Match

text: Therefore, a PUBLISH request that removes event state MUST NOT contain a body.
notes: the remove PUBLISH has Content-Length 0

text: If an EPA receives a 412 (Conditional Request Failed) response, it MUST NOT reattempt the PUBLISH request.
notes: a refresh answered 412 is not sent again with the same SIP-If-Match

text: Instead, to publish event state, the EPA SHOULD perform an initial publication, i.e., a PUBLISH request without a SIP-If-Match header field, as described in Section 4.2.
notes: after a 412 the full body goes out again in an initial PUBLISH

text: The EPA MUST also discard the entity-tag that produced this error response.
notes: the PUBLISH after the 412 names no entity-tag, and the one after it the new one

text: If an EPA receives a 423 (Interval Too Brief) response to a PUBLISH request, it MAY retry the publication after changing the expiration interval in the Expires header field to be equal to or greater than the expiration interval within the Min-Expires header field of the 423 (Interval Too Brief) response.
notes: a 423 with Min-Expires: 120 gets the PUBLISH again with Expires: 120

text: The ESC MUST ignore the Record-Route header field if it is included in a PUBLISH request.
notes: holds by construction: a PUBLISH forms no dialog (chappe_sip_esc never reads its Record-Route)

text: The ESC MUST NOT include a Record-Route header field in any response to a PUBLISH request.
notes: a PUBLISH with Record-Route gets a 200 with none

text: The ESC MUST ignore the Contact header field if one is present in a PUBLISH request.
notes: a PUBLISH with a Contact is stored the same and the 200 carries no Contact

text: PUBLISH requests with the same Request-URI MUST be processed in the order that they are received.
notes: holds by construction: chappe_sip_esc applies every publication in one process, in the order the requests reach it

text: PUBLISH requests MUST also be processed atomically, meaning that a particular PUBLISH request is either processed completely or not at all.
notes: holds by construction: a publication is one call to chappe_sip_esc, which checks then writes, or answers an error and writes nothing

text: If not, the ESC MUST return a 404 (Not Found) response and skip the remaining steps.
notes: a PUBLISH to a resource the resources option refuses gets 404

text: If the Event header field is missing or contains an event package which the ESC does not support, the ESC MUST respond to the PUBLISH request with a 489 (Bad Event) response, and skip the remaining steps.
notes: a PUBLISH for a package the ESC does not serve, or with no Event, gets 489

text: If the request does not contain a SIP-If-Match header field, the ESC MUST generate and store a locally unique entity-tag for identifying the publication.
notes: an initial PUBLISH gets 200 with a SIP-ETag the next PUBLISH can name

text: If not, the request is invalid, and the ESC MUST return with a 400 (Invalid Request) response and skip the remaining steps.
notes: a SIP-If-Match with two entity-tags gets 400

text: If no match is found, the ESC MUST reject the publication with a response of 412 (Conditional Request Failed), and skip the remaining steps.
notes: a SIP-If-Match naming no publication (or an expired one) gets 412

text: If the request has an Expires header field, that value MUST be taken as the requested expiration.
notes: Expires: 120 gives a 200 with Expires: 120

text: Else, a locally-configured default value MUST be taken as the requested expiration.
notes: no Expires gives the default_expires (3600)

text: This response MUST contain a Min-Expires header field that states the minimum expiration interval the ESC is willing to honor.
notes: Expires below min_expires gets 423 with Min-Expires

text: If the content type of the request does not match the event package, or is not understood by the ESC, the ESC MUST reject the request with an appropriate response, such as 415 (Unsupported Media Type), and skip the remainder of the steps.
notes: a presence PUBLISH with text/plain gets 415 with Accept

text: If the request has no message body and contained no entity-tag, the ESC SHOULD reject the request with an appropriate response, such as 400 (Invalid Request), and skip the remainder of the steps.
notes: a PUBLISH with neither body nor SIP-If-Match gets 400

text: If the chosen expiration interval has a special value of "0", the event state identified by the entity-tag MUST be immediately removed.
notes: a PUBLISH with Expires: 0 and SIP-If-Match removes the publication: the watchers get the state without it

text: The ESC MUST NOT store any event state as a result of such a request.
notes: after the remove, the entity-tag names nothing (a refresh gets 412)

text: If internal errors (such as the inability to access a back-end database) occur before processing is complete, the publication MUST NOT succeed, and the ESC MUST fail with an appropriate error response, such as 504 (Server Time-out), and skip the last step.
notes: holds by construction: the state lives in the ESC process; a call to it that fails gets 500 from the request worker and stores nothing

text: The response MUST contain an Expires header field indicating the expiration interval chosen by the ESC.
notes: every 200 to PUBLISH carries Expires

text: The response MUST also contain a SIP-ETag header field that contains a single entity-tag identifying the publication.
notes: every 200 to PUBLISH carries one SIP-ETag

text: The ESC MUST generate a new entity-tag for each successful publication, replacing any previous entity-tag associated with that event state.
notes: a refresh and a modify each get an entity-tag other than the one they named, and the old one then gets 412

text: The generated entity-tag MUST be unique from any other entity-tags currently assigned to event state associated with that Request-URI, and MUST be different from any entity-tag assigned previously to event state for that Request-URI.
notes: entity-tags are random 128-bit tokens: none repeats across the publications of a test

text: In the response to an OPTIONS request, the ESC SHOULD include "PUBLISH" to the list of allowed methods in the Allow header field.
notes: with the ESC registered, OPTIONS 200 lists PUBLISH in Allow

text: Also, it SHOULD list the supported event packages in an Allow-Events header field.
notes: OPTIONS 200 lists presence in Allow-Events

text: This response SHOULD contain a Retry- After header field indicating the time interval that the publication source is required to wait until sending another PUBLISH request.
notes: n/a: chappe pushes back with 503 only at the request-worker cap, the generic overload answer of RFC 3261

text: Any application of the PUBLISH mechanism for a given event package MUST define what content type or types are expected in PUBLISH requests.
notes: n/a: a duty of event package specifications

text: A PUA that uses PUBLISH to publish presence state to the PA MUST support the PIDF presence format.
notes: chappe_sip_pidf:render/1 builds the application/pidf+xml publish_state/4 sends

text: In presence publication, the EPA MUST keep the "id" attributes of tuples consistent in the context of an entity-tag.
notes: holds by construction: publish_state/4 sends the body you give it unchanged, on refresh, modify and the republish after a 412

text: If a publication modifies the contents of a tuple, that tuple MUST maintain its original "id".
notes: holds by construction: the tuple ids are the ones of your documents; chappe never rewrites them

text: The state agent SHOULD authenticate the EPA, and SHOULD apply its authorization policies (e.g., based on access control lists) to all requests.
notes: chappe_sip_esc authenticates with its auth option (digest) and authorizes every PUBLISH: by default an authenticated user may publish only its own AOR, an authorize hook sees the identity and the resource, and a PUBLISH without authentication is refused unless the app opts in with allow_unauthenticated

text: ESCs and EPAs MUST implement Digest for authenticating PUBLISH requests, as defined in RFC 3261 [4].
notes: the ESC's auth option challenges a PUBLISH with 401; publish_state/4 answers a 401 with its auth credentials

text: Also, the ESC SHOULD throttle incoming publications and the corresponding notifications resulting from the changes in event state.
notes: only the notifications are throttled (the presence notifier's min_interval); publications are bounded by the request-worker cap

text: If the subscriber is aware of both the protocol-independent pres URI and the SIP or SIPS URI for the same presentity, and both are valid (as discussed above) it SHOULD use the pres URI format.
notes: n/a: the app names the URI subscribe_to/3 subscribes to

text: When the subscriber is aware of both a pres and SIP URI for its own identity, it SHOULD use the pres URI in the From header field.
notes: n/a: the app names its From (the from option)

text: All subscribers and notifiers MUST support the "application/pidf+xml" presence data format described in [6].
notes: the presence notifier sends application/pidf+xml; the subscriber hands the parsed PIDF to its owner

text: If the header field is present, it MUST include "application/pidf+xml", and MAY include any other types capable of representing user presence.
notes: subscribe_to/3 for presence sends Accept: application/pidf+xml

text: A presence agent MUST authenticate all subscription requests.
notes: with auth set, a presence SUBSCRIBE without credentials gets 401 and is served once it answers it

text: A PA MUST NOT accept a subscription unless authorization has been provided by the presentity.
notes: the authorize fun is required; deny gives 403

text: For pending subscriptions, the state of the presentity SHOULD include some kind of textual note that indicates a pending status.
notes: a pending subscription gets a NOTIFY Subscription-State pending whose PIDF has a note

text: The contents of the presence document in such a NOTIFY are at the discretion of the implementor, but SHOULD be constructed in such a way as to not reveal to the subscriber that their request has actually been blocked.
notes: polite blocking: 200 and an active NOTIFY with one closed tuple

text: If the result of the authorization decision was success, a NOTIFY SHOULD be sent and SHOULD contain a presence document with the current state of the presentity.
notes: chappe_sip_presence:reauthorize/1 turns a pending watcher active: a NOTIFY active with the composed state

text: The body of the NOTIFY MUST be sent using one of the types listed in the Accept header field in the most recent SUBSCRIBE request, or using the type "application/pidf+xml" if no Accept header field was present.
notes: a SUBSCRIBE whose Accept leaves out application/pidf+xml gets 406; the NOTIFYs are application/pidf+xml

text: In other words, for a user pres:user@example.com, the signator of the NOTIFY SHOULD be the authority for example.com.
notes: chappe does not sign bodies (no S/MIME)

text: Therefore, if aggregation is needed, it MUST be done in a PA representing the presentity.
notes: the presence notifier composes the live publications of the presentity into one document, newest tuple of each id first

text: A PA SHOULD NOT generate notifications for a single presentity at a rate of more than once every five seconds.
notes: two changes in a row: the second NOTIFY waits min_interval (5000 ms by default) after the first

text: For this mechanism to be effective, all PUA SHOULD be capable of acting as a PA for the state that they manipulate, and that they authorize subscriptions that can be authenticated as coming from the domain of the presentity.
notes: n/a: a PUA product choice; chappe gives the PA side (chappe_sip_presence) and the PUA side (publish_state/4)

text: As a result, all watchers MUST support HTTP Digest.
notes: subscribe_to/3 answers a 401 to its SUBSCRIBE with the auth credentials

text: To support this, all PA MUST support TLS and SIPS as if they were a proxy (see Section 26.3.1 of RFC 3261).
notes: the presence notifier serves SUBSCRIBEs over the TLS listener like any request (see the TLS suite)

text: It MUST have the XML declaration and it SHOULD contain an encoding declaration in the XML declaration, e.g., "<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>".
notes: chappe_sip_pidf:render/1 starts with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

text: Every application conformant to this specification MUST accept the UTF-8 character encoding to ensure the minimal interoperability.
notes: parse/1 reads a UTF-8 note (non-ASCII) back unchanged

text: The <presence> element MUST have an 'entity' attribute.
notes: render/1 always writes entity; parse/1 refuses a document without one

text: The <presence> element MUST contain a namespace declaration ('xmlns') to indicate the namespace on which the presence document is based.
notes: render/1 declares xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf"; parse/1 takes a prefixed or a default namespace

text: The <tuple> element MUST contain an 'id' attribute which is used to distinguish this tuple from other tuples in the same PRESENTITY.
notes: render/1 writes each tuple's id; parse/1 drops a tuple without one

text: The value of an 'id' attribute MUST be unique within 'id' attribute values of other tuples for the same PRESENTITY.
notes: compose/2 keeps one tuple per id, and render/1 drops a repeated id

text: Tuples that contain a <basic> status element SHOULD contain a <contact> address.
notes: n/a: the tuples are the app's data; render/1 writes the contact you give

text: The value of the attribute MUST be a decimal number between 0 and 1 inclusive with at most 3 digits after the decimal point.
notes: render/1 writes a priority with at most 3 decimals and leaves out one outside 0..1

text: If the 'priority' attribute is omitted, applications MUST assign the contact address the lowest priority.
notes: parse/1 gives a contact without priority the priority 0.0

text: If the 'priority' value is out of the range, applications just SHOULD ignore the value and process it as if the attribute was not present.
notes: parse/1 reads priority="1.5" as 0.0

text: The value of this element MUST follow the IMPP datetime format [RFC3339].
notes: render/1 writes timestamps as RFC 3339 UTC

text: Timestamps that contain 'T' or 'Z' MUST use the capitalized forms.
notes: the rendered timestamp is 2026-10-03T12:00:00Z, capital T and Z

text: As a security measure, the <timestamp> element SHOULD be included in all tuples unless the exact time of the status change cannot be determined.
notes: render/1 stamps a tuple with the current time when it has none

text: A PRESENTITY MUST NOT generate successive <presence> elements containing the same timestamp.
notes: n/a: the presentity is the app; render/1 stamps a tuple without a timestamp with the current time in milliseconds

text: A URI used as a namespace identifier in PRESENCE INFORMATION data MUST be a full absolute-URI, per RFC 2396 [URI].
notes: render/1 uses urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:pidf only

text: Except as noted below, a processor of PRESENCE INFORMATION MUST ignore any XML element with an unrecognized name (i.e., having an unrecognized namespace URI, or an unrecognized local name within that namespace).
notes: parse/1 skips elements of other namespaces (rpid, a mustUnderstand extension) and reads the rest

text: Processors MUST handle these as described, even if they do not carry a mustUnderstand attribute.
notes: parse/1 reads tuple, status, basic, contact, note and timestamp

text: If a watcher receives presence information that is outdated, it SHOULD be ignored.
notes: n/a: the subscriber hands every document to its owner, which judges freshness from the timestamps parse/1 returns

text: All the processors conformant to this specification MUST be able to generate and accept UTF-8 encoding, this being one of the mandatory character encodings for XML conforming processors, and also required by the policies set out in RFC 2277 [RFC2277].
notes: a note with non-ASCII text renders as UTF-8 and parses back

text: If no "Accept" header is present in the SUBSCRIBE, the body type defined in this document MUST be assumed.
notes: a message-summary SUBSCRIBE without Accept gets application/simple-message-summary NOTIFYs

text: If the Request-URI or To header in a message-summary subscription corresponds to a group or collection of individual messaging accounts, the notifier MUST specify to which account the message- summary body corresponds.
notes: every NOTIFY of chappe_sip_mwi carries Message-Account

text: Note that the account URI MUST NOT be delimited with angle brackets ("<" and ">").
notes: Message-Account: sip:alice@example.com, no brackets

text: Notifiers MUST NOT generate a request with a larger value.
notes: render/1 caps a count at 4294967295

text: Subscribers MUST treat a larger value as 2^32-1.
Message headers MUST NOT be included in an initial NOTIFY, as new messages could be essentially unbounded in size.
notes: holds by construction: chappe_sip_mwi never writes message headers

text: Message headers included in subsequent notifications MUST only correspond to messages added since the previous notification for that subscription.
notes: n/a: chappe_sip_mwi sends no message headers

text: A messaging system which includes message headers in a NOTIFY MUST provide an administrator configurable mechanism to select which headers are sent.
notes: n/a: chappe_sip_mwi sends no message headers

text: However, the messaging notifier MUST NOT consider a message "old" merely because it generated a notification, as this could prevent another subscription from accurately receiving message-summary notifications.
notes: holds by construction: the counts are the app's (update/2); sending a NOTIFY changes none

text: If re-subscription fails, the Subscriber SHOULD periodically retry again until a subscription is successful, taking care to backoff to avoid network congestion.
notes: deactivated, probation and giveup re-subscribe (RFC 6665 rows); the retry-after sets the backoff

text: If a subscription has expired, new re- subscriptions MUST use a new Call-ID.
notes: a re-subscription after a terminated NOTIFY has a new Call-ID and From tag

text: The Subscriber MUST be prepared to receive and process a NOTIFY with new state immediately after sending a new SUBSCRIBE, a SUBSCRIBE renewal, an unsubscribe, a fetch, or at any other time during the subscription.
notes: a NOTIFY before the 200 to the SUBSCRIBE is taken (RFC 6665 4.1.2.4)

text: When a user de-registers from a device (logoff, power down of a mobile device, etc.), subscribers SHOULD unsubscribe by sending a SUBSCRIBE message with an Expires header of zero.
notes: n/a: the app knows when its user logs off; chappe_sip:unsubscribe/1 sends the Expires: 0

text: When a SIP Messaging System receives SUBSCRIBE messages with the message-summary event-type, it SHOULD authenticate the subscription request.
notes: with auth set, a message-summary SUBSCRIBE without credentials gets 401

text: Immediately after a subscription is accepted, the Notifier MUST send a NOTIFY with the current message summary information.
notes: the 200 to a message-summary SUBSCRIBE is followed by a NOTIFY with the counts of the summary fun

text: This initial synchronization NOTIFY MUST NOT include the optional RFC 2822 style message headers [8].
notes: holds by construction: chappe_sip_mwi never writes message headers

text: When the status of the messages changes sufficiently for a messaging account to change the number of new or old messages, the Notifier SHOULD send a NOTIFY message to all active subscribers of that account.
notes: chappe_sip_mwi:update/2 notifies every subscriber of the account

text: NOTIFY messages sent to subscribers of a group or alias, MUST contain the message account name in the notification body.
notes: every NOTIFY carries Message-Account

text: The Subscriber MUST be prepared to receive NOTIFYs from different Contacts corresponding to the same SUBSCRIBE.
notes: a forked message-summary NOTIFY is a subscription of its own (RFC 6665 4.1.4)

text: Notifiers SHOULD NOT generate NOTIFY requests more frequently than once per second.
notes: two updates in a row: the second NOTIFY to a subscriber waits a second after the first

text: At a minimum, subscriptions to this event package SHOULD be authenticated and properly authorized.
notes: the auth and authorize options of chappe_sip_mwi:serve/1: a SUBSCRIBE without credentials gets 401, a denied one 403

text: Furthermore, notifications SHOULD be encrypted and integrity protected using either end-to-end mechanisms, or the hop-by-hop protection afforded messages sent to SIPS URIs.
notes: chappe sends the NOTIFY over the subscription's transport (TLS when the dialog is sips); it does not encrypt bodies end to end (no S/MIME)

text: If the forwarded response was a final response, the proxy MUST generate a CANCEL request for all pending client transactions associated with this response context.
notes: B2BUA parallel fork shares the proxy selection: once a branch answers 2xx, every other ringing branch gets a CANCEL

text: As above, any given URI MUST NOT be added to the set more than once.
notes: follow_redirects: a 3xx Contact naming a target already in the target set is not tried again

text: If the proxy chooses to recurse on any contacts in a 3xx response by adding them to the target set, it MUST remove them from the response before adding the response to the response context.
notes: follow_redirects: the Contacts tried leave the 3xx; the 3xx that reaches the caller lists only the ones left

text: This technique consists of inserting before any existing Record-Route header, a Record-Route header with the URI reflecting to the input interface, including schemes and/or URI parameters, and secondly, a Record-Route header with the URI reflecting to the output interface.
notes: a request that arrives on one address or transport and leaves on another is record-routed twice: the inbound URI first, the outbound one on top

text: So, this means, in Section 16.4, "Route Information Preprocessing" [RFC3261], implementors can choose that a proxy MAY remove two Route headers instead of one when using the double Record-Routing.
notes: an in-dialog request carrying both of our Routes has both removed, so it does not spiral through us

text: Call-ID: All registrations from a UAC SHOULD use the same Call-ID header field value for registrations sent to a particular registrar.
notes: chappe_sip_regc: the challenged REGISTER, its answer and every refresh carry one Call-ID

text: A UA MUST increment the CSeq value by one for each REGISTER request with the same Call-ID.
notes: each REGISTER of a registration (credentials, refresh) has the previous CSeq plus one

text: UAs MUST NOT send a new registration (that is, containing new Contact header field values, as opposed to a retransmission) until they have received a final response from the registrar for the previous one or the previous REGISTER request has timed out.
notes: holds by construction: chappe_sip_regc is one gen_statem per registration that sends its next REGISTER only from the result of the previous one

text: UAs SHOULD support this mechanism so that bindings can be removed before their expiration interval has passed.
notes: unregister_client/1 (and a registration stopped by its supervisor) sends Expires: 0 for its Contact

text: A UA SHOULD use the same Call-ID for all registrations during a single boot cycle.
notes: refreshes and the unregister reuse the Call-ID of the first REGISTER

text: Registration refreshes SHOULD be sent to the same network address as the original registration, unless redirected.
notes: the refresh reaches the registrar peer that granted the binding

text: If the transaction layer returns a timeout error because the REGISTER yielded no response, the UAC SHOULD NOT immediately re-attempt a registration to the same registrar.
notes: a failed REGISTER is retried after a doubling backoff (and after Retry-After on 503), never at once

text: If a UA receives a 423 (Interval Too Brief) response, it MAY retry the registration after making the expiration interval of all contact addresses in the REGISTER request equal to or greater than the expiration interval within the Min-Expires header field of the 423 (Interval Too Brief) response.
notes: a 423 is retried with Expires set to its Min-Expires

text: Any party in a SIP session must be able to transfer any other party in that session at any point in that session.
notes: transfer => auto: a REFER from either leg of a relayed call is carried out by the B2BUA

text: The Transferor must know whether or not the transfer was successful.
notes: the referrer gets a final NOTIFY with the target's final status (200, or the failure) before any BYE

text: The Transferor and the Transferee must not be removed from a session as part of a transfer transaction.
notes: the referrer's leg is hung up only after a successful transfer and its final NOTIFY; the transferee's leg stays, with no re-INVITE

text: The Transferee must be able to replace an existing dialog with a new dialog.
notes: the target's new dialog replaces the referrer's leg behind rtpengine (replace_leg/4)

text: The signaling relationship between the Transferor and Transferee is not terminated, so the call is recoverable if the Transfer Target cannot be reached.
notes: a target that fails leaves the call as it was: the referrer gets the failure in its final NOTIFY and no BYE

text: Any REFER request MUST be appropriately authenticated and authorized using standard SIP mechanisms or else calls may be hijacked.
notes: every transfer goes through the call's policy; without one an off-net target (another host, tel:) is refused 403 before anything is called

text: Any REFER request MUST be appropriately authenticated and authorized using standard SIP mechanisms or else calls may be hijacked.
notes: the policy sees the REFER's From (its dialog's identity) apart from the Referred-By it claims; Referred-By alone grants nothing (RFC 3892 6)

text: Any REFER request MUST be appropriately authenticated and authorized using standard SIP mechanisms or else calls may be hijacked.
notes: a call carries at most max_transfers transfers (default 5), and one at a time (500 with Retry-After): a REFER loop is bounded

text: A user agent including the "multiple-refer" option-tag in a Supported header field indicates compliance with this specification.
notes: not supported: a B2BUA leg never lists multiple-refer, and a REFER with Require: multiple-refer gets 420 with Unsupported: multiple-refer

text: This implies that REFER-Recipients MUST NOT accept REFER requests for methods they do not understand.
notes: a REFER on a B2BUA call whose Refer-To method is not INVITE (BYE, ...) gets 403

text: The Transferor places the Transferee on hold, establishes a call with the Transfer Target to alert them to the impending transfer, places the target on hold, then proceeds with transfer using an escaped Replaces header field in the Refer-To header.
notes: a Replaces naming a leg of another B2BUA call of this node joins the transferee and the target through rtpengine: the target's leg is re-INVITEd, no new INVITE goes out, the transferee sees nothing

text: In case the triggered INVITE is routed to a different User Agent than the Transfer Target, the Require: replaces header field SHOULD be used in the triggered INVITE.
notes: a Replaces naming no dialog of this node goes to the target in an INVITE with Replaces and Require: replaces

text: An INVITE containing a Replaces header field SHOULD only be accepted if it has been properly authenticated and authorized using standard SIP mechanisms, and the requestor is authorized to perform dialog replacement.
notes: a REFER whose Replaces names a dialog of this node the referrer is not a party to (another user) gets 403; that call is untouched

text: The SRC MUST include the "+sip.src" feature tag in the Contact URI, defined in this specification as an extension to [RFC3840], for all RSs.
notes: chappe_sip_siprec: the RS INVITE Contact carries ;+sip.src (in-dialog requests repeat it)

text: An SRC MUST include the "siprec" option tag in the Require header when initiating an RS so that UAs that do not support the Session Recording Protocol extensions will simply reject the INVITE request with a 420 (Bad Extension) response.
notes: chappe_sip_siprec: the RS INVITE carries Require: siprec

text: For the CS, the SRC MUST provide recording indications to all participants in the CS.
notes: left to the app: chappe_sip_siprec sends no a=record and plays no tone; the app plays a prompt (chappe_mrf, rtpengine play) or relies on an agreement, as the RFC allows

text: The SRC sends recorded streams of participants to the SRS, and the SRC MUST provide a "label" attribute ("a=label"), as per [RFC4574], on each media stream in order to identify the recorded stream with the rest of the metadata.
notes: each m-line of the RS offer carries a=label, the label of its stream element in the metadata

text: Since the SRC does not expect to receive media from the SRS, the SRC typically sets each media stream of the SDP offer to only send media, by qualifying them with the "a=sendonly" attribute, according to the procedures in [RFC3264].
notes: each recorded stream is offered a=sendonly

text: In this case, the SRC sends a new SDP offer and sets the media stream to inactive (a=inactive) for each recorded stream to be paused, as per the procedures in [RFC3264].
notes: pause/1 re-INVITEs with every stream a=inactive, resume/1 with a=sendonly

text: For the purpose of base interoperability between SRC and SRS, an SRC MUST support separate m-lines in SDP, one per CS media direction.
notes: one m-line per party, so one per direction of the call

text: The SRC MUST send metadata to the SRS in an RS.
notes: the RS INVITE and each re-INVITE carry the metadata

text: When a SIP message contains both an SDP offer and metadata, the request body MUST have content type "multipart/mixed", with one subordinate body part containing the SDP offer and another containing the metadata.
notes: the body is multipart/mixed: application/sdp, then the metadata with Content-Disposition: recording-session

text: The SRC SHOULD include a full metadata snapshot in the initial INVITE request establishing the RS.
notes: the RS INVITE carries a complete snapshot

text: The SRC SHOULD send metadata as soon as it becomes available and whenever it changes.
notes: a party change (replace_b/3, update/1) re-INVITEs with the new metadata

text: If the SRC receives a snapshot request from the SRS, it MUST immediately send a full metadata snapshot.
notes: an UPDATE with a requestsnapshot body is answered 200, then a re-INVITE carries a complete snapshot

text: When the SRC receives a request for a metadata snapshot, it MUST immediately provide a full metadata snapshot in a separate INVITE or UPDATE transaction.
notes: the snapshot goes in its own re-INVITE, not in the UPDATE's response

text: The SRC and SRS MUST support SIP with Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2,
notes: the RS goes over the transport its URI names: a sips: SRS URI gives TLS

text: The 'recording' element MUST contain an xmlns namespace attribute with a value of urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:recording:1.
notes: chappe_sip_siprec_meta:build/1; parse/1 refuses another namespace

text: The algorithm MUST ensure that it does not use any potentially personally identifying information to generate the UUIDs.
notes: ids are random (version 4) UUIDs, base64 (chappe_sip_siprec_meta:new_id/0)

text: An SRC MAY, by policy, choose to limit the parts of the metadata sent to the SRS for recording.
notes: the metadata option drops names, AORs or the call_ref; participants names the parties as the app wants

text: Each instance of the following in [RFC7866]: | application/rs-metadata Is replaced with: | application/rs-metadata+xml
notes: the metadata goes as application/rs-metadata+xml; the older name is still read, and sent with legacy_content_type

text: REQ-011: The mechanism MUST support the ability to pause and resume the transmission and collection of RS media.
notes: pause/1 and resume/1

text: REQ-015: The mechanism MUST support a means to stop the recording.
notes: stop/1, the call ending, the owner exiting: BYE to the SRS

text: REQ-020: The mechanism MUST provide a way for metadata to be conveyed to the SRS incrementally during the CS.
notes: a re-INVITE with new metadata on a party change

text: When an SRS receives a new INVITE, the SRS MUST only consider the SIP session as an RS when both the "+sip.src" feature tag and the "siprec" option tag are included in the INVITE request.
notes: chappe_sip_siprec_srs:serve/3 takes an INVITE as an RS only with Contact ;+sip.src and Require: siprec, else {error, not_recording_session} with the request left to the app

text: The SRS MUST include the "+sip.srs" feature tag in the Contact URI, as per [RFC3840], for all RSs.
notes: the 200 of serve/3 carries Contact ;+sip.srs (create_uas contact_params)

text: Typically, the SRS only receives RTP streams from the SRC; therefore, the SDP offer/answer from the SRS normally sets each media stream to receive media, by setting them with the "a=recvonly" attribute, according to the procedures of [RFC3264].
notes: serve/3 answers each stream it takes a=recvonly with its label

text: The SDP answer from the SRS MUST include all m-lines, with any rejected m-lines indicated with a zero port, per [RFC3264].
notes: a stream serve/3 does not take (not G.711, past max_streams) keeps its m-line with port 0

text: For each "m=" line in the offer, there MUST be a corresponding "m=" line in the answer.
notes: run/1 answers a re-INVITE that adds a stream with one m-line per offered one: a receiver for the new stream, or port 0 past max_streams

text: If a stream is offered as sendonly, the corresponding stream MUST be marked as recvonly or inactive in the answer. If an offered media stream is listed as inactive, it MUST be marked as inactive in the answer.
notes: the SRS answers a sendonly stream recvonly and an inactive one inactive, in the INVITE and in each re-offer, at a new o= version when the answer changes

text: If the session description has changed, the UAS MUST adjust the session parameters accordingly and generate an answer in the 2xx response.
notes: run/1 answers an UPDATE with an SDP offer in its 200 (Content-Type application/sdp) through the re-INVITE path; an UPDATE with the metadata alone keeps an empty 200

text: The port number for a stream MAY be changed.
notes: a re-offer that moves a stream's source (port or address) re-latches its receiver: it learns again from the new address on any port, as at the start (a NAT may change the port), a late packet from the old source is dropped, the SRTP replay window and counters carry on

text: The transport for a stream MAY be changed.
notes: a re-offer that changes a stream's profile (RTP/AVP and RTP/SAVP) stops its receiver and takes the stream as a new one, under the profile and key rules an INVITE gets, the key rule judged on the transport of the request carrying the re-offer

text: The list of media formats used in the session MAY be changed.
notes: a re-offer that leaves a stream no PCMU or PCMA answers it port 0 and stops its receiver; one that keeps either keeps the stream, answered with the G.711 formats of the re-offer in its order

text: For the sake of data minimization, the SRS MUST NOT record additional metadata that is not explicitly required by local policy.
notes: the store gets the call_ref and the AORs of the senders of each stream, nothing else of the metadata; the rest goes to the app in the serve/3 result

text: REQ-012: The mechanism MUST include a means for providing the SRS with metadata describing CSs that are being recorded, including the media being used and the identifiers of parties involved.
notes: the metadata names the call, each stream and its label, and the AOR of each party, sender and receiver of each stream

text: Since the SRC can send partial updates based on the previous update, the SRS needs to keep track of the sequence of updates from the SRC.
notes: chappe_sip_siprec_srs:run/1 hands the metadata of each re-INVITE and UPDATE to the app, in order

text: Media encryption is an important element in the overall SIPREC solution; therefore, the SRC and the SRS MUST support RTP/SAVP [RFC3711] and RTP/SAVPF [RFC5124].
notes: serve/3 answers RTP/SAVP and RTP/SAVPF streams in their profile and decrypts them (chappe_audio_srtp); live: a real rtpengine's SRTP taps decrypt to both parties' audio

text: At a minimum, the SRC and SRS MUST support the SDP security descriptions key negotiation mechanism [RFC4568].
notes: the a=crypto line of each secure stream is read (chappe_sip_sdes) and answered with a line of the SRS

text: If the packet is judged to be replayed, then the packet MUST be discarded, and the event SHOULD be logged.
notes: a replayed SRTP packet never reaches the sink; counted in stats/1 and logged once per window

text: If the result is "AUTHENTICATION FAILURE" (see Section 4.2), the packet MUST be discarded from further processing and the event SHOULD be logged.
notes: a packet of another key, or with any bit flipped, is dropped before decryption, counted, logged once per window

text: After the packet has been processed and authenticated (when enabled for SRTP packets for the session), the receiver MUST use v to conditionally update its s_l and ROC variables as follows.
notes: the ROC and s_l move only after authentication; packets across the SEQ wrap, and late ones from before it, decrypt

text: After a re-keying occurs (changing to a new master key), the rollover counter always maintains its sequence of values, i.e., it MUST NOT be reset to zero.
notes: a re-INVITE with a new key rekeys the stream with its ROC, s_l and replay list kept

text: Packet indices which lag behind the packet index in the context by more than SRTP-WINDOW-SIZE can be assumed to have been received, where SRTP-WINDOW-SIZE is a receiver-side, implementation-dependent parameter and MUST be at least 64, but which MAY be set to a higher value.
notes: holds by construction: chappe_audio_srtp:new/1 takes a window of 64 to 1024 (default 128, or the offer's WSH)

text: Only packets with index ahead of the window, or, inside the window but not already received, SHALL be accepted.
notes: a packet out of order inside the window is taken once; a second copy, or one behind the window, is dropped

text: Message authentication for RTCP is REQUIRED, as it is the control protocol (e.g., it has a BYE packet) for RTP.
notes: SRTCP multiplexed on the stream's port is authenticated and its replay checked, then dropped

text: Regardless of the encryption or message authentication transform that is employed (it may be an SRTP pre-defined transform or newly introduced according to Section 6), interoperable SRTP implementations MUST use the SRTP key derivation to generate session keys.
notes: the session keys come from the AES-CM key derivation, checked against RFC 3711 B.3 (chappe_audio_srtp_tests) and decrypting rtpengine's SRTP

text: When the answerer receives the initial offer with one or more crypto attributes for a given unicast media stream, the answerer MUST either accept exactly one of the offered crypto attributes, or the offered stream MUST be rejected.
notes: the answer has one a=crypto line per secure stream, else the stream has port 0

text: If there are one or more crypto attributes in the offer, but none of them are valid or none of the valid ones are supported, the offered media stream MUST be rejected.
notes: F8, AES-256, several keys, a KDR, a key of the wrong length or an unknown parameter: port 0, and 488 when no stream is left

text: The tag and crypto-suite from the accepted crypto attribute in the offer (the same crypto-suite MUST be used in the send and receive direction).
notes: the answer echoes the tag and suite of the first line it can take

text: Compliant implementations obey the policies associated with a master key and MUST NOT accept incoming packets that violate the policy (e.g., after the master key lifetime has expired).
notes: past the key's lifetime, packets are dropped; the MKI of each packet must be the line's

text: If the length (after being decoded from base64) does not match that specified for the crypto-suite, the crypto attribute in question MUST be considered invalid.
notes: a key and salt other than 30 octets makes the line invalid; it is skipped

text: If an SDP crypto attribute is received with an unknown session parameter that is not prefixed with a "-" character, that crypto attribute MUST be considered invalid.
notes: an unknown session parameter makes the line invalid; one with a leading - is ignored

text: Media packets are authenticated: authentication MUST succeed; otherwise, the crypto context is not instantiated.
notes: an SSRC gets its context, and the stream latches to its source, only once a packet authenticates

text: When the answerer accepts an SRTP unicast media stream with a crypto line, the answerer MUST include one or more master keys appropriate for the selected crypto algorithm; the master key(s) included in the answer MUST be different from those in the offer.
notes: the answer's line carries a fresh random key, never the offer's

text: Furthermore, IT IS REQUIRED that encryption of the encapsulating payload be used whenever a master key parameter (inline) appears in the message.
notes: serve/3 rejects (port 0, then 488 with Warning 302) a secure stream offered over a transport that is not TLS or WSS, a sips: Request-URI reached over UDP or plain WS included, and takes it over TLS or WSS; each re-offer is judged on the transport of its own request (keys re-offered over UDP in a session set up over TLS are refused); unless the app passes keys_over_tls => false
